IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Typed and sourced requirement meaning

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Competing environment-property, intentional and necessary-feature definitions; no single original meaning.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: The relevant native distinctions are indicative domain statements, optative requirements and specifications (ERE-S-F004, manuscript §§3.1–3.2, pp.6–9), and beliefs, desires, intentions and attitudes in a revised requirements ontology (ERE-S-F008, introduction and §4, pp.7–8). 'Typed and sourced requirement meaning' is this packet's cross-source mechanism label, not either paper's original term.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: ERE-S-F004 asks how requirements, specifications and domain descriptions can be related without treating the machine alone as the subject of all requirements (§§3.1–3.2 and §5, pp.20–23). ERE-S-F008 asks whether the earlier requirements problem represents the kinds of concern stakeholders communicate, including preferences and quality concerns (§4, pp.7–8). The packet combines those questions; it does not attribute one common original problem statement to both papers.
GENEALOGY.INFLUENCE_OR_RELATION_CLASS: Documented source links distinguished from researcher comparisons in genealogy_edges.

records.title: Alternative-bounded necessity claims

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Alternative-bounded necessity claims

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: The necessary-feature critique exposes scope hidden by the word requirement.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: ERE-S-F007 uses design object, feature, goal, and a deliberately narrow definition of requirement as a feature necessary for a goal (§§1–2, especially §2's alternative-design argument). ERE-S-F008 uses the revised requirements problem with preferences (§4, pp.7–8). 'Alternative-bounded necessity' is an analyst label for a qualification, not a source-native school or theorem name.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: ERE-S-F007 challenges the inference that known successful designs establish necessary features: alternatives can lack common features, and unexamined alternatives prevent knowing that a feature is indispensable (§2; limitations in §3). ERE-S-F008 addresses the further problem of selecting acceptable specifications when stakeholder preferences and quality concerns matter (§4). The issue is the scope and warrant of a necessity claim, not a claim that all commitments are illusory.
GENEALOGY.INFLUENCE_OR_RELATION_CLASS: Documented source links distinguished from researcher comparisons in genealogy_edges.

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Four-variable functional documentation and environment-oriented RE developed related, differently partitioned boundary models.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: Requirements, specifications, domain properties, shared phenomena and indicative/optative descriptions are native terms in ERE-S-F004 (§§3.1–3.2 and §5). Monitored/controlled quantities and the descriptions linking them to program inputs/outputs occur in ERE-S-F003 (§§4.2–4.4). ERE-S-F005 supplies a reference model relating environment, machine and specification (§3, equations (1)–(3); §4.1, equations (4)–(8)). The packet's property label joins these related accounts without treating their notation as identical.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: The sources seek to show how specified computer behavior can justify a required change in the surrounding world when observations, actuators and domain knowledge intervene. Functional documentation must distinguish the quantities involved (ERE-S-F003, §§4.2–4.4), while a requirements argument needs a sound relation between domain knowledge, specification and required outcome (ERE-S-F004, §5; ERE-S-F005, §§3–5). The historical motivation is the missing semantic bridge, not the later objection that a model may encode the wrong world.
GENEALOGY.INFLUENCE_OR_RELATION_CLASS: Documented source links distinguished from researcher comparisons in genealogy_edges.

The assignment criterion asks whether an interface-compatible transition-system witness exists, whereas the actual responsibility relation has its own consistency rule (§3; lines 147–171 and 214–221).

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Observation- and control-compatible responsibility
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: Check(kind, ag, G, Mon, Ctrl, history_universe, Δ_witness?, Δ_actual?); kind is NECESSARY_INFORMATION_SCREEN, KAOS_2002_ASSIGNABILITY or ACTUAL_RESPONSIBILITY_CONSISTENCY.

VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.kind: One explicitly selected check; do not combine its verdict with the others without stating the conjunction.
VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.ag: Agent whose interface declares disjoint Mon(ag) and Ctrl(ag) sets of state variables.
VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.G: Goal interpreted over the common system-state history universe.
VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.State(V): Valuations of the variables V; model-structural, no numerical unit implied.
VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.Path(V): Sequences of valuations of V, with observed prefixes used for next-state decisions.
VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.Δ: Candidate transition system <Init,Next>: Init⊆State(Ctrl(ag)); Next⊆Path(Mon(ag)∪Ctrl(ag))×State(Ctrl(ag)), total on its source-model path domain.
VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.RUN_Δ(ag): Infinite system-state runs induced by the candidate Δ under the F012 conventions; distinct from RUN_Δactual(ag).
VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.HIST(G): All system-state histories permitted by G in that same universe.
VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.Δ_actual: The actual modeled implementation; not the variable existentially quantified in source assignability.
VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.observation_equivalence: A01 relation over admitted prefixes at the decision time, used in the separate researcher screen.
VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.action_capability: A02 available actions/next controlled valuations. For the screen, A_G(h,t) denotes actions compatible with the goal at prefix h and time t under the selected model.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: KAOS_2002_ASSIGNABILITY: ∃Δ compatible with the declared interface such that RUN_Δ(ag)=HIST(G). ACTUAL_RESPONSIBILITY_CONSISTENCY: Responsible(ag,G) implies ∀r∈RUN_Δactual(ag), r∈HIST(G); this does not quantify over a new actual implementation or require equality. NECESSARY_INFORMATION_SCREEN: ∀decision times t and admitted prefixes h1,h2, observation-equivalent prefixes must not require disjoint available action sets. Passing this pairwise necessary screen is not a complete synthesis or assignability proof.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: Separate possible witness transition system, actual transition system and goal histories under a declared common model; finite prefix examples illustrate distinctions but do not replace the infinite-run source semantics.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: The F012 agent model uses initial controlled states and a total next-state relation based on monitored/controlled histories, inducing infinite runs. Its existential witness is a capability claim under that model. Actual responsibility uses inclusion; C0008 retains its independently specified causal-strategy semantics and C0007 its operationalization semantics.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Faithful observation timing and control boundary; declare the selected check. Source assignability, actual responsibility consistency, general causal strategy and actual authority are distinct. See ERE-C0004-P01.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: An allocation or responsibility conclusion relies on an actor’s observation/control boundary; declare the check kind and model. ACTUAL_RESPONSIBILITY_CONSISTENCY applies only when Responsible(ag,G) is asserted; an unassigned goal does not receive a favorable consistency verdict.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Use the declared kind. (1) Researcher necessary screen: if h1 and h2 have the same observations at t but A_G(h1,t)∩A_G(h2,t)=∅, the proposed guaranteed allocation fails that screen. Its converse is not claimed. (2) F012 assignability: ∃Δ=<Init,Next> compatible with Mon/Ctrl and the source agent model, with RUN_Δ(ag)=HIST(G). (3) Actual responsibility consistency: Responsible(ag,G) ⇒ RUN_Δactual(ag)⊆HIST(G). For several assigned goals check actual inclusion for each; a proper subset for one goal is allowed. Do not test (2) by substituting Δ_actual for the existentially quantified Δ.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.NOTE: F012 supplies checks (2) and (3): §2 responsibility consistency; §3 Definition (Realizability) and its clarification about actual systems. Check (1), the kind-indexed presentation and finite example are researcher constructions. No source theorem proof is claimed to have been rerun.

ERE-S-F012: §2 agent model and responsibility consistency; local text lines 101–114 and 162–174
§3 clarification of stronger actual transition systems; lines 214–221

OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Declare check kind, goal version and common history universe.
Use A01/A02 to identify Mon/Ctrl and feasible candidate transitions; keep model evidence separate from operational capability/permission.
For assignability supply a compatible Δ witness or an adequate source-model argument; for actual consistency assess Δ_actual separately.
REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Versioned goal, Mon/Ctrl, state/history domains and decision timing.
Witness transition system and equality argument if source assignability is claimed; a bounded example alone is insufficient.
Actual transition model and inclusion argument if actual responsibility consistency is claimed.
Capability, authority and any environmental restrictions with separate provenance; explicitly flag any restriction that changes the source proposition.

EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.PASS: Only for the named check and sufficient evidence: a compatible equality witness establishes source assignability; actual-run inclusion establishes the stated actual consistency condition; an adequate screen establishes only that no represented indistinguishability obstruction was found. None substitutes for the others.
EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.FAIL: An exhibited indistinguishable-prefix/disjoint-action pair defeats the screen; a sound source-model impossibility argument defeats assignability; an actual run outside HIST(G) defeats responsibility consistency. Actual strict inclusion alone is not a failure.
EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.UNKNOWN: The claimed check lacks a justified model, witness/proof, actual-run description or load-bearing observation/control evidence. Passing only a finite screen leaves a stronger assignability claim unknown.
EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.INAPPLICABLE: No guaranteed allocation/control claim invokes this boundary, or the particular source model is not the chosen semantics; name the applicable cheaper check instead.
EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.PROCEDURE: Identify the check being claimed; establish an interface-compatible assignment witness where required, test actual-run inclusion separately, and verify operational capability and authority. Use ERE-C0008 for a separately specified causal-strategy claim.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Decidability depends on the selected formal fragment. A bounded finite relation illustrates the existential/actual distinction but is not the complete infinite-trace source test. The necessary screen is incomplete; model correspondence and authority remain outside its decision procedure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Researcher finite illustration with Mon={m}, Ctrl={y}, G1: m→next y. The witness relation W={(0,0),(0,1),(1,1)} equals the permitted one-step relation; an actual relation A={(0,1),(1,1)} is a proper subset satisfying G1 and an additional always-y goal. The example discriminates the checks; it is not a full source proof replication.

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Goal-directed acquisition and formal refinement patterns; broader GORE also uses qualitative contributions.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: Native terms include goal refinement, AND/OR refinement structures and refinement patterns. The early KAOS acquisition account uses goals and operationalization in its own metamodel (ERE-S-F009, §§2.6–2.7, manuscript pp.12–15); the later pattern account states completeness, consistency and minimality conditions for refinements (ERE-S-F032, §3.1). GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: The sources address how to acquire and progressively elaborate high-level objectives into lower-level requirements, and how to justify or construct refinement links rather than merely draw a goal tree (ERE-S-F009, §§2.6–2.7; ERE-S-F032, §3.1 and the persistence example in §§3.1.2–3.1.3). Child-removal minimality concerns the refinement argument; it is distinct from the later operationalization condition in ERE-C0007.

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Domain-feasible obstacle analysis with explicit residual risk

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Obstacle reasoning developed from earlier exception/scenario work into formal goal obstruction and resolution.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: ERE-S-F011 uses obstacle, obstruction, domain consistency and obstacle resolution (§3 definitions; §5 strategies). The focused successors use probabilistic goals/obstacles and required versus estimated satisfaction, followed by knowledge uncertainty in risk assessment (ERE-S-R019, §3.1 Definitions 1 and 3–6, PDF pp.5–6; ERE-S-R020, §III.A–B, pp.108–109). 'Explicit residual risk' is the packet's qualified synthesis, not a claim that the original Boolean obstacle definition already supplied calibrated probabilities.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: Initial goals and environmental assumptions can be too ideal, leaving plausible exceptional conditions unaddressed. ERE-S-F011 seeks to identify domain-feasible obstructions and resolve them while requirements-level options remain open (§1; §3; §5; application limits in §7). The probabilistic successors address assessing and prioritizing satisfaction shortfalls and handling uncertainty in their estimates (ERE-S-R019, §§3–4; ERE-S-R020, §I and §§III,V). These are historical problem extensions within the same property, not evidence of complete obstacle coverage or independent calibration.
GENEALOGY.INFLUENCE_OR_RELATION_CLASS: Documented source links distinguished from researcher comparisons in genealogy_edges.

EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.INAPPLICABLE: Guard false with the cheap-path/nontrigger reason documented.
EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.PROCEDURE: Seek an independently documented incident or realistic adversarial scenario missing from the model.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Depends on the stated model. Finite enumerations and selected fragments may be decidable; qualitative judgment and actual-world correspondence are not made decidable by this record. Bounded checks retain their bound.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: A plausible delayed input is linked to a missed deadline and a recovery option with remaining limitations.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: All difficult conditions are declared impossible without environmental evidence.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Unresolved values in either attribute, contradictory interpretations, or absent evidence for a load-bearing assumption.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: An irrelevant outage outside the agreed service scope is documented as outside the current analysis.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: The domain model can omit the very obstacle that matters, and retrospective stories can exaggerate prevention.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Restricting the admitted context, choosing an unrepresentative witness or treating documentation presence as semantic adequacy can game this check. Evaluate the named mechanism.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Change to either attribute, interpretation, source commitment or environment reopens the verdict.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Obstacle search can grow without bound; focus by consequence, known incidents and uncertainty Low-consequence reversible work may use a brief exception review
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Quantitative risk claims require probability/consequence evidence beyond a Boolean obstacle tree.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Model-conditional probabilistic satisfaction threshold: the estimated nonvacuous goal satisfaction rate in a declared obstacle model meets its required minimum.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: P02(G,M,q), where G is a behavioral goal, M is a versioned finite behavior/probability model with an explicit triggering condition C and temporal consequent H_G, and q is its prescribed satisfaction threshold.

VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.G: Behavioral goal C implies H_G in declared finite-trace temporal semantics.
VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.M: (Omega,D,mu,C,H_G,obstacle/refinement assertions,parameter provenance). Omega is a finite behavior-episode space; mu is a normalized probability measure. The source's unweighted finite count is the equal-weight case.
VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.theta: Optional uncertain probability parameters with an explicit joint epistemic law Pi; Pi is not the operational measure mu.
VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.SV: q-p_M, a signed probability-point gap, not a cost or harm measure.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: One named goal, version, trigger, environment regime and finite horizon. Compare the probability over all episodes in the declared conditional model; no universal statement over other deployments or future environments. If multiple parameter models are retained, report each result or conservative bounds, rather than silently select a favorable model.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A probability-bearing finite behavior model plus a separately supplied normative threshold.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: H_G retains the goal's deadline/temporal interpretation. Episodes with C false do not count as successes. A finite run cannot establish an unbounded eventuality without a separate model. PASS means true in the specified probability model, not an observed guarantee over all real executions.
ASSUMPTIONS: The trigger, denominator, horizon and event interpretation are fixed and aligned through propagation.
The joint measure or factorization is explicitly supplied; statistical independence is not inferred solely from graph shape or distinct names.
A represented failure event is equivalent to the modeled violation event, or a residual term/bound records missing coverage. A modeled residual of zero is an assumption requiring justification.
Shared obstacle/domain-hypothesis variables retain identity. Distinct variables may still be statistically correlated.
Point estimates and epistemic distributions retain provenance; numerical error, estimation error and structural omission are kept separate.
The q value comes from an identified requirement/decision source.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A decision genuinely depends on a partial probabilistic satisfaction target, and a meaningful behavior population plus probability model can be specified. If the goal is only qualitative or the model cannot support probabilities, retain P01 and report P02 as inapplicable or unknown.

EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE.CORE: P02(G,M,q) iff p_M = mu(C intersect H_G)/mu(C) >= q, with mu(C)>0; SV=q-p_M.
EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE.OBSTACLE_RECONSTRUCTION: Let V_G be the union of the jointly evaluated modeled obstruction combinations, including needed domain hypotheses. Only if V_G equals the violation event within C may p_M be replaced by 1-mu(V_G|C). Otherwise carry the unmatched failure event/residual bound. Use a joint contingency table, an equivalent probabilistic model, or a correctly weighted Boolean representation; product simplification requires its factorization premises.
EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE.UNCERTAINTY: For a declared epistemic law Pi over theta, VU(G)=Pi[p_theta(G)<q]. This is uncertainty about meeting the rate threshold, not the operational failure rate. A separate rule such as VU<=alpha is an additional normative decision requiring authorization; it is not silently added to the source's EPS>=RDS rule.
EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE.BOUNDS: For a justified model envelope L<=p_M<=U, PASS only if L>=q; FAIL only if U<q; otherwise UNKNOWN. State whether the envelope is deterministic, epistemic or statistical, and do not mislabel one as another.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.SOURCE_DEFINED: R019 §3.1 Definitions 1,3–6: nonvacuous finite-count satisfaction, EPS/RDS comparison and signed SV. R020 §III.B: VU as below-RDS probability mass.
SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.RESEARCHER_PROPOSED: Explicit measure and denominator alignment, joint-dependence guard, residual term, conservative bounds verdicts, evidence partition and examples. These narrow the permissible transfer; they are not attributed as exact historical KAOS rules.

OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Map each recorded episode to C and H_G with a specified observation/censoring rule.
Bind obstacle events to the same eligible population or give an explicit conditional transformation.
Record measurement/elicitation source, counts, selection effects, calibration method if actually performed, and unresolved estimates.
Compare the resulting model calculation with q; report model validity and external predictive support separately.
REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Versioned goal and operationalization of C/H_G.
A03 probability/joint-dependence model and provenance, including unknown/residual cases.
A04 prescribed threshold and its scope/authority.
An explicit calculation or evaluator result with assumptions and numerical precision.
Any empirical calibration or statistical guarantee claimed must have its own data and method; the cited papers alone cannot supply it for a target system.

EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.PASS: The applicable fixed model, or all models in an explicitly justified envelope, yields p>=q. Label PASS_MODEL and preserve assumed/estimated inputs.
EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.FAIL: The applicable fixed model yields p<q, or a justified envelope lies wholly below q. Label FAIL_MODEL; this is distinct from a directly observed violation.
EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.UNKNOWN: Missing/contradictory population, joint law, coverage, threshold, or unresolved uncertainty crosses q; report available conditional computations without claiming empirical assurance.
EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.INAPPLICABLE: No quantitative satisfaction threshold is a decision input, or the selected finite probabilistic semantics is inappropriate; name the cheaper path.
EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.PROCEDURE: Verify scope and threshold; construct the relevant joint violation event; evaluate p and SV; inspect dependencies/omissions; propagate uncertainty only under an explicit joint uncertainty model; issue a bounded verdict.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite explicitly enumerated rational models permit exact arithmetic. Finding a faithful goal/domain model is not thereby decidable or guaranteed complete. BDDs may reduce computation but do not create missing probabilities. Monte Carlo gives an approximation whose numerical error and sampling design must be reported independently of elicitation/model error; no numerical error bound was manufactured for this supplement.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: ERE-CASE-RISK001: a fully specified synthetic 10,000-episode population gives p=0.9702 and q=0.95, so PASS_MODEL with SV=-0.0202.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: ERE-CASE-RISK002: correlated redundant-channel failures produce p=0.92 at q=0.98, while unjustified multiplication reports 0.99. ERE-CASE-RISK003 separately exposes a vacuous denominator.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Only marginal probabilities supplied where joint probabilities matter; unobserved/censored outcome; nonpositive trigger count; uncertain parameters straddle q; unresolved model coverage or normative threshold.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: ERE-CASE-RISK005: low-consequence reversible work with no probabilistic commitment, where a concrete exception/fallback review answers the decision.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: Omitted failures, underweighted rare regimes, wrong conditioning, hidden correlation and optimistic expert estimates can produce false passes. Unrepresentative stress data, double-counted shared failures and overly pessimistic unsupported intervals can produce false failures.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Counting nontriggering cases as successes; shrinking the admitted population; assigning zero to undiscovered obstacles; assuming independence for convenience; weakening q and calling it performance improvement; using mean EPS to conceal substantial below-threshold epistemic mass.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Changes to goal meaning, q, environment, eligibility, horizon, obstacle coverage, shared variables, probability estimates or countermeasures invalidate the affected calculation until rebound to the new version.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Use quantitative propagation when decisions depend on threshold or obstacle-priority differences. For a small model, an explicit joint contingency table or sensitivity bounds may suffice. Otherwise a brief feasible-exception review with fallback ownership preserves P01 without spurious numeric assurance.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: A model-conditional threshold proposition and uncertainty-aware decision aid. It does not establish actual-world probability calibration, completeness of requirements, global safety, regulatory acceptance, or causal field improvement. Source case studies and an author retrospective are not independent replication.

VARIANTS.EXACT_VERSION_VARIANT: Cailliau/van Lamsweerde 2013 probabilistic goal/obstacle assessment, with the separately identified 2015 knowledge-uncertainty extension. The 2025 retrospective supplies genealogy/currentness context only.
VARIANTS.SEMANTIC_ASSUMPTIONS: Finite behavioral-goal satisfaction is nonvacuous and tied to a declared population. RDS is prescriptive; EPS is computed/estimated. Partial obstruction can have conditional probability strictly between zero and one. This transfer profile demands an explicit joint measure and aligned denominators; it does not silently endorse all syntactic independence shortcuts in the 2013 presentation.
VARIANTS.REFINEMENT: Keep qualitative entailment/refinement checks separately from 2013 probabilistic conditions: nonzero conditional support is weaker than deterministic entailment. Use the general joint-event calculation; product rules require factorization assumptions. Obstacle domain-completeness is relative to D and must not stand for exhaustiveness of real-world failure discovery.
VARIANTS.RESPONSIBILITY: Retain the existing qualitative allocation/authority checks. A probability annotation does not confer actor control, observation, authority or commitment.
VARIANTS.OBSTACLES: Preserve P01 for domain-feasible deterministic obstruction. In the probabilistic variant, a candidate may only increase/support a chance of violation. Bind occurrence and consequence probabilities separately. For P02, evaluate the combined violation event and any residual coverage.
VARIANTS.OPERATIONALIZATION: Maintain the versioned mapping from trigger and temporal outcome to observable episodes. Do not substitute an unconditional event frequency for a goal-conditioned satisfaction rate.

RESEARCHER_CHECKS: Model result versus external validation separation

VARIANTS.UNCERTAINTY_EXTENSION: R020 adds a distribution over uncertain satisfaction probabilities, below-threshold uncertainty and elicitation/calibration procedures. BDDs preserve logical sharing; Monte Carlo propagates stipulated input uncertainty. Neither supplies omitted common-cause dependencies, representative data or an external calibration guarantee automatically.
VARIANTS.EVIDENCE_LIMITS: R019's COOL estimates include personal experience; R020's case uses expert elicitation with confidential data presented through fictitious realistic values. Retain method/case evidence only. No general calibrated prediction or causal field-effect claim is established.
VARIANTS.CHEAPER_PATH: A feasible-exception narrative, fallback and small joint table/bounds can preserve the relevant mechanism without a complete KAOS model.

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: KAOS operationalization maps goal semantics to requirements on operations, using pruning semantics and frame axioms.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: The source uses goal operationalization, operation specifications, domain pre/postconditions, required pre/post/trigger conditions and frame axioms (ERE-S-F013, §3, especially §3.2 Definitions 1–3; §4 patterns). 'Progress-preserving operationalization' is this packet's label. Its minimality is the source's non-overrestriction condition, not refinement child-removal minimality.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: ERE-S-F013 observes that formal analysis methods often presuppose an operational specification and offers constructive support for deriving one from system goals (abstract and §1). The problem is how to build correct service specifications incrementally, including the conditions that permit, require and constrain operations (§3 Definitions 1–3), rather than only analyze an already supplied specification. ERE-S-F012 supplies the related agent framework (§2), not a replacement operationalization definition.
GENEALOGY.INFLUENCE_OR_RELATION_CLASS: Documented source links distinguished from researcher comparisons in genealogy_edges.

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Causal realizability separate from satisfiability

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Reactive-system theory, independently developed around late-1980s synthesis and specification work; later goal analysis imports control distinctions.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: ERE-S-F016 distinguishes realizability and weak realizability in a reactive behavior/game model, using environment choices and winning strategies (§2.1; §2.5 Theorems 3–5). ERE-S-F012 separately uses goal realizability by an agent (§3). 'Causal realizability separate from satisfiability' is the packet's normalized distinction; the two source models retain their different quantifiers.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: The reactive-systems source asks which specifications can be implemented despite an environment's choices, rather than merely admitting a behavior, and when related realizability characterizations coincide (ERE-S-F016, §§2.1 and 2.5). The agent-assignment source asks the different interface-compatible witness question (ERE-S-F012, §3). The packet retains these as related but nonidentical ways to expose a specification that cannot be achieved under the declared interaction model.
GENEALOGY.INFLUENCE_OR_RELATION_CLASS: Documented source links distinguished from researcher comparisons in genealogy_edges.

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Temporal model-checking vacuity develops into synthesis witness selection and finer specification review.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: Vacuity and interesting witnesses occur in the accessible abstract of ERE-S-F018; that abstract-only access supports historical terminology, not an appraisal of its full algorithm. ERE-S-F033 uses vacuity in synthesis, strengthening and witness-based distinctions (introduction and strengthening/witness definitions). 'Discriminating witness checks' also draws on positive and near-miss suites in ERE-S-F037 (§4.1). There is no single source-native term for the packet's combined mechanism.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: The motivating failure is a successful formal check or synthesized behavior that does not exercise a meaningful part of the specification. The inspected synthesis treatment examines how witnesses and strengthening distinguish such outcomes (ERE-S-F033, introduction and definitions). Later specification-review suites address intended and near-miss behaviors (ERE-S-F037, §4.1; §6.7 threats). The combined property does not claim that non-vacuity alone recovers stakeholder intent, and it does not infer an unread proof from ERE-S-F018's abstract.
GENEALOGY.INFLUENCE_OR_RELATION_CLASS: Documented source links distinguished from researcher comparisons in genealogy_edges.

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Design-by-contract inheritance rules and formal behavioral subtyping address clients relying on an established interface.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: Preconditions, postconditions, class invariants and inheritance-related contract rules appear in ERE-S-F021 (assertions, put-child example and inheritance discussion, pp.42 and 47–48). Behavioral subtyping and history constraints are native terms in ERE-S-F022 (Fig.4 and §5.2, pp.1822–1823). The packet combines these sources under a behavioral-substitution property while preserving their distinct contributions.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: The motivating problem is safe reuse and substitution: a replacement should preserve the behavioral expectations on which clients depend, including state evolution, not merely supply matching method names. ERE-S-F021 presents contract obligations for calls and redefinition; ERE-S-F022 extends the subtype relation to invariants and histories (Fig.4; §5.2). The original problem is behavioral compatibility, not the later criticism of proof cost.
GENEALOGY.INFLUENCE_OR_RELATION_CLASS: Documented source links distinguished from researcher comparisons in genealogy_edges.

GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: There is no source-native universal proposition or single historical origin for this rejected candidate. ERE-S-F007 deliberately defines a requirement narrowly as a necessary feature for a goal and uses design alternatives to challenge unwarranted necessity claims (§§1–3). ERE-S-F008 distinguishes a broader requirements problem involving stakeholder concerns and preferences (§4). The packet's universal sentence is an explicit analyst test of a stronger inference.

The packet turns that critique into a bounded negative: evidence about one chosen solution does not establish that every project has known solution-independent necessary features. This does not attribute that universal overclaim to a named historical author or deny authorized commitments.

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Historical criticism-derived universal lifecycle claim; early sources already document feedback and discovery.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: There is no single source-native term or demonstrated advocate for the blanket proposition that all requirements must be settled before any construction. The relevant native accounts discuss iterative design and user involvement (ERE-S-F027, §3.3 p.32 and §4.2.2 pp.40–41), staged development with explicit feedback provisions (ERE-S-F002, opening and Steps 3 and 5), an ideal rational design process (ERE-S-F025, §§I–III), and risk-driven spiral development (ERE-S-F026, opening pp.61–63).
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: This analyst negative tests an oversimplified historical/process claim. The inspected early accounts address difficulty understanding needs, learning from design and organizing dependable development despite iteration (ERE-S-F027, cited conference sections; ERE-S-F002, Steps 3 and 5; ERE-S-F025, §§I–III). ERE-S-F026 motivates risk-sensitive process choices. None is cited as an advocate of the universal no-construction-before-total-closure rule.
GENEALOGY.INFLUENCE_OR_RELATION_CLASS: Documented source links distinguished from researcher comparisons in genealogy_edges.

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Functional-document content and rational design accounts distinguish meaning from document format.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: There is no single source-native origin for 'decision-relevant semantic documentation.' It is a synthesis of functional documents for computer systems (ERE-S-F003, §§1–2 and 4.2–4.4), a rational design process and its documentary representation (ERE-S-F025, §§I–III), and qualified requirements-practice claims (ERE-S-F028, pp.1–2). The source terms remain separate from this modern mechanism label.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: ERE-S-F003 addresses descriptions that communicate and relate the functions and quantities needed to understand a computer-based system. ERE-S-F025 distinguishes the messy path of discovery from a rational account useful for communicating and maintaining the resulting design (§§I–III). The packet draws a consumer/decision/maintenance mechanism from those motivations and uses ERE-S-F028's opening argument to bound universal success claims; it does not invent a historically named doctrine of proportional documentation.
GENEALOGY.INFLUENCE_OR_RELATION_CLASS: Documented source links distinguished from researcher comparisons in genealogy_edges.

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Control-aware unavoidable conflict classification

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: 2025 unavoidable boundary-condition extension to earlier goal-conflict analysis.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: Boundary condition and unavoidable boundary condition (UBC) are the native terms; the latter uses a control/realizability distinction (ERE-S-F023, introduction and Definition 1, with minepump/extractor examples). 'Control-aware unavoidable conflict classification' is the packet's normalized property name.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: See exact source/version profiles; the candidate label is a researcher normalization, not an invented historical quotation.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: ERE-S-F023 challenges boundary-condition generation that produces conditions an appropriately controlled system could avoid, motivating a stronger, decision-relevant classification (introduction; Definition 1; benchmark discussion). The paper's question is whether a conflict condition can be avoided under its interaction model, not whether avoidance is costless, authorized or preferred in an application.
GENEALOGY.INFLUENCE_OR_RELATION_CLASS: Documented source links distinguished from researcher comparisons in genealogy_edges.

A sufficiency challenge tests an asserted implication or universal process benefit; ordinary operational assessment evaluates the bounded source-informed rule. Mechanical record checks do not settle semantic, empirical or authority judgments.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Universal only over explicitly enumerated material items needed for the declared decision and search scope. No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: An elicitation episode and its resulting candidate claims
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Assessed at the named evidence/configuration snapshot. Hypothesized, desired, agreed and observed states remain distinct. Later changes require the stated invalidation procedure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Sources can be accessed lawfully and their statements can be situated; observers recognize that observation can change conduct.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A material claim depends on tacit practice, disputed vocabulary, exceptions, inaccessible actors or conflicting accounts.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: For every material candidate in the declared episode, record origin class and source/context; resolve or explicitly carry each decision-relevant contradiction; require a separate authority witness for promotion to obligation. PASS denotes this bounded inquiry discipline, not discovery of every possible need.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.LIMIT: Not a verbatim source theorem, source standard requirement or empirically validated universal acceptance algorithm

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Interview/observation notes, document versions, hypothesis-to-question map and disposition of discrepancies.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Identify source role, collection method/date, context, direct versus interpreted content and unresolved disagreement.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: An informed evaluator checks applicability, identifies the exact claim and scope, reviews the named witnesses, tests the supplied counterexample class and records a reasoned four-valued outcome. Mechanical schema checks can establish presence/identity, not domain truth or authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite record checks are mechanically decidable. Semantic correspondence, legitimate representation, proxy validity and causal transfer generally require contextual judgment and may remain UNKNOWN. No claim of general decidability.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.TEXT: Observed night-shift workaround contradicts a manager interview; a shift observation and nurse discussion reveal a needed offline queue, retained as candidate pending acceptance.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.TEXT: A workshop statement becomes a mandatory requirement although field observations contradict it and neither source nor interpretation is retained.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: One authorized owner confirms a low-impact display-label correction against the current glossary.

FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_POSITIVE: Number of interviews or workshops is not the mechanism; a discriminating observation or short answer may be enough.
FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_NEGATIVE: Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. Number of interviews or workshops is not the mechanism; a discriminating observation or short answer may be enough.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: New operating shift, affected population or changed practice invalidates the relevant coverage claim even when requirement wording is unchanged.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Field access, transcription, interpretation and participant effort; richer observation justified by a decision it may change. Alternative: A reversible wording correction with one known owner and an unambiguous current policy may need only one recorded answer.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Historical methodological rationale and examples; no source here establishes a universally best technique or a necessary number of methods. The operational rule is a proposed audit discriminator, not a measured process-effect claim.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE: Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.RULE: For every material candidate in the declared episode, record origin class and source/context; resolve or explicitly carry each decision-relevant contradiction; require a separate authority witness for promotion to obligation. PASS denotes this bounded inquiry discipline, not discovery of every possible need.

OUTCOMES.PASS: Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation
OUTCOMES.FAIL: An applicable observed contradiction, failed criterion or valid counterexample defeats the specified claim
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Relevant evidence/meaning/authority is missing, disputed or not discriminating
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: An explicit guard excludes the claim; cheap path must be justified

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.EMPTY_SCOPE_RULE: Empty obligation/source sets never establish completeness by vacuity; show scope adequacy or label inapplicable/unknown.

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.LIMITS: Origin means inspected antecedent, not an assertion of absolute first invention

FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.SUPPORT: Named language definitions and explicit counterexamples where applicable; no general effectiveness theorem

EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.ASSESSMENT: Curto compares multi-LLM candidate-generation configurations and iteration rounds against reference SRS alignment and bounded human ratings. The observed precision/recall trade-offs bear on generated elicitation candidates, not a comparison of this property’s complete contextual inquiry and corroboration mechanism.
EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.LIMITS: Four reference SRSs, a fresh classroom case, one run per configuration/round, possible contamination and a prototype-assistant confound limit transfer. Historical rationale and the water-resource workshop belong to other evidence roles.

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.ASSESSMENT: No replication or external validation of the combined context-matched, discrepancy-preserving elicitation rule was identified in this record’s inspected evidence. The method-selection arguments, original inquiry exercise, domain workshop and candidate-generation study address different components or tasks.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.LIMITS: This is limited to the evidence enumerated in the resolvable supporting-link record. It is not a literature-wide absence claim, and original examples or adjacent automation results are not counted as replications of ERE-C0101-P01.

INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.SUPPORT: Qualitative practitioner cases or source-document rewrite; distinctions in source records apply
INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.LIMITS: Reported practices and perceptions are not randomized process benefits or universal prevalence

NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.SUPPORT: Triangulation can multiply correlated opinions; an intrusive field study can cost more than it reveals.
NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.LIMITS: A paper’s open problem is not an observed failure; the constructed cases are not incident reports

STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.SUPPORT: No external standard mandate asserted in this research sublane
STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.LIMITS: Language conventions and an author’s chosen criterion do not grant normative authority; cited ISO editions not independently adopted

PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Interview/observation notes, document versions, hypothesis-to-question map and disposition of discrepancies.
PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: A tool’s existence/performance on selected examples does not establish organizational success

TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.SUPPORT: Observed night-shift workaround contradicts a manager interview; a shift observation and nurse discussion reveal a needed offline queue, retained as candidate pending acceptance.
TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.LIMITS: Constructed examples expose distinctions; they are not evidence of implementation effectiveness in a target repository

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Unseen practices, inaccessible people and researcher interpretation remain; no numerical saturation guarantee.
CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: Contrary findings narrow claims; they do not justify symmetric overgeneralization

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.SUPPORT: Sources can be accessed lawfully and their statements can be situated; observers recognize that observation can change conduct.
ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.LIMITS: New operating shift, affected population or changed practice invalidates the relevant coverage claim even when requirement wording is unchanged.

DOMAIN_VALIDITY.ASSESSMENT: Goguen and Linde examine situated and tacit knowledge; ACRE relates elicitation techniques to information and access conditions. The water-management workshop supplies one domain-specific example of connecting tasks, information needs and a mock-up. These support contextual inquiry, not a validated correspondence test for every elicited claim.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.LIMITS: ACRE field effectiveness remained untested; one facilitated workshop did not validate actual operating efficiency. Corroboration and classification of observations, preferences and obligations remain the researcher-proposed discipline.

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.ASSESSMENT: Sharp supplies a role-and-interaction search method; contextual elicitation and the workshop expose the importance of whose activity and perspective were observed. This supports examining the declared source population and missing voices.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.LIMITS: Sharp explicitly leaves validation and stopping unresolved. Neither the role search nor the workshop establishes exhaustive coverage, a saturation threshold or representative participation.

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.ASSESSMENT: The inspected elicitation sources distinguish information sources and roles but do not demonstrate that an observed practice, preference or generated statement acquires binding authority. The separate authority witness in this record is an analytical safeguard.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.LIMITS: No applicable mandate or obligation-authorization outcome was examined for this research mechanism; documenting an account does not establish its normative force.

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.ASSESSMENT: Inquiry-based analysis connects questions, answers, reasons and requirement changes. It offers a process for revising interpretations, but the inspected material does not prove that this record’s complete observation-to-candidate-to-obligation chain preserves meaning.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: pp. 22–24, 29–31; inquiry cycle and level-of-effort discussion

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.LIMITS: The meeting-scheduler exercise is illustrative. The four-valued operational rule is a reconstruction, not a source theorem or verified transformation.

REALIZABILITY.ASSESSMENT: The facilitated water-resource workshop demonstrates that a task/data/display inquiry can be conducted and used to discuss information needs. ACRE explicitly considers practical prerequisites and interdependencies among techniques.
REALIZABILITY.LIMITS: This is feasibility of an elicitation activity. It neither establishes realizability of resulting requirements nor guarantees access, effort or success in another setting.

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.ASSESSMENT: The inquiry cycle records questions, answers, reasons and changes, providing a source-informed rationale for retaining interpretations and discrepancies. This supplies a trace structure relevant to elicitation provenance.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: pp. 22–24, 29–31; inquiry cycle and level-of-effort discussion

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.LIMITS: The inspected study did not evaluate downstream rationale use or measure semantic accuracy of provenance links. This record’s source/context checks have no measured error rate.

ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.ASSESSMENT: The inspected inquiry and contextual-workshop material concerns discovery and elaboration. It does not evaluate whether a receiving authority accepted the same obligation, scope and residual uncertainty represented by this record’s proposed gate.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: pp. 22–24, 29–31; inquiry cycle and level-of-effort discussion

ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: The requirement for a separate authorization witness is proposed here; neither source validates the complete acceptance rule.

EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.ASSESSMENT: The workshop and inquiry exercise show contextual elaboration in bounded cases. Curto compares multi-LLM candidate-generation configurations and finds reference-alignment trade-offs; it supplies adjacent automation evidence, not a comparison of this complete contextual/corroborative elicitation method.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: pp. 22–24, 29–31; inquiry cycle and level-of-effort discussion

EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.LIMITS: No causal estimate for the integrated mechanism is established by this evidence. Curto uses four reference SRSs, a classroom case and one run per configuration/round; the workshop lacks actual-use validation.

DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.ASSESSMENT: ACRE provides information-, context- and access-sensitive guidance for selecting acquisition methods. Inquiry-based analysis allows effort-sensitive shortcuts. These support asking which inquiry could change a decision.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: pp. 22–24, 29–31; inquiry cycle and level-of-effort discussion

DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.LIMITS: The inspected guidance does not validate an optimal selection rule, a minimum method count, or expected cost/benefit for the proposed predicate. Missing and correlated sources remain decision risks.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Historical methodological rationale and examples; no source here establishes a universally best technique or a necessary number of methods. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.TRANSFERABILITY_LIMITS: Declared operation, population, time and decision; observed work is evidence about work, not automatically permission to preserve it. Unseen practices, inaccessible people and researcher interpretation remain; no numerical saturation guarantee.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: Compare alternative elicitation paths on missed consequential requirements and total cost in the target context.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: The reviewers inspected the complete claim/disposition population and selected detailed semantics/source bodies. Absence of an individual finding does not establish independent validation of every field, source or proposed predicate.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: For a consequential requirement decision, distinguish who is affected, who supplied evidence, who represents whom, and who can bind which organization; preserve dissent and reopening conditions.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: A requirements decision with a declared affected population

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Treat taxonomy as discovery heuristic and record uncertainty/challenge rights; do not turn the resulting network into a legitimacy score. WinWin-descended preference analysis can structure options and sensitivity, but it does not guarantee agreement or settle rightful representation.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Decisions can be challenged on representation and authority rather than hidden in a priority weight.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ALTERNATIVE_MECHANISMS: For a single-owner private task, record that owner’s request and scope; use facilitated negotiation for unresolved cross-party conflicts.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: For a consequential requirement decision, distinguish who is affected, who supplied evidence, who represents whom, and who can bind which organization; preserve dissent and reopening conditions.

EVALUATION_MODE.DEFINITION: Mode describes how evidence is assessed, separate from the commissioned predicate-role enum. A sufficiency challenge tests an asserted implication or universal process benefit; ordinary operational assessment evaluates the bounded source-informed rule. Mechanical record checks do not settle semantic, empirical or authority judgments.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: Assess(subject: A requirements decision with a declared affected population, context, consumerDecision, evidenceSnapshot, validTime) -> PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|INAPPLICABLE

VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.CONSTRAINT: No single priority scalar substitutes for dimensions
Issuer, subject, scope, validity and revocation status

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Universal only over explicitly enumerated material items needed for the declared decision and search scope. No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A requirements decision with a declared affected population
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Assessed at the named evidence/configuration snapshot. Hypothesized, desired, agreed and observed states remain distinct. Later changes require the stated invalidation procedure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Affect and decision remit can be examined; any legitimate authority source is available and current.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: More than one affected role, absent constituency, surrogate, conflict, delegated decision or binding external commitment.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: For each material decision and each affected class identified by the declared search, either name a direct participant or document a proxy/exclusion with limits; require a current authority witness for each claimed commitment; preserve unresolved dissent and an explicit disposition. A bounded PASS cannot certify that all possible people were discovered.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.LIMIT: Not a verbatim source theorem, source standard requirement or empirically validated universal acceptance algorithm

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Role inventory, recruitment/search record, mandate/delegation, disagreement record and decision rationale.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Source of role and remit; represented population; proxy selection; exclusions; dissent; actual decision record.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: An informed evaluator checks applicability, identifies the exact claim and scope, reviews the named witnesses, tests the supplied counterexample class and records a reasoned four-valued outcome. Mechanical schema checks can establish presence/identity, not domain truth or authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite record checks are mechanically decidable. Semantic correspondence, legitimate representation, proxy validity and causal transfer generally require contextual judgment and may remain UNKNOWN. No claim of general decidability.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.TEXT: Scheduling policy records manager budget authority, nurses’ workflow expertise and a patient advocate’s limited remit; unresolved accessibility concern blocks only the affected release decision.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.TEXT: The sponsor and vendor agree unanimously while excluded night staff and patients bear consequences; the record labels consensus complete and binding on them.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: An individual reorganizes their own private notes without imposing a duty on another party.

FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_POSITIVE: Signatures, full meeting attendance or high stakeholder weights cannot substitute for representation and scope.
FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_NEGATIVE: Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. Signatures, full meeting attendance or high stakeholder weights cannot substitute for representation and scope.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Changed representative, contractual remit, affected population or decision scope requires reevaluation.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Recruitment, access, negotiation and continuing role-currentness; exhaustive social graphs can swamp the team. Alternative: A sole owner requests a reversible local change and no material external effect is identified after a scoped check.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Conceptual methods and current political-model proposals support the problem framing; Sharp explicitly reports no validation, and PEN only retrospective reinterpretations. The operational rule is a proposed audit discriminator, not a measured process-effect claim.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE: Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.RULE: For each material decision and each affected class identified by the declared search, either name a direct participant or document a proxy/exclusion with limits; require a current authority witness for each claimed commitment; preserve unresolved dissent and an explicit disposition. A bounded PASS cannot certify that all possible people were discovered.

OUTCOMES.PASS: Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation
OUTCOMES.FAIL: An applicable observed contradiction, failed criterion or valid counterexample defeats the specified claim
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Relevant evidence/meaning/authority is missing, disputed or not discriminating
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: An explicit guard excludes the claim; cheap path must be justified

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.EMPTY_SCOPE_RULE: Empty obligation/source sets never establish completeness by vacuity; show scope adequacy or label inapplicable/unknown.

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.SUPPORT: Sharp et al. 1999 role-network identification; Alexander 2005 taxonomy and surrogacy
HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.LIMITS: Origin means inspected antecedent, not an assertion of absolute first invention

FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.SUPPORT: Named language definitions and explicit counterexamples where applicable; no general effectiveness theorem
FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.LIMITS: The four-valued rule is an operational reconstruction; authority and world correspondence are not logically supplied by syntax

EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.ASSESSMENT: No comparative outcome study of the combined stakeholder coverage/representation/expertise/authority discipline is established by the inspected source set. Taxonomies, an unvalidated role-search method, retrospective political reinterpretations, descriptive traceability findings and a worked negotiation example are the actual evidence types.
EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.LIMITS: This is scoped to the linked inspected evidence. It does not convert author proposals, retrospective examples or methodological plausibility into measured legitimacy, fairness or delivery effects.

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.ASSESSMENT: The inspected stakeholder taxonomies, role-search proposal, retrospective political model and worked negotiation example do not constitute a replication or external validation of the combined coverage/representation/expertise/authority rule.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.LIMITS: Sharp’s stated unvalidated status and PEN’s future practitioner work bound those particular sources. They do not establish that no later stakeholder or negotiation validation exists; none is inferred from unavailable evidence.

INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.SUPPORT: Qualitative practitioner cases or source-document rewrite; distinctions in source records apply
INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.LIMITS: Reported practices and perceptions are not randomized process benefits or universal prevalence

NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.SUPPORT: No taxonomy can guarantee inclusion; power can distort consent; documenting a proxy does not make representation legitimate.
NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.LIMITS: A paper’s open problem is not an observed failure; the constructed cases are not incident reports

STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.SUPPORT: No external standard mandate asserted in this research sublane
STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.LIMITS: Language conventions and an author’s chosen criterion do not grant normative authority; cited ISO editions not independently adopted

PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Role inventory, recruitment/search record, mandate/delegation, disagreement record and decision rationale.
PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: A tool’s existence/performance on selected examples does not establish organizational success

TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.SUPPORT: Scheduling policy records manager budget authority, nurses’ workflow expertise and a patient advocate’s limited remit; unresolved accessibility concern blocks only the affected release decision.
TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.LIMITS: Constructed examples expose distinctions; they are not evidence of implementation effectiveness in a target repository

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Legitimate competing interests may have no technical resolution; supplied mandate can itself be disputed.
CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: Contrary findings narrow claims; they do not justify symmetric overgeneralization

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.SUPPORT: Affect and decision remit can be examined; any legitimate authority source is available and current.
ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.LIMITS: Changed representative, contractual remit, affected population or decision scope requires reevaluation.

DOMAIN_VALIDITY.ASSESSMENT: Sharp and Alexander distinguish affected roles, direct participation and surrogate representation. PEN represents political relationships through reinterpretations of published project accounts. These ground the concern that participation, influence, expertise and authority are different attributes.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: Introduction; Stakeholder Roles; Applying the Taxonomy in Practice
Abstract; §7.1–7.2; chapter 5 case descriptions only identified

DOMAIN_VALIDITY.LIMITS: Sharp’s method was unvalidated; PEN’s cases are retrospective reinterpretations, not original incident investigations or prospective validation of this combined discipline.

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.ASSESSMENT: The role taxonomy and supplier/client/satellite search identify ways to challenge an initial participant list and to expose inaccessible roles or proxies. The inspected sources support inquiry about missing constituencies.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: Introduction; Stakeholder Roles; Applying the Taxonomy in Practice

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.LIMITS: No empirical completeness or legitimacy rate is established. Role slots and graph expansion cannot show that every affected group is represented, and stopping remains a stated problem.

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.ASSESSMENT: The taxonomy distinguishes surrogates, regulators and decision-makers; PEN exposes political relations; MPARN organizes win conditions, issues, options and agreements. These are relevant to separating evidence, power and agreement from binding remit.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: Introduction; Stakeholder Roles; Applying the Taxonomy in Practice
Abstract; §7.1–7.2; chapter 5 case descriptions only identified

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.LIMITS: None supplies an applicable mandate for a real decision or proves that its aggregation legitimizes representation. The requirement for a witnessed remit is the synthesis’s explicit authority condition.

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.ASSESSMENT: This property separates social and evidential roles in a decision; it specifies no formal refinement calculus or executable transformation whose semantic preservation could be proved. Its operational rule asks for representation and remit evidence.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.LIMITS: This status concerns formal refinement correctness only. It does not excuse inaccurate role attribution or unsupported promotion of a preference into an obligation.

REALIZABILITY.ASSESSMENT: The stakeholder procedures describe operational searches; MPARN supplies a worked negotiation example and PEN a representational proposal. They show how role and political information can be organized.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: Abstract; §7.1–7.2; chapter 5 case descriptions only identified

REALIZABILITY.LIMITS: Successful practitioner use of PEN was future work, and the examples do not establish achievable agreement, availability of representatives, or implementability of agreed requirements.

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.ASSESSMENT: Gotel and Finkelstein identify source participation, access, provider/consumer conflicts and stale documentation. These are relevant to retaining who supplied a requirement and what role information a later consumer can recover.
TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.LIMITS: That descriptive study does not measure the correctness or currentness of this property’s representation/delegation links. A populated role record remains an assertion requiring its own evidence.

ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.ASSESSMENT: MPARN distinguishes issues, options and agreements and explicitly declines to guarantee agreement. This supports recording an actual disposition rather than treating a preference score as an acceptance event.
ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: Its worked example is not validation that an acceptance represents every affected party or comes from a competent authority. The combined representation-and-remit gate is untested.

EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.ASSESSMENT: The inspected base consists of stakeholder taxonomies/proposals, a political-model retrospective reinterpretation, descriptive traceability findings and a worked negotiation example. It does not compare outcomes with and without this combined role/authority discipline.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: Introduction; Stakeholder Roles; Applying the Taxonomy in Practice
Abstract; §7.1–7.2; chapter 5 case descriptions only identified

EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.LIMITS: This is a bound on the inspected evidence, not a claim that later validation is absent from the literature. Representation fairness, reduced political failure and improved delivery are not measured here.

DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.ASSESSMENT: MPARN’s preference analysis makes candidate options and subjective inputs visible, and its discussion retains disagreement and the possibility of no agreement. PEN adds a way to represent political context.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: Abstract; §7.1–7.2; chapter 5 case descriptions only identified

DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.LIMITS: Neither establishes unbiased weights, legitimate social aggregation, guaranteed consensus or valid decision rights. The property retains these as separate evidential questions.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Conceptual methods and current political-model proposals support the problem framing; Sharp explicitly reports no validation, and PEN only retrospective reinterpretations. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.TRANSFERABILITY_LIMITS: Coverage is relative to explicit system/lifecycle/context boundaries; power and graph centrality are descriptive, not automatic normative weights. Legitimate competing interests may have no technical resolution; supplied mandate can itself be disputed.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.UNVERIFIED_OR_OPEN_QUESTIONS: A prospective field evaluation should measure changed decisions and omissions, with independent checks of excluded interests.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: A prospective field evaluation should measure changed decisions and omissions, with independent checks of excluded interests.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: The reviewers inspected the complete claim/disposition population and selected detailed semantics/source bodies. Absence of an individual finding does not establish independent validation of every field, source or proposed predicate.

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.ASSESSMENT: Actor boundaries and dependency roles make modeled parties explicit, and Yu calls for cross-checking modeled content against different actors’ perceptions. These support an attribution question for each represented intention.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §§8.1–8.3, especially pp. 110–113; SD and SR model definitions

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.LIMITS: No coverage guarantee follows from a complete-looking graph. The teaching-task generation study does not test whether all real affected groups were identified or accurately represented.

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.ASSESSMENT: The iStar 2.0 guide is a primary authority for that language version’s legal elements and relations. Yu expressly identifies authority and trust as relationships whose treatment is unresolved, supporting the separation of notation from organizational mandate.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §§8.1–8.3, especially pp. 110–113; SD and SR model definitions

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.LIMITS: Language authorship does not grant actors consent or power to bind others. This is notation authority, not an external process standard or an assessed mandate.

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.ASSESSMENT: Tropos connects early/late requirements to design and implementation, but its inspected conclusion treats formal transformations as further work. The iStar guide defines local refinements and integrity rules; no general preservation proof from intentional model to running software was established here.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.LIMITS: The detailed JACK mapping was not fully audited. Generation/smell results are not translation proofs, and the complete version/attribution/mapping predicate remains an operational reconstruction.

REALIZABILITY.ASSESSMENT: Tropos supplies an illustrative development path, and the LLM study constructs candidate iStar models, checks syntax and assesses seeded modeling issues on teaching problems. These demonstrate bounded tooling and modeling activities.
REALIZABILITY.LIMITS: They do not establish the actual capability of modeled actors, organizational delivery or general industrial scalability. The code mapping was not independently verified.

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.ASSESSMENT: The generation study includes mapping between problem words and model elements, which is relevant to trace construction. Its inspected evaluation does not establish semantic accuracy of the complete source-attribution-to-transformation chain required by this property.
