STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.ASSESSMENT: The claim under challenge is a universal inference from one dependency edge, not a method claiming to enumerate or represent a stakeholder population. An applicable counterexample does not require representative sampling of all stakeholders.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.LIMITS: This does not assert that the graph covers every affected party. Population coverage and legitimacy of represented actors remain separate, unassessed claims.

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.ASSESSMENT: Yu explicitly leaves authority/trust relationships open; the guide’s dependency tuple defines a representation. Those definitions do not supply an actual mandate or agreement, so an edge alone cannot establish the normative consequent in the stated sufficiency claim.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §§8.1–8.3, especially pp. 110–113; SD and SR model definitions

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.LIMITS: This is a bounded inference about the inspected notation semantics, not legal advice or an assessment of an actual contract. Extra constitutive rules would change the premise set.

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.ASSESSMENT: The asserted map from EdgeWellFormed to consent, authority, capability and delivery has a same-representation/different-external-facts countermodel. The record therefore rejects this mapping as a sufficient refinement or correspondence warrant.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §§8.1–8.3, especially pp. 110–113; SD and SR model definitions

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.LIMITS: It does not disprove a separately specified and justified transformation with additional witnesses. The exact countermodel and four-valued predicate are researcher constructions, not quoted source theorems.

REALIZABILITY.ASSESSMENT: The constructed supplier-refusal/no-stock case holds the well-formed dependency fixed while changing capability and performance. This suffices to show that represented reliance alone does not establish the realizability or fulfillment asserted by the candidate claim.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §§8.1–8.3, especially pp. 110–113; SD and SR model definitions

REALIZABILITY.LIMITS: No real supplier’s capability is assessed. A hypothetical modeled dependency can remain useful without actual-delivery evidence when no stronger claim is made.

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.ASSESSMENT: The dependency relation has a source-defined meaning; it is not automatically a consent, authorization or fulfillment trace. The traceability investigation supplies adjacent rationale for retaining sources and relation context rather than treating any recorded link as sufficient.
TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.LIMITS: No empirical trace precision/recall is claimed. The counterexample rejects a relation-type substitution, not all dependency graphs or typed links.

ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.ASSESSMENT: A dependency edge can remain identical before agreement, after refusal and after non-delivery. It therefore does not by itself witness either receiving-party acceptance or the external outcome consumed by an acceptance criterion.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §§8.1–8.3, especially pp. 110–113; SD and SR model definitions

ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: The evidence establishes the insufficiency of the stated premise, not the effectiveness of every proposed separate-witness procedure or any actual acceptance decision.

EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.ASSESSMENT: The retained result is rejection of an edge-only universal implication by an analytical counterexample. It asserts no average treatment effect and is not supported by an observed failure-rate or process comparison.
EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.LIMITS: Empirical evaluation would be needed for claims that the replacement witness discipline improves delivery or review efficiency. Those claims are not established here.

DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.ASSESSMENT: The inspected notation semantics plus the constructed counterexample show why an approval rule using only edge existence can yield a false external conclusion. Separate witnesses change the information available to the decision.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §§8.1–8.3, especially pp. 110–113; SD and SR model definitions

DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.LIMITS: This refutes the specified sufficiency claim; it does not establish an optimal review cost, universal deployment procedure or validated effectiveness of the replacement rule.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.EVIDENCE_CEILING: The supplied semantics do not entail those external assertions; a concrete same-graph/different-world counterexample defeats universal sufficiency. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.TRANSFERABILITY_LIMITS: Counterexample is analytical, not an empirical incident; a contractual rule could add authority, but that is extra evidence. Even a current agreement may be breached; capability is conditional and delivery requires observation.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.UNVERIFIED_OR_OPEN_QUESTIONS: Only an explicit additional semantics/witness linking an edge to a binding and observed world state could narrow this rejection.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: Only an explicit additional semantics/witness linking an edge to a binding and observed world state could narrow this rejection.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: The reviewers inspected the complete claim/disposition population and selected detailed semantics/source bodies. Absence of an individual finding does not establish independent validation of every field, source or proposed predicate.

INTAKE.CROSSWALK_ELIGIBILITY_WITH_REASON: NOT_A_GENERAL_ADOPTION_CANDIDATE: rejected/ceremonial sufficiency claim; use as an overclaim discriminator
TARGET_NEUTRAL_AUDIT_QUESTIONS: What independent witness supports each external claim attributed to this edge?
Does a simpler existing mechanism already answer the same consumer question?
Which assumption, scope or authority change would require re-entry?
PROHIBITED_OVERCLAIMS: A diagram author can commit other parties or certify delivery.
No finding about any target repository or semantic owner is supplied.

SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.INPUT: Keep the graph and each claimed external witness separate to expose the missing implication.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.OUTPUT: Candidate sufficiency claim: a well-formed dependency link alone establishes that the dependee agreed, is authorized, can perform and delivered.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.CONSUMER: Any consumer treating the graph as authorization, feasibility or acceptance evidence.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.BOUNDARY: Counterexample is analytical, not an empirical incident; a contractual rule could add authority, but that is extra evidence.

INTENTIONAL_SOCIAL_MODEL_PROFILE.APPLICATION: Target-neutral schema applied to the property; worked cases are explicitly analytical
INTENTIONAL_SOCIAL_MODEL_PROFILE.NOTATION_VERSION: Yu i*1995, Tropos2004 and iStar2.0v3 2016 are separate versions; see VERSION_PROFILES
INTENTIONAL_SOCIAL_MODEL_PROFILE.ELEMENT_AND_RELATION_MEANINGS: Goal/task/resource/quality meanings and actor/dependency/refinement/contribution rules are taken from the selected version
INTENTIONAL_SOCIAL_MODEL_PROFILE.REASONING_RULES: For the proposed implication EdgeWellFormed ⇒ Consent∧Authority∧Capability∧Delivered, a case with EdgeWellFormed and a false consequent is FAIL. Confirming all consequent facts gives only bounded case PASS, never universal sufficiency. Missing external witnesses yields UNKNOWN; an edge used solely as hypothetical analysis is INAPPLICABLE.
INTENTIONAL_SOCIAL_MODEL_PROFILE.ACTOR_ASSUMPTIONS: Sufficiency would require a validated mapping from graph truth to world/authority truth; no such mapping follows from notation alone.
INTENTIONAL_SOCIAL_MODEL_PROFILE.DOWNSTREAM_TRANSLATION: The rejected inference replaces distinct evidential questions with the existence of an edge.
INTENTIONAL_SOCIAL_MODEL_PROFILE.VALIDATION: External confirmation, remit, capacity evidence and actual outcome record, each with date/configuration.
INTENTIONAL_SOCIAL_MODEL_PROFILE.UNRESOLVED_LIMITATIONS: Even a current agreement may be breached; capability is conditional and delivery requires observation.

VERSION_PROFILES.ELEMENTS: Strategic Dependency and Strategic Rationale; goals, tasks, resources and softgoals; open/committed/critical dependence strength
VERSION_PROFILES.RULE_LIMIT: Original conceptual reasoning; examples illustrative. Authority/trust and model validation explicitly unresolved. No later iStar 2.0 quality semantics imported.

VERSION_PROFILES.ELEMENTS: Actors include agents, roles and positions; hard goals/softgoals, plans, resources and dependencies; early/late requirements, architecture, detailed design and implementation
VERSION_PROFILES.RULE_LIMIT: Refinement/mapping methodology is not automatic proof of preserved world purpose; detailed transformations and lifecycle extension remained open.

VERSION_PROFILES.ELEMENTS: Actor/agent/role; goals, tasks, resources, qualities; five-part dependency; AND/OR refinement; Make/Help/Hurt/Break; precise or vague quality
VERSION_PROFILES.RULE_LIMIT: Partial dependency internals allowed; identical labels do not identify objects; weak contributions are not numeric probabilities. Integrity rules govern this representation, not observed delivery.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Operationalize a quality with its affected population, stimulus/environment, response, observation and criterion authority; retain uncertainty, excluded dimensions and anti-gaming conditions.

EVALUATION_MODE.DEFINITION: Mode describes how evidence is assessed, separate from the commissioned predicate-role enum. A sufficiency challenge tests an asserted implication or universal process benefit; ordinary operational assessment evaluates the bounded source-informed rule. Mechanical record checks do not settle semantic, empirical or authority judgments.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: Assess(subject: A quality criterion and the phenomenon it is intended to represent, context, consumerDecision, evidenceSnapshot, validTime) -> PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|INAPPLICABLE

VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.CONSTRAINT: Units and statistic fixed before evaluation
Distinguish stipulated target from empirical boundary

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Universal only over explicitly enumerated material items needed for the declared decision and search scope. No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A quality criterion and the phenomenon it is intended to represent
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Assessed at the named evidence/configuration snapshot. Hypothesized, desired, agreed and observed states remain distinct. Later changes require the stated invalidation procedure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: The measurement population and environment are observable; proxy validity and target choice are treated as separate claims.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A vague or conflicting quality concern influences design or acceptance.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: For a declared quality decision, PASS requires a criterion whose population, environment, unit/statistic and threshold remit are explicit and whose proxy correspondence has a stated warrant; a known material excluded dimension yields FAIL for the broad claim, while insufficient proxy evidence yields UNKNOWN. Meeting a numeric threshold is evaluated separately from criterion validity.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.LIMIT: Not a verbatim source theorem, source standard requirement or empirically validated universal acceptance algorithm

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Instrumentation plus denominator records, stakeholder task observations, threshold decision and counter-metrics.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Concern owner, source of threshold, measurement method, excluded cases, units, instrument and calibration/uncertainty.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: An informed evaluator checks applicability, identifies the exact claim and scope, reviews the named witnesses, tests the supplied counterexample class and records a reasoned four-valued outcome. Mechanical schema checks can establish presence/identity, not domain truth or authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite record checks are mechanically decidable. Semantic correspondence, legitimate representation, proxy validity and causal transfer generally require contextual judgment and may remain UNKNOWN. No claim of general decidability.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.TEXT: Booking response uses all valid requests at declared load, includes timeouts as failures, and records a stakeholder-selected 95th-percentile target plus error/abandonment constraints.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.TEXT: The system drops slow requests; latency of completed requests improves while users receive fewer successful results. The old metric alone wrongly certifies quality.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: A private export either contains the agreed fields or does not; a direct content check suffices.

FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_POSITIVE: A dashboard with precise units and green thresholds can still measure the wrong population.
FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_NEGATIVE: Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. A dashboard with precise units and green thresholds can still measure the wrong population.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Population, sampling, timeout policy, instrument or intended concern changes invalidate prior comparability.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Instrumentation, representative sampling and checking distribution/denominator changes; precision can cost more than the decision warrants. Alternative: A directly observable binary event with agreed scope may require a simple criterion, not a multi-attribute scorecard.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Primary scenario method and taxonomy plus bounded BDD performance case; no general empirical threshold or universal proxy validity demonstrated. The operational rule is a proposed audit discriminator, not a measured process-effect claim.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE: Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.RULE: For a declared quality decision, PASS requires a criterion whose population, environment, unit/statistic and threshold remit are explicit and whose proxy correspondence has a stated warrant; a known material excluded dimension yields FAIL for the broad claim, while insufficient proxy evidence yields UNKNOWN. Meeting a numeric threshold is evaluated separately from criterion validity.

OUTCOMES.PASS: Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation
OUTCOMES.FAIL: An applicable observed contradiction, failed criterion or valid counterexample defeats the specified claim
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Relevant evidence/meaning/authority is missing, disputed or not discriminating
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: An explicit guard excludes the claim; cheap path must be justified

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.EMPTY_SCOPE_RULE: Empty obligation/source sets never establish completeness by vacuity; show scope adequacy or label inapplicable/unknown.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.POSITIVE_WITNESS_OR_WORKED_EXAMPLE: Booking response uses all valid requests at declared load, includes timeouts as failures, and records a stakeholder-selected 95th-percentile target plus error/abandonment constraints.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.NEGATIVE_WITNESS_OR_COUNTEREXAMPLE: The system drops slow requests; latency of completed requests improves while users receive fewer successful results. The old metric alone wrongly certifies quality.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.NON_TRIGGER_EXAMPLE: A private export either contains the agreed fields or does not; a direct content check suffices.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.OBSERVABILITY_AND_MISSINGNESS: Instrumentation plus denominator records, stakeholder task observations, threshold decision and counter-metrics. Missing evidence remains UNKNOWN unless an explicit contradicted claim is being tested.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.CURRENTNESS_AND_INVALIDATION: Population, sampling, timeout policy, instrument or intended concern changes invalidate prior comparability.

CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Quantification can erase material qualitative aspects and introduce incentives to optimize the proxy.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.KNOWN_FAILURES_AND_MISUSES: The system drops slow requests; latency of completed requests improves while users receive fewer successful results. The old metric alone wrongly certifies quality.

CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.WHAT_CHANGED_AND_WHAT_DID_NOT: Refines vague concerns into bounded criteria while rejecting precision as a substitute for meaning.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESIDUAL_LIMITS: Some qualities remain disputed and indirectly observable; operational precision does not eliminate value judgments.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.CEREMONY_VERSUS_MECHANISM: A dashboard with precise units and green thresholds can still measure the wrong population.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RETENTION_RATIONALE: Retain the bounded mechanism with explicit guard, evidence and cheap path. Use a scenario-bound measure and keep qualitative concerns and adverse effects explicit; avoid forced weighted sums.

SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_SUPPORTED: Gherkin examples combined with Locust/Grafana/Jaeger and agreed thresholds can drive instrumented performance checks
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Single instrumented performance case; feasibility of scenario-to-measure execution, not a controlled effectiveness or universal-quality result.
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: Single Brazilian vendor/team case; one brief team-lead interview; no counterfactual/control and weak threat treatment; broad guarantee language exceeds design

SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_SUPPORTED: Consumer/task-relative quality effects; passive voice and ambiguous pronouns have different effects on domain modeling
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Adjacent new conceptual replication about wording factors in domain modeling; supports task-relative assessment, not replication of QAW or the full operationalization rule.
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: 25 participants/four single-sentence tasks; limited interaction power; context self-reports unvalidated; not a universal lint-weight derivation

CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_CHALLENGED: Measurability or a green aggregate score establishes the intended quality or legitimacy of a threshold.
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.QUALIFICATION: Conceptual taxonomy proposal, not consensus norm or empirical effect; some measures are proxy/subjective
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Conceptual separation of quality concern, representation and satisfaction; not a threshold-effect experiment.

CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_CHALLENGED: Measurability or a green aggregate score establishes the intended quality or legitimacy of a threshold.
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.QUALIFICATION: Contextual project outcomes unmeasured; researchers rephrase/rate without independent initial annotations; 2023 predecessor shares data
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Adjacent template study excludes necessary/feasible contextual criteria; does not test QAW thresholds or legitimacy.

CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_CHALLENGED: Measurability or a green aggregate score establishes the intended quality or legitimacy of a threshold.
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.QUALIFICATION: 25 participants/four single-sentence tasks; limited interaction power; context self-reports unvalidated; not a universal lint-weight derivation
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Adjacent controlled domain-modeling study of wording factors; not validation of a performance threshold or governance decision.

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.SUPPORT: NFR 1992 process rationale; QAW third edition 2003; Glinz 2007 conceptual critique
HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.LIMITS: Origin means inspected antecedent, not an assertion of absolute first invention

FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.SUPPORT: Named language definitions and explicit counterexamples where applicable; no general effectiveness theorem
FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.LIMITS: The four-valued rule is an operational reconstruction; authority and world correspondence are not logically supplied by syntax

EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.ASSESSMENT: Frattini compares passive-voice and ambiguous-pronoun effects on domain-model outputs. This directly supports distinguishing a textual quality factor from its task-dependent consequence; it does not evaluate QAW workshops, performance-threshold authority or this record’s full quality-operationalization discipline.
EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.LIMITS: The sample is 25 participants with four single-sentence tasks, limited interaction power and unvalidated self-reported context measures. The instrumented BDD case is field-feasibility evidence without a control, not the source of this comparative result.

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.ASSESSMENT: Frattini is a new conceptual replication of Femmer et al.’s 2014 passive-voice/domain-modeling study, with additional ambiguous-pronoun analysis: 25 industry/university participants model four natural-language requirements. Its differential task outcomes are adjacent support for context-sensitive quality assessment, not a replication of QAW, proxy calibration or the full ERE-C0106 predicate.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: Introduction (conceptual replication of Femmer et al. 2014); §§3.4, 5.1–5.4, 6; source-table RETRACTION_CORRECTION_OR_VERSION_NOTES.

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.LIMITS: The new experiment does not reuse the earlier study’s data, but the four single-sentence tasks, limited interaction power and unvalidated context self-reports constrain transfer. It establishes no universal quality threshold, stakeholder-authority test or anti-gaming effect.

INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.SUPPORT: Qualitative practitioner cases or source-document rewrite; distinctions in source records apply
INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.LIMITS: Reported practices and perceptions are not randomized process benefits or universal prevalence

NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.SUPPORT: Quantification can erase material qualitative aspects and introduce incentives to optimize the proxy.
NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.LIMITS: A paper’s open problem is not an observed failure; the constructed cases are not incident reports

STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.SUPPORT: No external standard mandate asserted in this research sublane
STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.LIMITS: Language conventions and an author’s chosen criterion do not grant normative authority; cited ISO editions not independently adopted

PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Instrumentation plus denominator records, stakeholder task observations, threshold decision and counter-metrics.
PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: A tool’s existence/performance on selected examples does not establish organizational success

TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.SUPPORT: Booking response uses all valid requests at declared load, includes timeouts as failures, and records a stakeholder-selected 95th-percentile target plus error/abandonment constraints.
TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.LIMITS: Constructed examples expose distinctions; they are not evidence of implementation effectiveness in a target repository

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Some qualities remain disputed and indirectly observable; operational precision does not eliminate value judgments.
CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: Contrary findings narrow claims; they do not justify symmetric overgeneralization

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.SUPPORT: The measurement population and environment are observable; proxy validity and target choice are treated as separate claims.
ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.LIMITS: Population, sampling, timeout policy, instrument or intended concern changes invalidate prior comparability.

DOMAIN_VALIDITY.ASSESSMENT: Glinz distinguishes quality concerns from their representation and satisfaction; QAW refines quality scenarios; the BDD case connects selected performance scenarios to instruments. Frattini supplies adjacent evidence that wording quality depends on the consumer task and outcome.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.LIMITS: These do not validate every proxy-to-concern mapping or the entire anti-gaming rule. The changed-denominator latency example is an analytical construction, and task-quality findings do not establish a universal quality threshold.

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.ASSESSMENT: QAW elicits and prioritizes scenarios with system stakeholders, making participant perspectives and concerns inputs to quality refinement. This supports asking whose quality concern and use situation a criterion represents.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.LIMITS: Workshop participation and voting do not establish that all affected populations or adverse effects were considered. The BDD case supplies no independent completeness assessment of represented users.

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.ASSESSMENT: QAW separates stakeholder prioritization from technical scenario refinement; the BDD case uses agreed performance thresholds. These illustrate local criterion selection rather than a scientifically discovered universal acceptable-quality boundary.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.LIMITS: The sources do not verify a broadly applicable mandate for those thresholds. A published method, local vote or instrumentation result does not by itself authorize a trade-off for excluded parties.

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.ASSESSMENT: QAW’s scenario refinement makes stimulus, environment, affected artifact, response and response measure explicit. Glinz cautions against inferring satisfaction semantics solely from a requirement category; together these support scrutinizing the concern-to-measure step.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.LIMITS: There is no general proof that completing the scenario fields preserves the original concern or captures omitted populations. The proposed proxy-warrant condition is not a verified refinement algorithm.

REALIZABILITY.ASSESSMENT: The BDD case demonstrates a practical path from agreed scenarios to load generation and monitoring using Locust, Grafana and Jaeger. It supports feasibility of instrumenting selected performance observations.
REALIZABILITY.LIMITS: One company/team case does not show that arbitrary targets are achievable, that every quality is numerically measurable, or that the complete operationalization discipline scales to other environments.

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.ASSESSMENT: QAW keeps a scenario connected to a named quality concern and response measure; the BDD case connects scenarios to measurements and selected thresholds. These expose the links that a proxy-validity review would need to examine.
TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.LIMITS: No independent error-rate or semantic-accuracy evaluation of concern-to-metric traces is reported in the inspected material. Instrument connectivity does not establish that the measure represents the full concern.

ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.ASSESSMENT: The BDD case shows performance observations evaluated against agreed scenario thresholds. This provides a bounded example of evidence tied to a criterion, while QAW explains how a response measure makes the criterion explicit.
ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: A threshold result applies to the measured scenario and configuration. It does not establish valid proxy choice, legitimate authority for the threshold or satisfaction of every quality concern.

EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.ASSESSMENT: S020 provides a single instrumented BDD performance case with a brief team-lead interview. S027 studies passive voice and ambiguous pronouns in domain modeling, supporting task-relative quality assessment but not testing QAW or this combined operationalization rule.
EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.LIMITS: S020 lacks a counterfactual/control; S027 has 25 participants and four single-sentence tasks. Neither estimates the process benefit of this property’s population, authority, uncertainty and anti-gaming safeguards.

DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.ASSESSMENT: NFR reasoning retains conflicting quality contributions; QAW makes selected scenarios and priorities explicit; Frattini’s task-level results challenge treating all textual defects as equally consequential. These support decisions tied to a stated concern and outcome.
DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.LIMITS: They do not validate forced weighted sums, universal defect weights or optimal acceptance thresholds. The denominator counterexample exposes one invalid proxy inference without measuring the success of a replacement decision model.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Primary scenario method and taxonomy plus bounded BDD performance case; no general empirical threshold or universal proxy validity demonstrated. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.TRANSFERABILITY_LIMITS: Measured response in a selected scenario; external validity does not extend automatically to other users, load or failures. Some qualities remain disputed and indirectly observable; operational precision does not eliminate value judgments.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.UNVERIFIED_OR_OPEN_QUESTIONS: A deliberately adverse proxy-optimization test and representative task study can test whether passing the metric preserves the intended concern.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: A deliberately adverse proxy-optimization test and representative task study can test whether passing the metric preserves the intended concern.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: The reviewers inspected the complete claim/disposition population and selected detailed semantics/source bodies. Absence of an individual finding does not establish independent validation of every field, source or proposed predicate.

INTAKE.CROSSWALK_ELIGIBILITY_WITH_REASON: ELIGIBLE_WITH_CONTEXT: inspect equivalent existing mechanism, guard, cheap path and evidence before considering any adoption
TARGET_NEUTRAL_AUDIT_QUESTIONS: Which users/events disappear from the denominator, and could the metric improve while their intended outcome worsens?
Does a simpler existing mechanism already answer the same consumer question?
Which assumption, scope or authority change would require re-entry?
PROHIBITED_OVERCLAIMS: Measurability or a green aggregate score establishes the intended quality or legitimacy of a threshold.
No finding about any target repository or semantic owner is supplied.

SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.INPUT: Concern owner, source of threshold, measurement method, excluded cases, units, instrument and calibration/uncertainty.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.OUTPUT: Operationalize a quality with its affected population, stimulus/environment, response, observation and criterion authority; retain uncertainty, excluded dimensions and anti-gaming conditions.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.CONSUMER: Architect, tester, operator and receiving stakeholder deciding acceptable quality.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.BOUNDARY: Measured response in a selected scenario; external validity does not extend automatically to other users, load or failures.

QUALITY_OPERATIONALIZATION_PROFILE.APPLICATION: Target-neutral schema applied to the property; worked cases are explicitly analytical
QUALITY_OPERATIONALIZATION_PROFILE.QUALITY_MEANING: Operationalize a quality with its affected population, stimulus/environment, response, observation and criterion authority; retain uncertainty, excluded dimensions and anti-gaming conditions.
QUALITY_OPERATIONALIZATION_PROFILE.AFFECTED_PARTIES: Identify who experiences the quality and bears each trade-off; keep their interpretations and decision remit separate
QUALITY_OPERATIONALIZATION_PROFILE.SCENARIO: Booking response uses all valid requests at declared load, includes timeouts as failures, and records a stakeholder-selected 95th-percentile target plus error/abandonment constraints.
MEASURE_PROXY: Events and people included, including failed/abandoned events
Observable response with unit, window and uncertainty
Units and statistic fixed before evaluation
Who chose the threshold and why it is acceptable
Distinguish stipulated target from empirical boundary
QUALITY_OPERATIONALIZATION_PROFILE.THRESHOLD_AUTHORITY: A chosen SLA/acceptance target is a governance decision; it is not a scientifically established universal boundary.
QUALITY_OPERATIONALIZATION_PROFILE.EVIDENCE: Instrumentation plus denominator records, stakeholder task observations, threshold decision and counter-metrics.
QUALITY_OPERATIONALIZATION_PROFILE.UNCERTAINTY: Some qualities remain disputed and indirectly observable; operational precision does not eliminate value judgments.
QUALITY_OPERATIONALIZATION_PROFILE.TRADE_OFFS: Quantification can erase material qualitative aspects and introduce incentives to optimize the proxy.
QUALITY_OPERATIONALIZATION_PROFILE.GAMING_RISKS: The system drops slow requests; latency of completed requests improves while users receive fewer successful results. The old metric alone wrongly certifies quality.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.INPUT_AND_EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMEN: Alternative, target concern, contribution rationale/source, uncertainty and version-specific propagation rule.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Use qualitative contributions as explicit, defeasible reasons about alternatives under declared semantics; retain conflicts and uncertainty instead of assuming objective additive utility.

EVALUATION_MODE.DEFINITION: Mode describes how evidence is assessed, separate from the commissioned predicate-role enum. A sufficiency challenge tests an asserted implication or universal process benefit; ordinary operational assessment evaluates the bounded source-informed rule. Mechanical record checks do not settle semantic, empirical or authority judgments.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: Assess(subject: An alternative-to-quality argument in a declared model version, context, consumerDecision, evidenceSnapshot, validTime) -> PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|INAPPLICABLE

VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.CONSTRAINT: For iStar2: MAKE|HELP|HURT|BREAK; no invented numeric mapping

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Universal only over explicitly enumerated material items needed for the declared decision and search scope. No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: An alternative-to-quality argument in a declared model version
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Assessed at the named evidence/configuration snapshot. Hypothesized, desired, agreed and observed states remain distinct. Later changes require the stated invalidation procedure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Contribution directions are defensible and context-specific; stakeholders accept the qualitative interpretation, not necessarily the chosen trade-off.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: Material qualities conflict or their satisfaction cannot be responsibly reduced to one objective test.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Every contribution used to select an alternative has a version-specific meaning and an explicit support/assumption record; unresolved opposing contributions remain visible. Numeric aggregation without a justified mapping FAILS. Human assessment may yield UNKNOWN for a contested effect rather than forcing a score.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.LIMIT: Not a verbatim source theorem, source standard requirement or empirically validated universal acceptance algorithm

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Argument graph/table, measured supporting observations, dissent and defeated assumptions.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Alternative, target concern, contribution rationale/source, uncertainty and version-specific propagation rule.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: An informed evaluator checks applicability, identifies the exact claim and scope, reviews the named witnesses, tests the supplied counterexample class and records a reasoned four-valued outcome. Mechanical schema checks can establish presence/identity, not domain truth or authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite record checks are mechanically decidable. Semantic correspondence, legitimate representation, proxy validity and causal transfer generally require contextual judgment and may remain UNKNOWN. No claim of general decidability.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.TEXT: Caching helps response time but may hurt freshness; measured workload and stale-data risks are recorded and a scoped choice is authorized.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.TEXT: Help is assigned +1 and Hurt −1 without evidence; the highest total is declared objectively best and acceptable to every stakeholder.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: An agreed checksum-format constraint is directly checkable and has no relevant qualitative trade-off.

FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_POSITIVE: Filling every edge with a sign is not a reason for the sign.
FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_NEGATIVE: Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. Filling every edge with a sign is not a reason for the sign.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Change to contribution evidence or interaction context invalidates propagated conclusions and selected trade-off.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Maintaining rationale, assessing interactions and reviewing subjective contributions; too many edges hide rather than explain trade-offs. Alternative: One directly agreed criterion and one feasible design do not require a softgoal network.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Foundational framework and worked examples provide reasoning rationale; formal-semantic and real-size validation limits explicitly admitted in 1992. The operational rule is a proposed audit discriminator, not a measured process-effect claim.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE: Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.RULE: Every contribution used to select an alternative has a version-specific meaning and an explicit support/assumption record; unresolved opposing contributions remain visible. Numeric aggregation without a justified mapping FAILS. Human assessment may yield UNKNOWN for a contested effect rather than forcing a score.

OUTCOMES.PASS: Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation
OUTCOMES.FAIL: An applicable observed contradiction, failed criterion or valid counterexample defeats the specified claim
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Relevant evidence/meaning/authority is missing, disputed or not discriminating
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: An explicit guard excludes the claim; cheap path must be justified

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.EMPTY_SCOPE_RULE: Empty obligation/source sets never establish completeness by vacuity; show scope adequacy or label inapplicable/unknown.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.POSITIVE_WITNESS_OR_WORKED_EXAMPLE: Caching helps response time but may hurt freshness; measured workload and stale-data risks are recorded and a scoped choice is authorized.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.NEGATIVE_WITNESS_OR_COUNTEREXAMPLE: Help is assigned +1 and Hurt −1 without evidence; the highest total is declared objectively best and acceptable to every stakeholder.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.NON_TRIGGER_EXAMPLE: An agreed checksum-format constraint is directly checkable and has no relevant qualitative trade-off.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.OBSERVABILITY_AND_MISSINGNESS: Argument graph/table, measured supporting observations, dissent and defeated assumptions. Missing evidence remains UNKNOWN unless an explicit contradicted claim is being tested.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.CURRENTNESS_AND_INVALIDATION: Change to contribution evidence or interaction context invalidates propagated conclusions and selected trade-off.

CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Qualitative labels can conceal arbitrary judgment; numerical encodings can manufacture certainty.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.KNOWN_FAILURES_AND_MISUSES: Help is assigned +1 and Hurt −1 without evidence; the highest total is declared objectively best and acceptable to every stakeholder.

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.LIMITS: Change to contribution evidence or interaction context invalidates propagated conclusions and selected trade-off.

DOMAIN_VALIDITY.ASSESSMENT: The NFR framework uses qualitative refinement and correlation to reason about design alternatives; Yu and iStar provide intentional-model interpretations; Glinz separates qualities from the assumption that all such requirements are inherently soft.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §§8.1–8.3, especially pp. 110–113; SD and SR model definitions

DOMAIN_VALIDITY.LIMITS: These ground the concepts but do not establish that a particular Help/Hurt attribution matches real effects. Source-defined relation meaning and the empirical truth of a contribution remain distinct.

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.ASSESSMENT: The inspected contribution-model definitions and illustrative reasoning do not evaluate whether the concerns and affected parties in a softgoal model exhaust the relevant stakeholder population.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §§8.1–8.3, especially pp. 110–113; SD and SR model definitions

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.LIMITS: A model can preserve known conflicts while omitting a constituency. This assessment neither asserts completeness nor infers empirical exclusion from the absence of a coverage study.

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.ASSESSMENT: The NFR paper and iStar guide define the intended meanings of qualitative links and satisficing in their respective versions. They are primary references for interpreting the notation used in an argument.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.LIMITS: They are not mandates authorizing a trade-off for affected people. A positive contribution or favorable propagated label does not create consent or binding acceptance.

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.ASSESSMENT: The NFR source describes refinement/correlation and qualitative satisficing; iStar 2.0 separately defines refinement and Make/Help/Hurt/Break. This supports checking which version’s interpretation a derived conclusion uses.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.LIMITS: The 1992 authors acknowledge missing formal-semantic/proof foundations and need for real-size evaluation; propagation was not independently reproduced here. No arbitrary numeric conversion or cross-version preservation theorem is justified.

REALIZABILITY.ASSESSMENT: Worked reasoning illustrates how alternatives and competing quality effects can be represented and discussed. It establishes an expressible argument structure for considering implementation choices.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §§8.1–8.3, especially pp. 110–113; SD and SR model definitions

REALIZABILITY.LIMITS: A satisficing label is not a guarantee that an alternative can be implemented or achieve its attributed effects. Real-size validation is explicitly limited in the inspected foundational material.

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.ASSESSMENT: The NFR and intentional-model sources make qualitative contribution and dependency relations visible, providing a structure for recording why an alternative is believed to affect a concern.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §§8.1–8.3, especially pp. 110–113; SD and SR model definitions

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.LIMITS: The inspected evidence does not quantify whether those reasons or link directions are semantically accurate in real projects. A labeled edge remains a defeasible attribution, not an observed causal trace.

ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.ASSESSMENT: Satisficing is a source-defined reasoning treatment for qualities, and Glinz distinguishes representation from satisfaction. The inspected material does not validate that a propagated qualitative conclusion corresponds to an authorized receiving party’s acceptance criterion.
ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: This record therefore treats contribution assessment and acceptance of a trade-off as separate questions. No empirical acceptance guarantee follows from model evaluation.

EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.ASSESSMENT: The examined support consists of foundational framework definitions, illustrative examples, a language guide and conceptual taxonomy criticism. The NFR paper and Yu explicitly retain substantial real-size/content-validation limits.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §§8.1–8.3, especially pp. 110–113; SD and SR model definitions

EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.LIMITS: No comparative causal effect of this defeasible-contribution discipline is established in the inspected base. This is not a claim that the wider NFR or iStar literature has no empirical studies.

DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.ASSESSMENT: The framework offers defeasible reasons for why alternatives help or hurt concerns under stated assumptions. The iStar guide’s qualitative contribution categories support preserving uncertainty and opposing effects instead of inventing additive values.
DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.LIMITS: Neither source supplies a universal utility scale, justified +1/−1 aggregation, objective optimum or proof of stakeholder agreement. The property’s explicit-support rule remains a proposed discipline rather than a validated optimizer.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Foundational framework and worked examples provide reasoning rationale; formal-semantic and real-size validation limits explicitly admitted in 1992. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.TRANSFERABILITY_LIMITS: Weak contribution is not a probability, magnitude or universal effect; Make/Break semantics belong to a named model and premises. Judgment disagreement and interaction effects may remain irreducible; evidence may support only direction.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: Independently test the pivotal contribution under the chosen scenario, or expose how reversing it changes the decision.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: The reviewers inspected the complete claim/disposition population and selected detailed semantics/source bodies. Absence of an individual finding does not establish independent validation of every field, source or proposed predicate.

EVALUATION_MODE.DEFINITION: Mode describes how evidence is assessed, separate from the commissioned predicate-role enum. A sufficiency challenge tests an asserted implication or universal process benefit; ordinary operational assessment evaluates the bounded source-informed rule. Mechanical record checks do not settle semantic, empirical or authority judgments.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: Assess(subject: A scenario family, general requirement and derived tests, context, consumerDecision, evidenceSnapshot, validTime) -> PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|INAPPLICABLE

No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A scenario family, general requirement and derived tests

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: The requirement changes only a static label and a before/after check observes the whole effect.

FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_NEGATIVE: Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. A large count of Given/When/Then tests is not coverage without a defined behavior domain.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE: Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

PASS for examples means those traces meet their criteria; a broader claim needs a separate coverage/generalization warrant. PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: CheckSyntax(statement, declaredPattern, EARS2009Definition) -> PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|INAPPLICABLE

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Universal only over explicitly enumerated material items needed for the declared decision and search scope. No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: Repeated event/state-dependent statements whose structure obscures activation or response.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Check the declared pattern: ubiquitous names system and required response; event-driven uses WHEN with the event and any stated precondition; state-driven uses WHILE with the relevant state; optional-feature uses WHERE with the feature; unwanted behavior uses IF with the unwanted condition and THEN with system response. Combined patterns preserve the corresponding clauses. PASS only if the declared structural slots and ordering are present; a malformed/missing required slot is FAIL. Unknown pattern interpretation is UNKNOWN. This is not semantic completeness, necessity, feasibility or authority.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.LIMIT: Not a verbatim source theorem, source standard requirement or empirically validated universal acceptance algorithm

Mechanical schema checks can establish presence/identity, not domain truth or authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Once the chosen grammar/slot convention is fixed, structural conformance is a finite check. Natural-language domain interpretation is deliberately excluded and evaluated by P02.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.TEXT: An event-driven sentence has explicit WHEN trigger, system and shall-response slots, so its declared syntactic form passes even before external validity is assessed.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.TEXT: An event-driven sentence omits the required response; it fails the selected structural rule.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: A fixed export-format constraint is already precise and a template adds no useful information.

FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_POSITIVE: The modal verb and occupied slots are not a full requirement-quality test.
FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_NEGATIVE: Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. The modal verb and occupied slots are not a full requirement-quality test.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Changed pattern version or trigger/exception/domain definition requires renewed meaning-preservation assessment.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Training, semantic preservation review and template edge cases; novice rewriting can damage meaning. Alternative: A short unambiguous static constraint can stay a direct sentence if all consumers understand it.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Original EARS2009 structural definition and this finite operational check establish conformance only. A conforming infeasible or unauthorized statement remains a valid counterexample to broader sufficiency.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: A structured rewrite preserves the original intended meaning, or its substantive change is explicitly sourced and authorized within scope.

EVALUATION_MODE.DEFINITION: Mode describes how evidence is assessed, separate from the commissioned predicate-role enum. A sufficiency challenge tests an asserted implication or universal process benefit; ordinary operational assessment evaluates the bounded source-informed rule. Mechanical record checks do not settle semantic, empirical or authority judgments.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: CheckMeaning(originalStatement, rewrittenStatement, domainInterpretation, changeDecision, evidenceSnapshot) -> PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|INAPPLICABLE

VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.CONSTRAINT: Original, rewritten statement and change rationale

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Universal only over explicitly enumerated material items needed for the declared decision and search scope. No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A natural-language requirement statement and its interpretation
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Assessed at the named evidence/configuration snapshot. Hypothesized, desired, agreed and observed states remain distinct. Later changes require the stated invalidation procedure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Domain vocabulary and pattern interpretation are understood; a syntactic rewrite preserves intended meaning.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A requirement is being rewritten or translated into a structured pattern and the result is claimed to preserve or validly change meaning.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Compare actor, activation, exceptions, response, modality and scope under a shared domain interpretation. PASS if each material meaning is preserved or a changed obligation has a separate valid source/decision witness. A known unintended omission/change is FAIL. Unresolved vocabulary, missing source intent or unreviewed substantive change is UNKNOWN. A no-rewrite case makes preservation checking INAPPLICABLE. P01 syntax PASS supplies no semantic-preservation result.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.LIMIT: Not a verbatim source theorem, source standard requirement or empirically validated universal acceptance algorithm

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Statement pair, pattern grammar and semantic review with source terminology.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Original statement, selected template/version, semantic interpretation and reviewer/source for changed meaning.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: An informed evaluator checks applicability, identifies the exact claim and scope, reviews the named witnesses, tests the supplied counterexample class and records a reasoned four-valued outcome. Mechanical schema checks can establish presence/identity, not domain truth or authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite record checks are mechanically decidable. Semantic correspondence, legitimate representation, proxy validity and causal transfer generally require contextual judgment and may remain UNKNOWN. No claim of general decidability.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.TEXT: A command-triggered response explicitly names the trigger, relevant state, system and response, with a domain expert confirming the interpretation.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.TEXT: An author removes an exception to fit a simpler template; the sentence is grammatical but changes the required behavior.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: A fixed export-format constraint is already precise and a template adds no useful information.

FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_POSITIVE: The modal verb and occupied slots are not a full requirement-quality test.
FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_NEGATIVE: Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. The modal verb and occupied slots are not a full requirement-quality test.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Changed pattern version or trigger/exception/domain definition requires renewed meaning-preservation assessment.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Training, semantic preservation review and template edge cases; novice rewriting can damage meaning. Alternative: A short unambiguous static constraint can stay a direct sentence if all consumers understand it.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Human/domain correspondence judgment tied to the original statement and current sources; no claim of general semantic-equivalence decidability or universal template benefit.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE: Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.RULE: Given a fitting requirement type, check explicit slots and pattern use, then separately assess meaning preservation. Syntax PASS alone does not pass the semantic review; unknown domain terms or an unreviewed substantive rewrite yield UNKNOWN for meaning.

OUTCOMES.PASS: Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation
OUTCOMES.FAIL: An applicable observed contradiction, failed criterion or valid counterexample defeats the specified claim
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Relevant evidence/meaning/authority is missing, disputed or not discriminating
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: An explicit guard excludes the claim; cheap path must be justified

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.EMPTY_SCOPE_RULE: Empty obligation/source sets never establish completeness by vacuity; show scope adequacy or label inapplicable/unknown.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.POSITIVE_WITNESS_OR_WORKED_EXAMPLE: A command-triggered response explicitly names the trigger, relevant state, system and response, with a domain expert confirming the interpretation.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.NEGATIVE_WITNESS_OR_COUNTEREXAMPLE: An author removes an exception to fit a simpler template; the sentence is grammatical but changes the required behavior.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.NON_TRIGGER_EXAMPLE: A fixed export-format constraint is already precise and a template adds no useful information.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.OBSERVABILITY_AND_MISSINGNESS: Statement pair, pattern grammar and semantic review with source terminology. Missing evidence remains UNKNOWN unless an explicit contradicted claim is being tested.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.CURRENTNESS_AND_INVALIDATION: Changed pattern version or trigger/exception/domain definition requires renewed meaning-preservation assessment.

CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Benefits are partly expert interpretation and heuristic alignment; structured rewriting can lose meaning and does not reveal all missing requirements.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.KNOWN_FAILURES_AND_MISUSES: An author removes an exception to fit a simpler template; the sentence is grammatical but changes the required behavior.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESPONSE_OR_DESCENDANT_FORM: Limit claims to sentence structure and use quality-in-use evaluation for the real reader/task.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.WHAT_CHANGED_AND_WHAT_DID_NOT: Moves from an initial36-statementcase to comparative linguistic analysis; reliable broad usability and project benefits remain unproved.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESIDUAL_LIMITS: Lexical ambiguity, unknown requirements, feasibility and authority remain outside the template.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.CEREMONY_VERSUS_MECHANISM: The modal verb and occupied slots are not a full requirement-quality test.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RETENTION_RATIONALE: Retain the bounded mechanism with explicit guard, evidence and cheap path. Limit claims to sentence structure and use quality-in-use evaluation for the real reader/task.

SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_SUPPORTED: Preconditions/triggers/responses; five patterns; 36 source statements rewritten into 47; omissions not established eliminated
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Original EARS pattern definitions and small author rewriting case; directly relevant but bounded syntax-aid evidence.
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: Single small high-level safety domain; specialist interpretation co-intervention and subjective ratings; no universal applicability

SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_SUPPORTED: Five templates, 249 originals/1764 phrasings; heuristic wording effects; user experiment 43 mostly students judged unreliable by authors
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Direct template comparison including EARS and separate Adv-EARS; shared-data journal extension, not independent replication of the 2009 EARS case or the full predicate.
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: Contextual project outcomes unmeasured; researchers rephrase/rate without independent initial annotations; 2023 predecessor shares data

SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_SUPPORTED: Consumer/task-relative quality effects; passive voice and ambiguous pronouns have different effects on domain modeling
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Adjacent conceptual replication of passive-voice/domain-modeling effects, not an EARS experiment or replication.
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: 25 participants/four single-sentence tasks; limited interaction power; context self-reports unvalidated; not a universal lint-weight derivation

CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_CHALLENGED: Template conformance guarantees clear, complete, valid and feasible requirements.
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.QUALIFICATION: Single small high-level safety domain; specialist interpretation co-intervention and subjective ratings; no universal applicability
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Original EARS omission caveat and case-design limits; syntax aid does not prove general completeness.

CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_CHALLENGED: Template conformance guarantees clear, complete, valid and feasible requirements.
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.QUALIFICATION: Contextual project outcomes unmeasured; researchers rephrase/rate without independent initial annotations; 2023 predecessor shares data
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Template-comparison scope excludes contextual necessity/feasibility and limits usability conclusions.

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.SUPPORT: Mavin et al. 2009 EARS; Großer et al. 2024 comparative templates
HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.LIMITS: Origin means inspected antecedent, not an assertion of absolute first invention

FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.SUPPORT: Named language definitions and explicit counterexamples where applicable; no general effectiveness theorem
FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.LIMITS: The four-valued rule is an operational reconstruction; authority and world correspondence are not logically supplied by syntax

EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.ASSESSMENT: S018 supplies the original small EARS rewriting case; S019 compares EARS and four other template systems using selected linguistic heuristics on 249 originals/1,764 phrasings. S027 separately compares passive voice and pronouns in domain modeling and contributes a task-relative caution, not an EARS treatment result.
EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.LIMITS: The original case has specialist co-intervention and subjective ratings; the benchmark shares predecessor data and excludes necessity/feasibility. Its 43-person user experiment cannot support reliable usability answers by the authors’ account. No universal template superiority follows.

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.ASSESSMENT: Großer’s journal article extends its 2023 conference study using the previously created 249-original rephrasing dataset and enhanced analysis plus additional experiments; it directly bears on EARS as one of five template systems, with Adv-EARS kept distinct. Frattini separately replicates a passive-voice/domain-modeling subclaim and is adjacent task-quality evidence, not an EARS study.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: Introduction (extension of the 2023 conference predecessor, reference [18]); §§5.1.1–5.1.4, 8.1–8.3, 9; source-table RETRACTION_CORRECTION_OR_VERSION_NOTES.
Introduction (conceptual replication of Femmer et al. 2014); §§3.4, 5.1–5.4, 6; source-table RETRACTION_CORRECTION_OR_VERSION_NOTES.

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.LIMITS: The shared template dataset is not an independent replication of the 2009 EARS case or the proposed ERE-C0109 predicate. The 43-person mostly-student template user experiment was judged unreliable for its usability questions. Frattini’s 25-person/four-task experiment supplies no EARS effect estimate.

INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.SUPPORT: Qualitative practitioner cases or source-document rewrite; distinctions in source records apply
INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.LIMITS: Reported practices and perceptions are not randomized process benefits or universal prevalence

NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.SUPPORT: Benefits are partly expert interpretation and heuristic alignment; structured rewriting can lose meaning and does not reveal all missing requirements.
NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.LIMITS: A paper’s open problem is not an observed failure; the constructed cases are not incident reports

STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.SUPPORT: No external standard mandate asserted in this research sublane
STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.LIMITS: Language conventions and an author’s chosen criterion do not grant normative authority; cited ISO editions not independently adopted

PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Statement pair, pattern grammar and semantic review with source terminology.
PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: A tool’s existence/performance on selected examples does not establish organizational success

TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.SUPPORT: A command-triggered response explicitly names the trigger, relevant state, system and response, with a domain expert confirming the interpretation.
TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.LIMITS: Constructed examples expose distinctions; they are not evidence of implementation effectiveness in a target repository

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Lexical ambiguity, unknown requirements, feasibility and authority remain outside the template.
CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: Contrary findings narrow claims; they do not justify symmetric overgeneralization

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.SUPPORT: Domain vocabulary and pattern interpretation are understood; a syntactic rewrite preserves intended meaning.
ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.LIMITS: Changed pattern version or trigger/exception/domain definition requires renewed meaning-preservation assessment.

DOMAIN_VALIDITY.ASSESSMENT: The original EARS study supplies five activation/response patterns and a small high-level safety-domain rewrite. The template benchmark includes EARS and Adv-EARS as distinct systems and evaluates selected wording characteristics; Frattini supplies an adjacent consumer-task perspective.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.LIMITS: Wording improvement does not establish necessity, feasibility or world correspondence. The original specialist interpretation and subjective ratings limit causal attribution, and the benchmark explicitly excludes necessity/feasibility.

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.ASSESSMENT: The original paper concerns high-level stakeholder requirements, but the inspected rewriting and template-comparison evaluations assess statements and language tasks, not whether every affected stakeholder or relevant need was included.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.LIMITS: The label stakeholder requirement and a filled EARS pattern do not constitute a stakeholder-coverage assessment. The evidence does not support general completeness.

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.ASSESSMENT: The original EARS paper defines its pattern conventions and use of required responses. It is a primary reference for what conforming to that syntax means.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.LIMITS: Neither the word shall nor conformity to the template supplies issuer authority, stakeholder consent or an applicable external mandate. The benchmark’s cited standards are not independently adopted obligations here.

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.ASSESSMENT: The original case rewrites 36 source statements into 47 and includes specialist interpretation; the benchmark also constructs alternate phrasings. These show rewriting activity, but the inspected evidence does not establish a general meaning-preservation guarantee for applying an EARS pattern.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.LIMITS: Linguistic ratings and template slots do not prove that removed exceptions or changed guards preserve the original obligation. Any formal mapping or semantic review is a separate warrant.

REALIZABILITY.ASSESSMENT: The original rewrite and benchmark show that EARS can be applied to concrete requirement statements. The benchmark’s user experiment also exposes substantial training and domain-knowledge demands.
REALIZABILITY.LIMITS: The 43-participant user experiment was judged unable to yield reliable usability answers; authoring a conforming sentence does not establish technical feasibility of the stated response.

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.ASSESSMENT: The inspected studies retain original and rephrased statements for linguistic comparison, but an evaluation of semantic source-to-rewrite trace accuracy under requirement change was not examined.
TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.LIMITS: Retaining paired texts provides review material; it is not a validated relation saying that all original meaning, exceptions and authority were preserved.

ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.ASSESSMENT: EARS makes conditions, triggers and required responses easier to inspect, but the original paper explicitly cannot establish that all omitted requirements were discovered. The benchmark assesses selected intrinsic criteria and withholds necessity/feasibility.
ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: No complete mapping from syntax compliance to valid acceptance for the actual need is established. Executable oracles, coverage and receiving authority require separate evidence.

EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.ASSESSMENT: EARS’s small author case reports rewriting results; Großer compares five template systems across 249 originals and 1,764 phrasings. Frattini instead tests passive voice/pronouns during domain modeling and is adjacent evidence about task-relative wording effects.
EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.LIMITS: The benchmark shares data with its conference predecessor; its 43-person mostly-student usability experiment is not a reliable comparative result by the authors’ account. No universal process advantage or full-predicate validation follows.

DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.ASSESSMENT: Original EARS distinguishes structural forms, while the benchmark reports context-dependent template trade-offs without a universal winner. Frattini gives a concrete reason to assess a wording rule against a downstream task rather than an undifferentiated defect count.
DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.LIMITS: These do not validate a globally best template, an automatic validity gate or a uniform lint weighting. Original EARS, Adv-EARS and other template systems must retain their separate meanings.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Original small author case and2024 comparisons support selected linguistic effects; neither establishes necessity, feasibility or global completeness. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.TRANSFERABILITY_LIMITS: Original2009 high-level stakeholder focus; Adv-EARS and other templates are separate systems. Lexical ambiguity, unknown requirements, feasibility and authority remain outside the template.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.UNVERIFIED_OR_OPEN_QUESTIONS: Ask actual readers to use the original/rewrite for the intended downstream task and check meaning errors, not merely lint scores.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: Ask actual readers to use the original/rewrite for the intended downstream task and check meaning errors, not merely lint scores.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: The reviewers inspected the complete claim/disposition population and selected detailed semantics/source bodies. Absence of an individual finding does not establish independent validation of every field, source or proposed predicate.

INTAKE.CROSSWALK_ELIGIBILITY_WITH_REASON: ELIGIBLE_WITH_CONTEXT: inspect equivalent existing mechanism, guard, cheap path and evidence before considering any adoption
TARGET_NEUTRAL_AUDIT_QUESTIONS: Which exact ambiguity or omission did the pattern remove, and who checked that meaning survived?
Does a simpler existing mechanism already answer the same consumer question?
Which assumption, scope or authority change would require re-entry?
PROHIBITED_OVERCLAIMS: Template conformance guarantees clear, complete, valid and feasible requirements.
No finding about any target repository or semantic owner is supplied.

SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.INPUT: Original statement, selected template/version, semantic interpretation and reviewer/source for changed meaning.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.OUTPUT: Use a suitable EARS pattern to expose condition/trigger/response omissions and promote consistent interpretation, with domain review and explicit semantics remaining separate.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.CONSUMER: Requirement author and reader who need consistent sentence structure.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.BOUNDARY: Original2009 high-level stakeholder focus; Adv-EARS and other templates are separate systems.

SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.APPLICATION: Target-neutral schema applied to the property; worked cases are explicitly analytical
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.NARRATIVE_NOTATION: Five simple structural patterns separate optional conditions, triggers and response.
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.BEHAVIOURAL_SCOPE: Original2009 high-level stakeholder focus; Adv-EARS and other templates are separate systems.
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.EXCEPTIONS: An author removes an exception to fit a simpler template; the sentence is grammatical but changes the required behavior.
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.ASSUMPTIONS: Domain vocabulary and pattern interpretation are understood; a syntactic rewrite preserves intended meaning.
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.FORMAL_LINKS: Any mapping to a state/temporal specification or executable oracle must be named and checked separately; no such map is presumed from prose form
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.TEST_DERIVATION: Select ubiquitous, event-driven, state-driven, unwanted-behavior or optional-feature form; review what belongs in each slot and retain interpreted domain definitions.
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.EVIDENCE_LIMITS: Original small author case and2024 comparisons support selected linguistic effects; neither establishes necessity, feasibility or global completeness.
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: A short unambiguous static constraint can stay a direct sentence if all consumers understand it.
