GENEALOGY.DISPUTED_ATTRIBUTION_OR_ANACHRONISM_RISK: No claim of absolute first invention. Counterexample rejects universal sufficiency; no rejection of useful writing aids.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: Candidate sufficiency claim: a template-conforming or lint-clean requirement is therefore necessary, feasible, complete and valid for its stakeholders.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: A requirement statement plus a proposed validity decision
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.FAILURE_MODE_OR_LIMIT_ADDRESSED: Intrinsic textual scores are promoted into claims about need, feasibility, authority or achieved outcomes.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MECHANISM: The rejected inference replaces external evidence with a textual proxy.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Evaluate each rule against actual downstream tasks and retain unmeasured validity dimensions.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Would automate validity approval; no inspected source warrants that payoff.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE: EARS expressly cannot establish eliminated omissions; comparative templates exclude necessity/feasibility; current LLM study deliberately scores intrinsic criteria only.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Reviewer tempted to approve a requirement from a dashboard or quality score.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ALTERNATIVE_MECHANISMS: Use lint as an issue-finding aid, then gather evidence for the validity dimensions actually claimed.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: A textual score is used as a sufficient acceptance/baselining gate for external validity.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Lint used only for a named syntactic convention is legitimate and this sufficiency claim is inapplicable.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: A valid implication would need an established mapping from all relevant textual features to external need/feasibility/authority; no such mapping follows.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ENVIRONMENT_AND_BOUNDARY: Counterexample rejects universal sufficiency; no rejection of useful writing aids.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: Counterexample rejects universal sufficiency; no rejection of useful writing aids. Excludes any target repository finding or inter-lineage ownership assignment.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: Textual syntax does not confer stakeholder mandate.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.INPUT_AND_EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMEN: Separate evaluated textual feature, score, standard/version, consumer task and external validity witnesses.

DEPENDENCIES_AND_CONFLICTS.LIMIT: Relations are conditional; see internal_relations, not all listed items are mandatory prerequisites

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.FAILURE_OF_ASSUMPTIONS: “When an order is placed, the system shall deliver the physical parcel anywhere within one millisecond” conforms to a pattern but is infeasible in the stated world.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.COST_AND_MAINTENANCE_BURDEN: Automatic lint is cheap; false reassurance and reviewer attention to inconsequential rules can be expensive.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RETIREMENT_OR_REENTRY_CONDITION: Reject sufficiency; reconsider only a narrow outcome with demonstrated criterion correspondence.

ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.INTENDED_MEANING: Observed result for a named text rule
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.BEARER_OR_OBJECT_TYPE: The exact requirement-text version evaluated by a named text rule, tool/version and configuration, with the actual evaluation/run and observed output identified.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.UNIT_OR_SCALE: Boolean TRUE/FALSE for a Boolean rule, or the named rule-defined score with its range, direction and scale declared. No generic physical/time/cost unit and no aggregation across unlike rules.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.ALLOWED_VALUES_OR_CONSTRAINTS: Identify the text, rule, tool/version, configuration and actual evaluation/run. Record only an established output in the declared Boolean or score domain; missing or unresolved output is not zero or FALSE.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.OBSERVED_DERIVED_ASSUMED_OR_STIPULATED: Observed output of the identified evaluation, or a derivation under the named text rule whose inputs and procedure are supplied. The choice of rule/threshold is stipulated. External validity is not inferred from this output.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.MEASUREMENT_OR_DERIVATION_METHOD: Apply or inspect the named text rule on the exact text under the identified tool/version, configuration and evaluation/run; record its actual Boolean result or rule-defined score. External need, feasibility, stakeholder coverage and authority are assessed separately in A02 and compared by P01, not used to redefine A01. For a stochastic tool, distinguish the recorded run from any proposed later run; no deterministic repeatability is assumed.

SOURCE_OR_WITNESS.LOCAL_WITNESS_REQUIRED: The exact evaluated text and rule, tool/version/configuration, run or derivation record and output. External validity witnesses belong to A02 and the joint P01 judgment, not the measurement of A01.

ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.RESOLUTION_AND_UNCERTAINTY: Retain the rule-specific textual unit, score resolution and actual output. Ambiguous rule interpretation or unestablished evaluation output is UNKNOWN. Disagreement between outputs from different runs is retained rather than averaged into an invented validity score.

MISSING_UNKNOWN_NOT_APPLICABLE_DISTINCTI.UNKNOWN: The relevant text-rule output, rule interpretation or evaluation identity is not established. Unknown external validity alone does not make an established intrinsic output unknown.
MISSING_UNKNOWN_NOT_APPLICABLE_DISTINCTI.NOT_APPLICABLE: An explicit guard excludes the attribute in this context; an empty field is not sufficient

ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.VALID_TIME_OR_VERSION: An observation is bound to its exact text, rule, tool/version, configuration and actual evaluation/run. Changed evaluation inputs require a new assessment for current use; the old observation remains an attributed historical fact. External domain, population or mandate changes alone do not change that recorded text-rule output.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.CHANGE_IMPACT: Re-evaluate A01 for a changed text, rule, tool/version, configuration or requested run. A02 and P01 require separate reconsideration when external need, feasibility, population or authority changes; an unchanged intrinsic output does not carry external validity forward. A02 is the paired comparison, not a value-generating dependency of A01.

ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.INTENDED_MEANING: Necessity, feasibility, authority and scoped completeness evidence
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.BEARER_OR_OBJECT_TYPE: A requirement statement plus a proposed validity decision
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.UNIT_OR_SCALE: Qualitative record, no ordinal score
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.ALLOWED_VALUES_OR_CONSTRAINTS: UNKNOWN distinct from missing syntax defect
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.OBSERVED_DERIVED_ASSUMED_OR_STIPULATED: Observed source/record where available; derived judgment must name its rule; criterion choices are stipulated and labeled; unsupported content is assumed, not observed
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.MEASUREMENT_OR_DERIVATION_METHOD: Text-rule outputs compared with domain, feasibility and authority evidence.

SOURCE_OR_WITNESS.LOCAL_WITNESS_REQUIRED: Separate evaluated textual feature, score, standard/version, consumer task and external validity witnesses.

ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.RESOLUTION_AND_UNCERTAINTY: Resolution is the declared item, role, relation or observation—not a whole-project score. Disagreement and measurement uncertainty are retained in the record.

MISSING_UNKNOWN_NOT_APPLICABLE_DISTINCTI.UNKNOWN: Relevant value or validity cannot yet be established
MISSING_UNKNOWN_NOT_APPLICABLE_DISTINCTI.NOT_APPLICABLE: An explicit guard excludes the attribute in this context; an empty field is not sufficient

ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.VALID_TIME_OR_VERSION: Changing the domain, population or mandate invalidates validity even if the lint score remains identical.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.CHANGE_IMPACT: Changing the domain, population or mandate invalidates validity even if the lint score remains identical.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Candidate sufficiency claim: a template-conforming or lint-clean requirement is therefore necessary, feasible, complete and valid for its stakeholders.

EVALUATION_MODE.DEFINITION: Mode describes how evidence is assessed, separate from the commissioned predicate-role enum. A sufficiency challenge tests an asserted implication or universal process benefit; ordinary operational assessment evaluates the bounded source-informed rule. Mechanical record checks do not settle semantic, empirical or authority judgments.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: Assess(subject: A requirement statement plus a proposed validity decision, context, consumerDecision, evidenceSnapshot, validTime) -> PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|INAPPLICABLE

VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.CONSTRAINT: Identify the text, rule, tool/version, configuration and actual evaluation/run. Record only an established output in the declared Boolean or score domain; missing or unresolved output is not zero or FALSE.
UNKNOWN distinct from missing syntax defect

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Universal only over explicitly enumerated material items needed for the declared decision and search scope. No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A requirement statement plus a proposed validity decision
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Assessed at the named evidence/configuration snapshot. Hypothesized, desired, agreed and observed states remain distinct. Later changes require the stated invalidation procedure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: A valid implication would need an established mapping from all relevant textual features to external need/feasibility/authority; no such mapping follows.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A textual score is used as a sufficient acceptance/baselining gate for external validity.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: For TextConforms ⇒ ValidForNeed, a conforming invented or infeasible requirement is a counterexample and FAIL. Case-specific corroborated validity can PASS only that case; absent world/authority evidence is UNKNOWN. Mere syntax review with no validity inference is INAPPLICABLE.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.LIMIT: Not a verbatim source theorem, source standard requirement or empirically validated universal acceptance algorithm

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Text-rule outputs compared with domain, feasibility and authority evidence.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Separate evaluated textual feature, score, standard/version, consumer task and external validity witnesses.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: An informed evaluator checks applicability, identifies the exact claim and scope, reviews the named witnesses, tests the supplied counterexample class and records a reasoned four-valued outcome. Mechanical schema checks can establish presence/identity, not domain truth or authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite record checks are mechanically decidable. Semantic correspondence, legitimate representation, proxy validity and causal transfer generally require contextual judgment and may remain UNKNOWN. No claim of general decidability.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.TEXT: A concise requirement is both pattern-conforming and independently shown necessary, feasible and authorized; validity is supported by those separate witnesses.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.TEXT: “When an order is placed, the system shall deliver the physical parcel anywhere within one millisecond” conforms to a pattern but is infeasible in the stated world.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: An editor flags a missing unit without asserting any external validity.

FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_POSITIVE: A perfect score may signify obedience to a style guide without a defensible requirement.
FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_NEGATIVE: Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. A perfect score may signify obedience to a style guide without a defensible requirement.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Changing the domain, population or mandate invalidates validity even if the lint score remains identical.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Automatic lint is cheap; false reassurance and reviewer attention to inconsequential rules can be expensive. Alternative: Lint used only for a named syntactic convention is legitimate and this sufficiency claim is inapplicable.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: EARS expressly cannot establish eliminated omissions; comparative templates exclude necessity/feasibility; current LLM study deliberately scores intrinsic criteria only. The operational rule is a proposed audit discriminator, not a measured process-effect claim.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE: Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.RULE: For TextConforms ⇒ ValidForNeed, a conforming invented or infeasible requirement is a counterexample and FAIL. Case-specific corroborated validity can PASS only that case; absent world/authority evidence is UNKNOWN. Mere syntax review with no validity inference is INAPPLICABLE.

OUTCOMES.PASS: Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation
OUTCOMES.FAIL: An applicable observed contradiction, failed criterion or valid counterexample defeats the specified claim
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Relevant evidence/meaning/authority is missing, disputed or not discriminating
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: An explicit guard excludes the claim; cheap path must be justified

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.EMPTY_SCOPE_RULE: Empty obligation/source sets never establish completeness by vacuity; show scope adequacy or label inapplicable/unknown.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.POSITIVE_WITNESS_OR_WORKED_EXAMPLE: A concise requirement is both pattern-conforming and independently shown necessary, feasible and authorized; validity is supported by those separate witnesses.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.NEGATIVE_WITNESS_OR_COUNTEREXAMPLE: “When an order is placed, the system shall deliver the physical parcel anywhere within one millisecond” conforms to a pattern but is infeasible in the stated world.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.NON_TRIGGER_EXAMPLE: An editor flags a missing unit without asserting any external validity.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.OBSERVABILITY_AND_MISSINGNESS: Text-rule outputs compared with domain, feasibility and authority evidence. Missing evidence remains UNKNOWN unless an explicit contradicted claim is being tested.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.CURRENTNESS_AND_INVALIDATION: Changing the domain, population or mandate invalidates validity even if the lint score remains identical.

CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Proxy validation is circular when templates are scored against the same conventions they encode.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.KNOWN_FAILURES_AND_MISUSES: “When an order is placed, the system shall deliver the physical parcel anywhere within one millisecond” conforms to a pattern but is infeasible in the stated world.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESPONSE_OR_DESCENDANT_FORM: Evaluate each rule against actual downstream tasks and retain unmeasured validity dimensions.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.WHAT_CHANGED_AND_WHAT_DID_NOT: Retain issue detection; reject universal quality score or lint-as-validity substitution.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESIDUAL_LIMITS: Some language defects do harm particular tasks, but effect sizes and weights are context-dependent.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.CEREMONY_VERSUS_MECHANISM: A perfect score may signify obedience to a style guide without a defensible requirement.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RETENTION_RATIONALE: Retain the rejection in the denominator, not an adoption candidate. Evaluate each rule against actual downstream tasks and retain unmeasured validity dimensions.

SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: Single small high-level safety domain; specialist interpretation co-intervention and subjective ratings; no universal applicability

SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_SUPPORTED: Five templates, 249 originals/1764 phrasings; heuristic wording effects; user experiment 43 mostly students judged unreliable by authors
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Template comparison and explicit exclusion of necessary/feasible criteria; shared-data extension supplies a scope limit, not replication of the analytical negative property.
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: Contextual project outcomes unmeasured; researchers rephrase/rate without independent initial annotations; 2023 predecessor shares data

SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Adjacent controlled conceptual replication showing task-specific wording effects; not proof that every lint-clean requirement is invalid or validation of the full predicate.

SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Intrinsic-only generated-requirements evaluation; explicit exclusion of need/feasibility/context completeness bounds inference from judge scores.

CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_CHALLENGED: No smell or a high LLM-judge score means the requirement is correct and authorized.
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.QUALIFICATION: Contextual project outcomes unmeasured; researchers rephrase/rate without independent initial annotations; 2023 predecessor shares data
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Template-benchmark outcome scope, shared-data dependence and contextual exclusions; not a full external-validity test.

CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_CHALLENGED: No smell or a high LLM-judge score means the requirement is correct and authorized.
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.QUALIFICATION: 25 participants/four single-sentence tasks; limited interaction power; context self-reports unvalidated; not a universal lint-weight derivation
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Adjacent consumer-task experiment shows differentiated wording effects, not a sufficient score-to-authority mapping.

CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_CHALLENGED: No smell or a high LLM-judge score means the requirement is correct and authorized.
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.QUALIFICATION: Qwen QwQ-32B judge plus 50-item five-rater check; necessity, feasibility and domain completeness explicitly outside evaluation
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: Explicit intrinsic-only outcome scope and judge/human-check limits; not evidence of authorized or necessary features.

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.SUPPORT: Overclaim contrasted with EARS2009 limitations, QUS2016 and2024–26 evaluation scope
HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.LIMITS: Origin means inspected antecedent, not an assertion of absolute first invention

FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.SUPPORT: Named language definitions and explicit counterexamples where applicable; no general effectiveness theorem
FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.LIMITS: The four-valued rule is an operational reconstruction; authority and world correspondence are not logically supplied by syntax

EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.ASSESSMENT: S018/S019 concern selected wording effects, S027 passive voice/pronouns in domain modeling, S029 intrinsic quality of 900 generated requirements, and S031 story-defect detection. These are separately scoped component outcomes; none compares the complete text-compliance-to-external-validity implication.
EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.LIMITS: Their limits and excluded criteria constrain what can be inferred; they are not five independent replications of the negative property. The universal sufficiency rejection uses the constructed counterexample, not a fabricated causal experiment.

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.ASSESSMENT: Großer extends earlier template comparisons using shared rephrasing data; QUS/AQUSA’s journal work extends its conference precursor; Frattini newly conceptually replicates a passive-voice/domain-modeling effect. Their examined outcomes concern textual characteristics, detection and one consumer task, not replication of the universal textual-compliance-to-validity implication or this record’s counterexample predicate.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: Introduction (extension of the 2023 conference predecessor, reference [18]); §§5.1.1–5.1.4, 8.1–8.3, 9; source-table RETRACTION_CORRECTION_OR_VERSION_NOTES.
§§1–3, 5.1–5.2; source-table RETRACTION_CORRECTION_OR_VERSION_NOTES (2015 conference precursor/2016 extension dependence).
Introduction (conceptual replication of Femmer et al. 2014); §§3.4, 5.1–5.4, 6; source-table RETRACTION_CORRECTION_OR_VERSION_NOTES.

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.LIMITS: The two extensions are not independent evidence units; Frattini’s fresh data do not turn an adjacent linguistic subclaim into validation of complete stakeholder, authority or feasibility validity. Rejection of the stated sufficiency claim remains analytical, not a pooled empirical result.

INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.SUPPORT: Qualitative practitioner cases or source-document rewrite; distinctions in source records apply
INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.LIMITS: Reported practices and perceptions are not randomized process benefits or universal prevalence

NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.SUPPORT: Proxy validation is circular when templates are scored against the same conventions they encode.
NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.LIMITS: A paper’s open problem is not an observed failure; the constructed cases are not incident reports

STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.SUPPORT: No external standard mandate asserted in this research sublane
STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.LIMITS: Language conventions and an author’s chosen criterion do not grant normative authority; cited ISO editions not independently adopted

PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Text-rule outputs compared with domain, feasibility and authority evidence.
PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: A tool’s existence/performance on selected examples does not establish organizational success

TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.SUPPORT: A concise requirement is both pattern-conforming and independently shown necessary, feasible and authorized; validity is supported by those separate witnesses.
TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.LIMITS: Constructed examples expose distinctions; they are not evidence of implementation effectiveness in a target repository

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Some language defects do harm particular tasks, but effect sizes and weights are context-dependent.
CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: Contrary findings narrow claims; they do not justify symmetric overgeneralization

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.SUPPORT: A valid implication would need an established mapping from all relevant textual features to external need/feasibility/authority; no such mapping follows.
ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.LIMITS: Changing the domain, population or mandate invalidates validity even if the lint score remains identical.

DOMAIN_VALIDITY.ASSESSMENT: The conforming but physically infeasible parcel-delivery example refutes the proposed universal implication from textual compliance to real validity. EARS’s omission limit and the benchmark’s exclusion of necessity/feasibility identify the same boundary in the source-defined evaluation scopes.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.LIMITS: The parcel example is constructed, not an incident. Source exclusions establish what was not tested; they do not show that every template-compliant statement is invalid.

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.ASSESSMENT: QUS treats a user story as text plus conversation and acceptance criteria; the issue-title generation study evaluates intrinsic wording. Those scopes supply no route from clean syntax alone to complete coverage of real stakeholder needs.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.LIMITS: No stakeholder-completeness experiment for the full sufficiency claim was examined. The analytical rejection of the conjunction does not estimate how often wording tools miss a constituency.

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.ASSESSMENT: The challenged rule contains no mandate or authorized decision premise: it supplies only textual conformity. EARS syntax conventions and the benchmark’s chosen criteria therefore cannot by themselves establish the issuer’s right to create an obligation.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.LIMITS: This is a premise/conclusion boundary for the stated rule, not an assessment of actual legal or contractual authority. Any external authority rule would need to be added and assessed separately.

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.ASSESSMENT: The proposed TextConforms-to-ValidForNeed mapping is defeated by a conforming statement whose required behavior is infeasible in the stated world. The sources evaluate bounded linguistic characteristics rather than a semantics-preserving map from wording to external need.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.LIMITS: The exact counterexample and four-valued challenge are researcher constructions. This does not refute separately verified transformations within an explicitly constrained formal language.

REALIZABILITY.ASSESSMENT: The record’s delivery-within-one-millisecond construction preserves the template while violating the stipulated physical feasibility constraint. The template benchmark explicitly does not assess feasibility outside project context.
REALIZABILITY.LIMITS: The construction rejects universal syntactic sufficiency; it does not establish the realizability status of any actual project requirement or an empirical failure frequency.

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.ASSESSMENT: The template study measures selected textual characteristics, QUS measures story-quality detection, and the issue-title study evaluates generated wording. None of those inspected outcomes establishes a semantically correct source-to-need or implementation-to-acceptance trace merely because text is clean.
TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.LIMITS: A reference in the text or a metric called traceable must not be promoted into verified semantic correspondence. No accuracy estimate for the full external-validity relation is inferred.

ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.ASSESSMENT: The candidate gate substitutes a linguistic proxy for need, feasibility, completeness and stakeholder validity. Its counterexample demonstrates that passing the proxy can coexist with failure of an external criterion, while the source studies deliberately assess narrower outcomes.
ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: A case may still be valid if separately corroborated. The negative result rejects syntax as sufficient acceptance evidence, not the utility of syntax checks within a larger review.

EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.ASSESSMENT: EARS/Großer evaluate selected wording effects; QUS evaluates story-defect detection; Paiva evaluates intrinsic quality of generated statements. Frattini finds different downstream effects of passive voice and ambiguous pronouns. These preserve useful local effects while bounding the rejected universal claim.
EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.LIMITS: No inspected experiment validates text compliance as sufficient for complete external validity. The analytical counterexample supplies the rejection; these studies do not estimate the benefit of the replacement review procedure.

DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.ASSESSMENT: The stipulated counterexample shows that a proxy-only approval rule can accept an infeasible obligation. Frattini’s differential task effects and the benchmark’s excluded contextual criteria further show why one undifferentiated linguistic score is an insufficient decision basis.
DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.LIMITS: This rejects the stated universal implication, not every limited lint gate. A narrow convention-only gate can be appropriate when it makes no external-validity inference; replacement-policy effectiveness remains unmeasured.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.EVIDENCE_CEILING: EARS expressly cannot establish eliminated omissions; comparative templates exclude necessity/feasibility; current LLM study deliberately scores intrinsic criteria only. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.TRANSFERABILITY_LIMITS: Counterexample rejects universal sufficiency; no rejection of useful writing aids. Some language defects do harm particular tasks, but effect sizes and weights are context-dependent.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.UNVERIFIED_OR_OPEN_QUESTIONS: A controlled downstream-task study can justify a particular rule, not the entire validity implication.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: A controlled downstream-task study can justify a particular rule, not the entire validity implication.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: The reviewers inspected the complete claim/disposition population and selected detailed semantics/source bodies. Absence of an individual finding does not establish independent validation of every field, source or proposed predicate.

INTAKE.CROSSWALK_ELIGIBILITY_WITH_REASON: NOT_A_GENERAL_ADOPTION_CANDIDATE: rejected/ceremonial sufficiency claim; use as an overclaim discriminator
TARGET_NEUTRAL_AUDIT_QUESTIONS: Which validity claims have evidence beyond the text-quality instrument?
Does a simpler existing mechanism already answer the same consumer question?
Which assumption, scope or authority change would require re-entry?
PROHIBITED_OVERCLAIMS: No smell or a high LLM-judge score means the requirement is correct and authorized.
No finding about any target repository or semantic owner is supplied.

SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.OUTPUT: Candidate sufficiency claim: a template-conforming or lint-clean requirement is therefore necessary, feasible, complete and valid for its stakeholders.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.CONSUMER: Reviewer tempted to approve a requirement from a dashboard or quality score.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.BOUNDARY: Counterexample rejects universal sufficiency; no rejection of useful writing aids.

VALIDATION_ACCEPTANCE_PROFILE.APPLICATION: Target-neutral schema applied to the property; worked cases are explicitly analytical
VALIDATION_ACCEPTANCE_PROFILE.CLAIM: Candidate sufficiency claim: a template-conforming or lint-clean requirement is therefore necessary, feasible, complete and valid for its stakeholders.
VALIDATION_ACCEPTANCE_PROFILE.CRITERION: For TextConforms ⇒ ValidForNeed, a conforming invented or infeasible requirement is a counterexample and FAIL. Case-specific corroborated validity can PASS only that case; absent world/authority evidence is UNKNOWN. Mere syntax review with no validity inference is INAPPLICABLE.
VALIDATION_ACCEPTANCE_PROFILE.SUBJECT_CONFIGURATION: A requirement statement plus a proposed validity decision
VALIDATION_ACCEPTANCE_PROFILE.METHOD: The rejected inference replaces external evidence with a textual proxy.
VALIDATION_ACCEPTANCE_PROFILE.EVALUATOR: Named competent reviewer for the criterion; independence and shared priors disclosed
VALIDATION_ACCEPTANCE_PROFILE.OBSERVER: Person/tool that actually observes the relevant behavior or task result
VALIDATION_ACCEPTANCE_PROFILE.ENVIRONMENT: Counterexample rejects universal sufficiency; no rejection of useful writing aids.
VALIDATION_ACCEPTANCE_PROFILE.NEGATIVE_CONTROLS: “When an order is placed, the system shall deliver the physical parcel anywhere within one millisecond” conforms to a pattern but is infeasible in the stated world.
VALIDATION_ACCEPTANCE_PROFILE.EVIDENCE: Text-rule outputs compared with domain, feasibility and authority evidence.
VALIDATION_ACCEPTANCE_PROFILE.RECEIVING_AUTHORITY: Textual syntax does not confer stakeholder mandate.
VALIDATION_ACCEPTANCE_PROFILE.REMAINING_LIMITS: Some language defects do harm particular tasks, but effect sizes and weights are context-dependent.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Maintain the minimum trace relations needed by named decisions, with type, meaning, provenance, versions/context and a revalidation/impact rule.

EVALUATION_MODE.DEFINITION: Mode describes how evidence is assessed, separate from the commissioned predicate-role enum. A sufficiency challenge tests an asserted implication or universal process benefit; ordinary operational assessment evaluates the bounded source-informed rule. Mechanical record checks do not settle semantic, empirical or authority judgments.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: Assess(subject: A trace link and the decision that consumes it, context, consumerDecision, evidenceSnapshot, validTime) -> PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|INAPPLICABLE

VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.CONSTRAINT: Empty consumer means burden needs justification

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Universal only over explicitly enumerated material items needed for the declared decision and search scope. No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A trace link and the decision that consumes it
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Assessed at the named evidence/configuration snapshot. Hypothesized, desired, agreed and observed states remain distinct. Later changes require the stated invalidation procedure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Link meaning can be evaluated; version/context identities and responsible sources remain accessible.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: Future change/acceptance questions cannot reliably be answered from immediate shared context.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: A relied-on trace passes only if its typed relation has a semantic witness at the specified versions/context and can answer its declared consumer query. Known stale/spurious relation FAILS; missing review after material change is UNKNOWN. Connectivity or matching IDs is never the witness.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.LIMIT: Not a verbatim source theorem, source standard requirement or empirically validated universal acceptance algorithm

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Link record, query result, version/context differences, rationale and reviewer/source confirmation.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Source and target identity/version; relation type; rationale/witness; maintainer; applicable context; last semantic review.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: An informed evaluator checks applicability, identifies the exact claim and scope, reviews the named witnesses, tests the supplied counterexample class and records a reasoned four-valued outcome. Mechanical schema checks can establish presence/identity, not domain truth or authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite record checks are mechanically decidable. Semantic correspondence, legitimate representation, proxy validity and causal transfer generally require contextual judgment and may remain UNKNOWN. No claim of general decidability.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.TEXT: A changed notification timing assumption marks linked requirement, test oracle and acceptance decision for review even though their IDs remain unchanged.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.TEXT: The requirement now covers all customers but the linked test still samples only active accounts; a complete matrix falsely reports coverage.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: A one-off personal text correction is fully evidenced by the request and direct resulting diff.

FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_POSITIVE: A filled matrix, stable identifier or large number of edges is not the mechanism.
FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_NEGATIVE: Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. A filled matrix, stable identifier or large number of edges is not the mechanism.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Changed source meaning, actor authority, environment, target behavior or consumer query invalidates relevant relation assurance.

The operational rule is a proposed audit discriminator, not a measured process-effect claim.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE: Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

Known stale/spurious relation FAILS; missing review after material change is UNKNOWN. Connectivity or matching IDs is never the witness.

OUTCOMES.PASS: Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.SUPPORT: S024 reproduces and compares published requirement-to-code recovery methods; S023/S030 provide additional practitioner reports relevant to tracing burdens. These are bounded support for narrower subclaims, not a replication of the complete consumer-directed typed/currentness mechanism.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.LIMITS: No direct validation of the synthesized predicate is established in this inspected set. Reused public benchmark artifacts/labels and overlapping survey/interview participants must not be counted as independent validations; no wider absence-of-replication claim is made.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.ORIGINAL_OR_REPLICATED_CLAIM: S024 tests published recovery-method performance against stronger comparators; the property additionally requires consumer purpose, semantic type and version/currentness, which that reproduction does not test.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.POPULATION_TASK_AND_OUTCOME: S024: six methods, 13 Java datasets, labeled requirement-to-code recovery and precision/recall/F1. S023: 55 survey respondents and 14 interviewees, eight overlapping; S030: 20 practitioners, documentation/update reports.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.DEPENDENCE: S024 reuses public benchmark assets; independence from every original method dataset is not established. S023 has 61 distinct participants, not 69. S025 is a different prompt-framework study, not a replication of the full tracing policy.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.TRANSFER_TO_RETAINED_PROPERTY: Corroborates practical need for useful maintained traces and bounded candidate-recovery evaluation. It does not establish causal maintenance return or validate each synthesized trace type.

INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.SUPPORT: Qualitative practitioner cases or source-document rewrite; distinctions in source records apply
INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.LIMITS: Reported practices and perceptions are not randomized process benefits or universal prevalence

NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.SUPPORT: Maintaining every conceivable relation is costly, fragile and politically disconnected from users’ actual needs.
NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.LIMITS: A paper’s open problem is not an observed failure; the constructed cases are not incident reports

STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.SUPPORT: No external standard mandate asserted in this research sublane
STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.LIMITS: Language conventions and an author’s chosen criterion do not grant normative authority; cited ISO editions not independently adopted

PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Link record, query result, version/context differences, rationale and reviewer/source confirmation.
PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: A tool’s existence/performance on selected examples does not establish organizational success

TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.SUPPORT: A changed notification timing assumption marks linked requirement, test oracle and acceptance decision for review even though their IDs remain unchanged.
TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.LIMITS: Constructed examples expose distinctions; they are not evidence of implementation effectiveness in a target repository

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Unrecorded tacit knowledge and inaccessible people can still defeat retrieval; unknown future queries cannot all be anticipated.
CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: Contrary findings narrow claims; they do not justify symmetric overgeneralization

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.SUPPORT: Link meaning can be evaluated; version/context identities and responsible sources remain accessible.
ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.LIMITS: Changed source meaning, actor authority, environment, target behavior or consumer query invalidates relevant relation assurance.

DOMAIN_VALIDITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Trace consumers, source participation and requirement/test maintenance in the inspected practitioner studies.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.SUPPORT: Gotel/Finkelstein, the 2023 barriers study and the 2016 documentation interviews identify context-dependent rationale and change questions that a trace should answer. They support consumer-directed tracing as a response to observed practical problems.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.LIMITS: They do not validate every semantic link type or demonstrate that the synthesized minimum-link/currentness rule matches every domain; the operational rule remains an analytical reconstruction.

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Who supplies, maintains and consumes trace information.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.SUPPORT: The sources distinguish providers from beneficiaries; S023 uses 55 survey responses and 14 interviews with eight people in both, and S030 covers 20 practitioners in 17 business units. This supports attention to unequal costs and inaccessible source people.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.LIMITS: These purposive/convenience and self-report samples are not a census of affected stakeholders or evidence that all consumer needs are represented.

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Legitimate authority inherited through a typed source/target relation.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.SUPPORT: The inspected traceability studies address information needs and practice, not legal or organizational authorization of a linked requirement. The property deliberately requires an independently warranted source/remit path.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.LIMITS: No normative instrument or authority-preservation evaluation is established for this mechanism; a correct trace cannot itself authorize the endpoint.

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Whether a traceability relation supplies a formal refinement proof.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.SUPPORT: This property maintains and queries typed relations; it does not define a goal-refinement calculus. The Viewpoints source supplies inter-viewpoint coordination concepts, not a theorem for every refines link.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.LIMITS: A link labeled refines requires its own semantic warrant; this assessment supplies no entailment or preservation result.

LOCATORS.LOCATOR: §§2–5 and 7; viewpoint slots and inter-viewpoint rules

REALIZABILITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Whether current trace links establish that a required system can be built or operated.
REALIZABILITY.SUPPORT: The claim concerns access to rationale and impact information, not existence of an implementation satisfying requirements. Practitioner use demonstrates that tracing activities can occur, not system realizability.
REALIZABILITY.LIMITS: Neither an accurate matrix nor a responsible source contact establishes capability or environment assumptions.

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Semantic trace meaning, staleness and recovery against labeled links.
TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.SUPPORT: S021/S023 motivate checking meaningful and maintained relations. S024 compares recovery methods on 13 datasets; S025 evaluates prompted candidates against benchmark labels. These support bounded retrieval assessments, not automatic truth.
TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.LIMITS: Benchmark precision/recall does not validate the synthesized typed, versioned and consumer-specific trace rule or its semantic currentness after change.

ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Connections between requirement documentation, tests and the decision using them.
ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.SUPPORT: S030 reports updating and technical-role involvement problems; S021 explains why source and consumer context matter. These support checking whether a test/accepts relation actually addresses the current requirement.
ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: The studies do not validate authorized acceptance or downstream need fulfillment from a link alone; no complete acceptance-correspondence treatment was tested.

EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Practice burdens and recovery performance, distinguished from maintenance return.
EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.SUPPORT: The field studies report usefulness and maintenance barriers; S024/S025 supply bounded algorithm comparisons. Neither evidence class measures the net lifecycle effect of this combined consumer-directed currentness discipline.
EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.LIMITS: Self-reported benefit and benchmark performance are not measured causal maintenance benefit; abstract-only maintenance results are not promoted here.

DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Selecting useful links by consumer query, effort and change consequences.
DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.SUPPORT: The provider/consumer distinction and reported cost distribution support making the decision and cost rationale explicit instead of maximizing link count.
DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.LIMITS: No calibrated model establishes the optimal minimum relation set, future query coverage or total return; the proposed rule requires contextual judgment.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Historical practitioner investigation and2023/2016 field reports identify practical needs and burdens; controlled maintenance benefits are abstract-only here, not promoted. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.TRANSFERABILITY_LIMITS: A link is relative to its semantic type, granularity and current context; unchanged source text may support a changed meaning poorly. Unrecorded tacit knowledge and inaccessible people can still defeat retrieval; unknown future queries cannot all be anticipated.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.UNVERIFIED_OR_OPEN_QUESTIONS: Test representative change questions against the maintained links and compare result quality plus maintenance effort with a cheaper method.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: Test representative change questions against the maintained links and compare result quality plus maintenance effort with a cheaper method.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: The reviewers inspected the complete claim/disposition population and selected detailed semantics/source bodies. Absence of an individual finding does not establish independent validation of every field, source or proposed predicate.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Candidate universal claim: collecting and maintaining every possible trace link improves decisions enough to justify its cost.

EVALUATION_MODE.DEFINITION: Mode describes how evidence is assessed, separate from the commissioned predicate-role enum. A sufficiency challenge tests an asserted implication or universal process benefit; ordinary operational assessment evaluates the bounded source-informed rule. Mechanical record checks do not settle semantic, empirical or authority judgments.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: Assess(subject: A traceability policy and the decisions it is meant to improve, context, consumerDecision, evidenceSnapshot, validTime) -> PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|INAPPLICABLE

VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.CONSTRAINT: Unknown value is not assumed positive or zero
Unit/window and who bears it explicit

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Universal only over explicitly enumerated material items needed for the declared decision and search scope. No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A traceability policy and the decisions it is meant to improve
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Assessed at the named evidence/configuration snapshot. Hypothesized, desired, agreed and observed states remain distinct. Later changes require the stated invalidation procedure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Universal benefit would require all additional links to improve decisions more than their creation, maintenance and false-alarm costs.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A proposed tracing mandate adds relations without a named material consumer or a cost/value rationale.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: For a policy increment, inspect actual consumer questions and effort. A documented positive net contribution can support bounded PASS; a material cost with no useful decision change is a counterexample to universal benefit and FAIL. Unmeasured payoff/cost is UNKNOWN; independently mandated links are evaluated for compliance, not this universal claim.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.LIMIT: Not a verbatim source theorem, source standard requirement or empirically validated universal acceptance algorithm

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Decision logs/query trials, effort records, link error/staleness and mandate scope.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Policy source, required relation set, consuming queries, predicted benefits, observed effort and false/stale-link burden.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: An informed evaluator checks applicability, identifies the exact claim and scope, reviews the named witnesses, tests the supplied counterexample class and records a reasoned four-valued outcome. Mechanical schema checks can establish presence/identity, not domain truth or authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite record checks are mechanically decidable. Semantic correspondence, legitimate representation, proxy validity and causal transfer generally require contextual judgment and may remain UNKNOWN. No claim of general decidability.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.TEXT: A new high-risk interface has a named impact-analysis consumer and observed retrieval savings that justify a small required relation set.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.TEXT: A short-lived two-person task adds hundreds of cross-product links, none consumed before retirement, while review time delays the only requested fix.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: A small mandatory relation set has a specific binding source and a defined consumer; universal maximal tracing is not asserted.

FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_POSITIVE: Link-count quotas and matrix completion can reward administrative conformity over useful explanations.
FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_NEGATIVE: Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. Link-count quotas and matrix completion can reward administrative conformity over useful explanations.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: New consumers, retention duties, change rates or costs may change the policy decision.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Combinatorial candidate links, review, tool administration and notification noise. Alternative: One source note and direct contact in a small short-lived team can answer the actual queries.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Historical and2023 practice identify heterogeneous needs, costs, work/benefit imbalance and suitable use of existing tools; no universal exhaustive-policy outcome study. The operational rule is a proposed audit discriminator, not a measured process-effect claim.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE: Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.RULE: For a policy increment, inspect actual consumer questions and effort. A documented positive net contribution can support bounded PASS; a material cost with no useful decision change is a counterexample to universal benefit and FAIL. Unmeasured payoff/cost is UNKNOWN; independently mandated links are evaluated for compliance, not this universal claim.

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.SUPPORT: Overclaim challenged by1994 provider/consumer conflicts and2023 practice
HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.LIMITS: Origin means inspected antecedent, not an assertion of absolute first invention

FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.SUPPORT: Named language definitions and explicit counterexamples where applicable; no general effectiveness theorem
FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.LIMITS: The four-valued rule is an operational reconstruction; authority and world correspondence are not logically supplied by syntax

EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.SUPPORT: No comparative net-outcome test of the exact exhaustive collection policy is established in S021/S023/S030. Those sources provide descriptive evidence about heterogeneous trace needs, costs and maintenance difficulties.
EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.LIMITS: This statement is bounded to the linked inspected sources, not a claim that no such study exists; descriptive objections and the analytical counterexample are not measured treatment effects.

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.SUPPORT: No direct replication or external test of the universally exhaustive link-collection policy is established by the linked inspected sources. S021, S023 and S030 instead supply descriptive evidence of heterogeneous needs, costs and maintenance problems.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.LIMITS: This bounded source check is not an exhaustive absence claim. A constructed unconsumed-link counterexample is logical/analytical evidence, not a replicated field result.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.ORIGINAL_OR_REPLICATED_CLAIM: The rejected claim is that every added possible trace necessarily improves decisions enough to offset its cost. None of these sources reports an original-and-replicated treatment test of that exact policy.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.POPULATION_TASK_AND_OUTCOME: Historical practitioner investigation; S023 survey/interviews with 61 distinct participants; S030 interviews with 20 practitioners across 17 business units. Outcomes are reported needs/burdens rather than comparative net effects of exhaustive tracing.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.DEPENDENCE: The 1993/1994 Gotel/Finkelstein versions are one line of work; S023 survey/interview overlap is disclosed. Similar themes across reports do not create replicated policy-effect estimates.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.TRANSFER_TO_RETAINED_PROPERTY: Supports the relevance of cost/consumer qualifications and preserves the rejection of universality; does not prove all extensive tracing harmful.

INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.SUPPORT: Qualitative practitioner cases or source-document rewrite; distinctions in source records apply
INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.LIMITS: Reported practices and perceptions are not randomized process benefits or universal prevalence

NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.SUPPORT: Potential future usefulness is unfalsifiable without declared queries and an observation horizon.
NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.LIMITS: A paper’s open problem is not an observed failure; the constructed cases are not incident reports

STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.SUPPORT: No external standard mandate asserted in this research sublane
STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.LIMITS: Language conventions and an author’s chosen criterion do not grant normative authority; cited ISO editions not independently adopted

PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Decision logs/query trials, effort records, link error/staleness and mandate scope.
PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: A tool’s existence/performance on selected examples does not establish organizational success

TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.SUPPORT: A new high-risk interface has a named impact-analysis consumer and observed retrieval savings that justify a small required relation set.
TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.LIMITS: Constructed examples expose distinctions; they are not evidence of implementation effectiveness in a target repository

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Some future information needs are unknowable; minimalism also needs explicit risk judgment.
CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: Contrary findings narrow claims; they do not justify symmetric overgeneralization

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.SUPPORT: Universal benefit would require all additional links to improve decisions more than their creation, maintenance and false-alarm costs.
ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.LIMITS: New consumers, retention duties, change rates or costs may change the policy decision.

DOMAIN_VALIDITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: The universal claim that collecting every possible trace link necessarily pays off.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.SUPPORT: Inspected practice studies report heterogeneous trace needs, maintenance burden and small-team shortcuts. They undermine a context-free benefit assumption and motivate the explicit analytical counterexample.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.LIMITS: The constructed costly-unconsumed-link case is not an observed incident or a measured prevalence claim; no universal magnitude of harm is inferred.

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Distribution of tracing work and benefits among participants.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.SUPPORT: S021 and S023 distinguish people who create information from consumers who gain from it; S030 reports documentation needs across technical roles. This is relevant to costs hidden by an organization-level link quota.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.LIMITS: Convenience/purposive practitioner evidence does not enumerate every affected party or settle whose benefit should take priority.

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: An empirical universality claim versus a valid tracing obligation.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.SUPPORT: Rejecting universal process benefit does not discharge a contract, safety or other authorized requirement to retain specified traces. This record makes no normative mandate claim.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.LIMITS: No particular applicable tracing instrument was assessed; independently required links need their own source and scope assessment.

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Whether exhaustive link collection proves a valid refinement.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.SUPPORT: The candidate concerns administrative collection and net decision value, not a formal transformation relation. Link quantity provides no refinement entailment.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.LIMITS: Rejecting the universal policy does not establish correctness of any replacement refinement or minimal trace set.

REALIZABILITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Whether an exhaustive tracing policy establishes implementation feasibility.
REALIZABILITY.SUPPORT: The retained result rejects a universal process-value claim; it neither constructs a system nor proves a requirements set realizable.
REALIZABILITY.LIMITS: Reducing trace burden can save effort but does not establish that any technical obligation is achievable.

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Stale, unconsumed or semantically inadequate links as costs of the universal policy.
TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.SUPPORT: S021/S023 identify maintenance and source-access problems; the proposed counterexample separates a filled matrix from a useful answer.
TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.LIMITS: The sources do not measure accuracy of every possible link or prove that fewer links are always more accurate; link correctness and policy value remain separate.

ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Whether exhaustive linkage establishes current requirement/test correspondence.
ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.SUPPORT: S030 describes documentation/update problems that a link count alone cannot resolve. The negative policy claim preserves the need to check the particular acceptance question.
ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: This is an inference boundary, not an empirical demonstration that a specified acceptance workflow or minimal policy succeeds.

EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Comparative net outcomes for the exact universally exhaustive collection policy in the linked inspected sources.
EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.SUPPORT: No such treatment comparison is established in S021/S023/S030. Their descriptive reports of effort, conflicting needs and shortcuts supply bounded reasons to doubt universality, not a measured treatment effect.
EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.LIMITS: The assessment is limited to these inspected sources; it is not a claim that no exhaustive-policy experiment exists. The constructed counterexample is explicitly analytical.

DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Incremental decision value relative to creation, maintenance and false-alarm costs.
DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.SUPPORT: A material added cost with no decision contribution defeats the asserted necessity of positive net benefit under the stated criterion. Practitioner accounts show why consumer and cost distinctions matter.
DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.LIMITS: The counterexample does not establish optimal tracing effort or a universal cost threshold; future unknown queries and independent obligations can justify retention.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Historical and2023 practice identify heterogeneous needs, costs, work/benefit imbalance and suitable use of existing tools; no universal exhaustive-policy outcome study. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.TRANSFERABILITY_LIMITS: Rejects universality, not a justified safety/contract-specific required set of links. Some future information needs are unknowable; minimalism also needs explicit risk judgment.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.UNVERIFIED_OR_OPEN_QUESTIONS: Run a bounded query/value comparison and identify which link classes actually change decisions.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: Run a bounded query/value comparison and identify which link classes actually change decisions.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: The reviewers inspected the complete claim/disposition population and selected detailed semantics/source bodies. Absence of an individual finding does not establish independent validation of every field, source or proposed predicate.

INTAKE.CROSSWALK_ELIGIBILITY_WITH_REASON: NOT_A_GENERAL_ADOPTION_CANDIDATE: rejected/ceremonial sufficiency claim; use as an overclaim discriminator
TARGET_NEUTRAL_AUDIT_QUESTIONS: What decision would be worse if this additional relation class were absent?
Does a simpler existing mechanism already answer the same consumer question?
Which assumption, scope or authority change would require re-entry?
PROHIBITED_OVERCLAIMS: More trace links always mean better assurance or lower total cost.
No finding about any target repository or semantic owner is supplied.

SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.INPUT: Policy source, required relation set, consuming queries, predicted benefits, observed effort and false/stale-link burden.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.OUTPUT: Candidate universal claim: collecting and maintaining every possible trace link improves decisions enough to justify its cost.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.CONSUMER: Manager specifying tracing obligations and people paying/benefiting from them.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.BOUNDARY: Rejects universality, not a justified safety/contract-specific required set of links.

TRACEABILITY_CHANGE_PROFILE.APPLICATION: Target-neutral schema applied to the property; worked cases are explicitly analytical
TRACEABILITY_CHANGE_PROFILE.RELATION_TYPES: Derives-from, refines, implements, tests, accepts, supersedes, and explicitly defined local relations; do not collapse into related-to
TRACEABILITY_CHANGE_PROFILE.SOURCE_TARGET_IDENTITIES: Bind object identity and version/context independently of display text or shared identifier
TRACEABILITY_CHANGE_PROFILE.MEANING: Candidate universal claim: collecting and maintaining every possible trace link improves decisions enough to justify its cost.
TRACEABILITY_CHANGE_PROFILE.EVIDENCE: Decision logs/query trials, effort records, link error/staleness and mandate scope.
TRACEABILITY_CHANGE_PROFILE.VERSION_CONTEXT: Rejects universality, not a justified safety/contract-specific required set of links.
TRACEABILITY_CHANGE_PROFILE.DEPENDENCY_PROPAGATION: New consumers, retention duties, change rates or costs may change the policy decision.
TRACEABILITY_CHANGE_PROFILE.REUSE_CONDITIONS: Universal benefit would require all additional links to improve decisions more than their creation, maintenance and false-alarm costs.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: State the exact claim and criterion, configuration/environment, evaluator/observer and receiving authority; maintain separate evidence statuses for conformance, need correspondence, real-world outcome and acceptance.

EVALUATION_MODE.DEFINITION: Mode describes how evidence is assessed, separate from the commissioned predicate-role enum. A sufficiency challenge tests an asserted implication or universal process benefit; ordinary operational assessment evaluates the bounded source-informed rule. Mechanical record checks do not settle semantic, empirical or authority judgments.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: Assess(subject: An acceptance/satisfaction claim for a named requirement and delivered configuration, context, consumerDecision, evidenceSnapshot, validTime) -> PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|INAPPLICABLE

VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.CONSTRAINT: Exact versions, scope, time and exclusions

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Universal only over explicitly enumerated material items needed for the declared decision and search scope. No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: An acceptance/satisfaction claim for a named requirement and delivered configuration
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Assessed at the named evidence/configuration snapshot. Hypothesized, desired, agreed and observed states remain distinct. Later changes require the stated invalidation procedure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: The intended need and receiving remit can be identified; evidence is tied to the actual configuration/environment.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: An implementation test, review or approval is used to claim broader satisfaction.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Evaluate each required dimension separately as PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN/INAPPLICABLE. The consuming decision may PASS only under its declared rule over those statuses and current authority; an observed contradiction FAILS the affected dimension. A passed local test cannot fill UNKNOWN external-outcome or representation cells.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.LIMIT: Not a verbatim source theorem, source standard requirement or empirically validated universal acceptance algorithm

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Test traces, observed outcomes, criterion mapping, negative-case checks and scoped acceptance decision.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Criterion source, subject/configuration, environment, observation method, negative controls, evidence identity/date, evaluator and receiving authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: An informed evaluator checks applicability, identifies the exact claim and scope, reviews the named witnesses, tests the supplied counterexample class and records a reasoned four-valued outcome. Mechanical schema checks can establish presence/identity, not domain truth or authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite record checks are mechanically decidable. Semantic correspondence, legitimate representation, proxy validity and causal transfer generally require contextual judgment and may remain UNKNOWN. No claim of general decidability.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.TEXT: A delivery service verifies message enqueueing, then separately observes recipient receipt in the relevant channel; the receiving owner accepts only the supported service scope.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.TEXT: The application reports email queued and all unit tests pass, but the downstream provider rejects the address and no user is notified; external notification remains failed.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: A private static-format output with one receiving user and no external dependency is settled by direct content inspection.

FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_POSITIVE: A green test suite and signed checklist are indexes to evidence, not substitutes for it.
FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_NEGATIVE: Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. A green test suite and signed checklist are indexes to evidence, not substitutes for it.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Changed build, data population, external service, criterion or receiving remit reopens the corresponding evidence dimension.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Independent observations only when they resolve a material remaining claim; redundant reviews can add burden without changing evidence. Alternative: A user requests a private file with specified content; inspection of that exact file under the agreed criterion may settle the decision.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Field requirement/test-documentation problems and bounded operational cases support the need for distinct links; no claim this combined schema itself has trial-proven effectiveness. The operational rule is a proposed audit discriminator, not a measured process-effect claim.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE: Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.RULE: Evaluate each required dimension separately as PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN/INAPPLICABLE. The consuming decision may PASS only under its declared rule over those statuses and current authority; an observed contradiction FAILS the affected dimension. A passed local test cannot fill UNKNOWN external-outcome or representation cells.

OUTCOMES.PASS: Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation
OUTCOMES.FAIL: An applicable observed contradiction, failed criterion or valid counterexample defeats the specified claim
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Relevant evidence/meaning/authority is missing, disputed or not discriminating
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: An explicit guard excludes the claim; cheap path must be justified

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.EMPTY_SCOPE_RULE: Empty obligation/source sets never establish completeness by vacuity; show scope adequacy or label inapplicable/unknown.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.POSITIVE_WITNESS_OR_WORKED_EXAMPLE: A delivery service verifies message enqueueing, then separately observes recipient receipt in the relevant channel; the receiving owner accepts only the supported service scope.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.NEGATIVE_WITNESS_OR_COUNTEREXAMPLE: The application reports email queued and all unit tests pass, but the downstream provider rejects the address and no user is notified; external notification remains failed.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.NON_TRIGGER_EXAMPLE: A private static-format output with one receiving user and no external dependency is settled by direct content inspection.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.OBSERVABILITY_AND_MISSINGNESS: Test traces, observed outcomes, criterion mapping, negative-case checks and scoped acceptance decision. Missing evidence remains UNKNOWN unless an explicit contradicted claim is being tested.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.CURRENTNESS_AND_INVALIDATION: Changed build, data population, external service, criterion or receiving remit reopens the corresponding evidence dimension.

CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: An elaborate assurance record can become ritual; tests and signatures can be redundant or misunderstand the need.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.KNOWN_FAILURES_AND_MISUSES: The application reports email queued and all unit tests pass, but the downstream provider rejects the address and no user is notified; external notification remains failed.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESPONSE_OR_DESCENDANT_FORM: Require explicit claim correspondence and only decision-changing additional evidence; distinguish unresolved facts from risk acceptance.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.WHAT_CHANGED_AND_WHAT_DID_NOT: Makes dimensions and scope explicit; does not replace field observation or social judgment with formal verification.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESIDUAL_LIMITS: An authorized party can accept residual risk without making an unsupported proposition true; latent outcomes may remain unobserved.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.CEREMONY_VERSUS_MECHANISM: A green test suite and signed checklist are indexes to evidence, not substitutes for it.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RETENTION_RATIONALE: Retain the bounded mechanism with explicit guard, evidence and cheap path. Require explicit claim correspondence and only decision-changing additional evidence; distinguish unresolved facts from risk acceptance.
