ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.VALID_TIME_OR_VERSION: Model/provider changes, source revisions or new affected parties invalidate benchmark transfer or promotion evidence as appropriate.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.CHANGE_IMPACT: Model/provider changes, source revisions or new affected parties invalidate benchmark transfer or promotion evidence as appropriate.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Use LLM output to propose hypotheses and questions; preserve source, additions, model/prompt/version and independent domain/authority review before promotion.

EVALUATION_MODE.DEFINITION: Mode describes how evidence is assessed, separate from the commissioned predicate-role enum. A sufficiency challenge tests an asserted implication or universal process benefit; ordinary operational assessment evaluates the bounded source-informed rule. Mechanical record checks do not settle semantic, empirical or authority judgments.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: Assess(subject: A generated statement and its transition into an accepted requirement, context, consumerDecision, evidenceSnapshot, validTime) -> PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|INAPPLICABLE
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Universal only over explicitly enumerated material items needed for the declared decision and search scope. No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A generated statement and its transition into an accepted requirement
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Assessed at the named evidence/configuration snapshot. Hypothesized, desired, agreed and observed states remain distinct. Later changes require the stated invalidation procedure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Human reviewers have independent source/domain access; model output is not accepted merely because evaluators share its priors.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: Sparse initial descriptions or many candidate formulations, with an available qualified review process.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: A generated statement may be promoted only when its material factual and normative additions have independent source/domain/authority support at the declared scope. Fluent or high-scoring ungrounded content remains UNKNOWN; contradicted or unauthorized additions FAIL. Generation used solely as labeled brainstorming is INAPPLICABLE to promotion.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.LIMIT: Not a verbatim source theorem, source standard requirement or empirically validated universal acceptance algorithm

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Input/output diff, review decisions and source links, not a model’s explanation alone.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Input snapshot, model identifier/access date, prompt/temperature, generated additions, transformation steps, reviewer judgments and decision source.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: An informed evaluator checks applicability, identifies the exact claim and scope, reviews the named witnesses, tests the supplied counterexample class and records a reasoned four-valued outcome. Mechanical schema checks can establish presence/identity, not domain truth or authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite record checks are mechanically decidable. Semantic correspondence, legitimate representation, proxy validity and causal transfer generally require contextual judgment and may remain UNKNOWN. No claim of general decidability.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.TEXT: A draft suggests an offline mode; the analyst labels it a hypothesis, asks affected users, checks feasibility and records the resulting authorized bounded requirement.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.TEXT: Five models agree on automatic penalties, so the team treats penalties as required despite no source or affected-party approval.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: A user has specified an exact one-line change; additional model-generated requirements are unnecessary.

FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_POSITIVE: Multi-agent or multi-LLM agreement is not independent stakeholder evidence.
FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_NEGATIVE: Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. Multi-agent or multi-LLM agreement is not independent stakeholder evidence.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Model/provider changes, source revisions or new affected parties invalidate benchmark transfer or promotion evidence as appropriate.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: API cost, latency and verification of plausible additions; multiple outputs can increase review burden and hallucinated scope. Alternative: A precise authorized request needs no multi-model orchestration to invent additional features.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: 2026 studies measure reference alignment, intrinsic text quality and human perceived utility; one reports iteration trade-offs and disagreement. No stakeholder representation, contractual authorization or deployment outcome is established. The operational rule is a proposed audit discriminator, not a measured process-effect claim.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE: Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.RULE: A generated statement may be promoted only when its material factual and normative additions have independent source/domain/authority support at the declared scope. Fluent or high-scoring ungrounded content remains UNKNOWN; contradicted or unauthorized additions FAIL. Generation used solely as labeled brainstorming is INAPPLICABLE to promotion.

OUTCOMES.PASS: Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation
OUTCOMES.FAIL: An applicable observed contradiction, failed criterion or valid counterexample defeats the specified claim
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Relevant evidence/meaning/authority is missing, disputed or not discriminating
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: An explicit guard excludes the claim; cheap path must be justified

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.EMPTY_SCOPE_RULE: Empty obligation/source sets never establish completeness by vacuity; show scope adequacy or label inapplicable/unknown.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.POSITIVE_WITNESS_OR_WORKED_EXAMPLE: A draft suggests an offline mode; the analyst labels it a hypothesis, asks affected users, checks feasibility and records the resulting authorized bounded requirement.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.NEGATIVE_WITNESS_OR_COUNTEREXAMPLE: Five models agree on automatic penalties, so the team treats penalties as required despite no source or affected-party approval.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.OBSERVABILITY_AND_MISSINGNESS: Input/output diff, review decisions and source links, not a model’s explanation alone. Missing evidence remains UNKNOWN unless an explicit contradicted claim is being tested.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.CURRENTNESS_AND_INVALIDATION: Model/provider changes, source revisions or new affected parties invalidate benchmark transfer or promotion evidence as appropriate.

CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Correlated models and judges can reward plausible hallucination; iterative expansion may reduce precision and add review costs.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.KNOWN_FAILURES_AND_MISUSES: Five models agree on automatic penalties, so the team treats penalties as required despite no source or affected-party approval.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESPONSE_OR_DESCENDANT_FORM: Use models as proposal/search support, measure downstream review value and keep generation distinct from authorization.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.WHAT_CHANGED_AND_WHAT_DID_NOT: Automation changes candidate production; it does not eliminate contextual elicitation, evidence or authority checks.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESIDUAL_LIMITS: Training-data contamination, stochastic variation, evaluator expertise and unseen domain risks remain.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.CEREMONY_VERSUS_MECHANISM: Multi-agent or multi-LLM agreement is not independent stakeholder evidence.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RETENTION_RATIONALE: Retain the bounded mechanism with explicit guard, evidence and cheap path. Use models as proposal/search support, measure downstream review value and keep generation distinct from authorization.

SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_SUPPORTED: Iteration can trade precision for recall and fail to improve F1; human ratings differ; draft plausibility not authority
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: DIRECT_BOUNDED_AI_PIPELINE_EVALUATION for reference alignment, iteration trade-offs and human judgment
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: Four reference SRSs; fresh classroom case; one run/configuration/round; contamination not excluded; students and two professionals; prototype coding assistant confounds effects

SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_SUPPORTED: 150 titles, two models and three prompts produce 900 requirements; assessment restricted to intrinsic wording criteria
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: DIRECT_BOUNDED_AI_WORDING_EVALUATION; excludes necessity, feasibility and completeness
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: Qwen QwQ-32B judge plus 50-item five-rater check; necessity, feasibility and domain completeness explicitly outside evaluation

SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_SUPPORTED: Contextual and tacit knowledge; method-specific blind spots; nonliteral lifecycle categories
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: CONCEPTUAL_ELICITATION_CONTEXT for tacit/domain knowledge; not an AI workflow evaluation
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: No controlled between-method efficacy trial; anthropological examples and rationale cannot establish universal superiority

SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_SUPPORTED: Five templates, 249 originals/1764 phrasings; heuristic wording effects; user experiment 43 mostly students judged unreliable by authors
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.ROLE: ADJACENT_NON_AI_TEMPLATE_QUALITY_LIMIT only; shared-data extension is not AI-assistance replication
SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: Contextual project outcomes unmeasured; researchers rephrase/rate without independent initial annotations; 2023 predecessor shares data

SUPPORTING_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: Three 9–13-sentence teaching problems; one-author injection and correction judgment; five trained beginners for comparison; no industrial or stakeholder-validity result

CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_CHALLENGED: LLM consensus, similarity or intrinsic-quality scores establish complete, necessary and authorized requirements.
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.QUALIFICATION: Four reference SRSs; fresh classroom case; one run/configuration/round; contamination not excluded; students and two professionals; prototype coding assistant confounds effects

CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_CHALLENGED: LLM consensus, similarity or intrinsic-quality scores establish complete, necessary and authorized requirements.
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.QUALIFICATION: Qwen QwQ-32B judge plus 50-item five-rater check; necessity, feasibility and domain completeness explicitly outside evaluation

CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.CLAIM_CHALLENGED: LLM consensus, similarity or intrinsic-quality scores establish complete, necessary and authorized requirements.
CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.QUALIFICATION: Three 9–13-sentence teaching problems; one-author injection and correction judgment; five trained beginners for comparison; no industrial or stakeholder-validity result

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.SUPPORT: 2026 issue-title drafting and multi-LLM elicitation experiments, interpreted against contextual elicitation
HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.LIMITS: Origin means inspected antecedent, not an assertion of absolute first invention

FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.SUPPORT: Named language definitions and explicit counterexamples where applicable; no general effectiveness theorem
FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.LIMITS: The four-valued rule is an operational reconstruction; authority and world correspondence are not logically supplied by syntax

EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.SUPPORT: S028 measures reference alignment and human judgments of multi-model pipelines, including iteration trade-offs. S029 compares two models and three prompts on 150 issue titles/900 generated statements using intrinsic wording criteria. S011 evaluates generated goal models on small teaching tasks.
EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.LIMITS: No source establishes stakeholder representation, authorized promotion or total lifecycle benefit. S019 is a non-AI template study retained only as adjacent evidence that wording scores do not establish contextual correctness.

SOURCE_ROLES.ERE-S-S029: DIRECT_INTRINSIC_WORDING_COMPARISON; excludes necessity, feasibility and domain completeness

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.SUPPORT: S019 extends a 2023 template-system study with enhanced analysis and additional usability/metamodel work. It supplies context about the limits of wording-quality evidence, not replication of AI assistance or candidate-promotion safeguards.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.LIMITS: No direct replication of the complete AI-source/domain/authority review mechanism is established in the linked inspected studies. This is a scoped reading assessment, not a literature-wide absence claim.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.ORIGINAL_OR_REPLICATED_CLAIM: S019 original/extended claim concerns the effects of five human-applied requirement templates on selected quality factors. S028/S029/S011 study different AI drafting/modeling tasks; they do not replicate that template mechanism or one another as a common full workflow.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.POPULATION_TASK_AND_OUTCOME: S019 reuses 249 original requirements and template rephrasings totaling 1,764 expressions; added usability work has 43 mostly-student subjects and acknowledged reliability problems. AI studies separately evaluate reference alignment, intrinsic quality or teaching model checks.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.DEPENDENCE: S019 explicitly shares its phrasing dataset with the 2023 precursor; the journal extension is not independent replication. The separate AI studies have distinct tasks/outcomes and are not counted as replicates of a single promotion rule.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.TRANSFER_TO_RETAINED_PROPERTY: S019 only cautions against promoting measured form/wording quality to contextual truth. Direct bounded AI-output evidence comes from S011/S028/S029; none establishes authorized acceptance or net lifecycle benefit.

INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.SUPPORT: Qualitative practitioner cases or source-document rewrite; distinctions in source records apply
INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.LIMITS: Reported practices and perceptions are not randomized process benefits or universal prevalence

NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.SUPPORT: Correlated models and judges can reward plausible hallucination; iterative expansion may reduce precision and add review costs.
NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.LIMITS: A paper’s open problem is not an observed failure; the constructed cases are not incident reports

STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.SUPPORT: No external standard mandate asserted in this research sublane
STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.LIMITS: Language conventions and an author’s chosen criterion do not grant normative authority; cited ISO editions not independently adopted

PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Input/output diff, review decisions and source links, not a model’s explanation alone.
PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: A tool’s existence/performance on selected examples does not establish organizational success

TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.SUPPORT: A draft suggests an offline mode; the analyst labels it a hypothesis, asks affected users, checks feasibility and records the resulting authorized bounded requirement.
TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.LIMITS: Constructed examples expose distinctions; they are not evidence of implementation effectiveness in a target repository

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Training-data contamination, stochastic variation, evaluator expertise and unseen domain risks remain.
CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: Contrary findings narrow claims; they do not justify symmetric overgeneralization

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.SUPPORT: Human reviewers have independent source/domain access; model output is not accepted merely because evaluators share its priors.
ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.LIMITS: Model/provider changes, source revisions or new affected parties invalidate benchmark transfer or promotion evidence as appropriate.

DOMAIN_VALIDITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Generated requirements and goal models compared with supplied/reference material or wording criteria.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.SUPPORT: S028 studies reference alignment and human perceptions, S029 studies intrinsic wording quality, and S011 studies small teaching goal-model tasks. They justify treating generated additions as candidates whose relationship to the actual problem remains to be checked.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.LIMITS: Those tasks do not establish necessity, domain completeness or stakeholder-grounded correctness of every generated requirement; the promotion rule is a synthesis.

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Who judges AI output and what their judgments represent.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.SUPPORT: S028 includes students and two professionals; S029 supplements a model judge with a small human check; S011 uses a small teaching comparison. These provide bounded evaluation judgments.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.LIMITS: Evaluator agreement or usefulness ratings are not independent elicitation from all affected stakeholders or proof that legitimate interests are covered.

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Whether generated additions have legitimate authority to become requirements.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.SUPPORT: The inspected AI studies evaluate model outputs and human judgments, not a valid mandate for every addition. The retained rule requires independent source/remit support before promotion.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.LIMITS: No model score, multi-model agreement or inferred standard citation is adopted as an authorization witness.

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Generated goal-model structure and mappings from problem wording.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.SUPPORT: S011 examines syntax checks, injected model smells and corrections on three short teaching problems. It supplies bounded structural checks and examples of model generation.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.LIMITS: Author-created defects and correction judgments do not prove semantically correct goal refinement, faithful stakeholder intent or universal translation correctness.

REALIZABILITY.SUPPORT: S029 explicitly excludes feasibility and domain completeness from its intrinsic-text evaluation; S028 does not establish deployment feasibility from reference alignment or prototype-related judgments.
REALIZABILITY.LIMITS: Generated fluency, a repaired sentence or a classroom prototype does not establish that requirements can be realized under a relevant environment and budget.

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Source additions, model/prompt provenance and problem-word mappings.
TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.SUPPORT: S011 offers task-local mappings to problem wording; S028 exposes variation and alignment limits that motivate preserving generation context and additions for review.
TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.LIMITS: Neither validates the full provenance/currentness discipline across a requirements lifecycle or turns a generated explanation into evidence that the source actually entails the claim.

ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: The boundary between a generated candidate and an accepted requirement.
ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.SUPPORT: The different evaluation targets in S028/S029 support withholding stronger conclusions from plausibility, reference similarity and wording scores. Independent need/domain/authority review is the proposed promotion safeguard.
ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: The complete safeguard has not been validated as an acceptance workflow; reviewer competence and actual evidence can remain inadequate even when a review field is present.

EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Model/prompt/pipeline outputs and small evaluator tasks.
EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.SUPPORT: S028 reports iteration trade-offs and human disagreement, S029 compares two models and three prompt strategies on 150 titles, and S011 evaluates generated teaching models.
EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.LIMITS: These are not measurements of the net lifecycle benefit of the synthesized human-review policy. S019 is a non-AI template study and supplies only adjacent quality-evaluation limits.

DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Whether model output warrants promotion or another generation stage.
DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.SUPPORT: S028 shows why iteration and agreement cannot be assumed to improve the relevant decision; S029 bounds its scores to wording. The rule therefore ties promotion to independently supported additions.
DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.LIMITS: No universal model/prompt winner, optimal review intensity or measured cost-benefit model follows; the proposed decision rule is not an empirical effectiveness finding.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.EVIDENCE_CEILING: 2026 studies measure reference alignment, intrinsic text quality and human perceived utility; one reports iteration trade-offs and disagreement. No stakeholder representation, contractual authorization or deployment outcome is established. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.TRANSFERABILITY_LIMITS: Model/prompt and benchmark versions fixed; quality judgments and similarity are proxies, not a complete truth oracle. Training-data contamination, stochastic variation, evaluator expertise and unseen domain risks remain.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.UNVERIFIED_OR_OPEN_QUESTIONS: Prospective blinded study with real stakeholder decisions, total review cost and traced rejected additions; fix versions and repeat runs.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: Prospective blinded study with real stakeholder decisions, total review cost and traced rejected additions; fix versions and repeat runs.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: The reviewers inspected the complete claim/disposition population and selected detailed semantics/source bodies. Absence of an individual finding does not establish independent validation of every field, source or proposed predicate.

INTAKE.CROSSWALK_ELIGIBILITY_WITH_REASON: ELIGIBLE_WITH_CONTEXT: inspect equivalent existing mechanism, guard, cheap path and evidence before considering any adoption
TARGET_NEUTRAL_AUDIT_QUESTIONS: Which generated additions are independently supported, and what review burden was needed to discover the unsupported ones?
Does a simpler existing mechanism already answer the same consumer question?
Which assumption, scope or authority change would require re-entry?
PROHIBITED_OVERCLAIMS: LLM consensus, similarity or intrinsic-quality scores establish complete, necessary and authorized requirements.
No finding about any target repository or semantic owner is supplied.

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Automated trace recovery proposes links for semantic verification

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Information-retrieval/machine-learning recovery;2024 benchmark comparison and2026 TraceLLM
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: Recovery ranks candidate relations against reference links.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: Recovery ranks candidate relations against reference links.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: High recall/F-score on a benchmark is treated as a current, semantically valid trace set for another project.
GENEALOGY.INFLUENCE_OR_RELATION_CLASS: ANALYTICAL_QUALIFICATION_OF_DOCUMENTED_BRANCH; see genealogy edges for evidence-backed historical relations

HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.CLAIM_SUPPORTED: Six selected methods on 13 datasets; stronger baselines can alter apparent progress; precision/recall/F1 are recovery metrics
HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.ROLE: DIRECT_RECOVERY_METHOD_REPRODUCTION_AND_COMPARISON for benchmark performance and comparator sensitivity
HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: Java-only datasets; preprocessing/POS/language threats; benchmarks do not establish semantic currentness or maintenance payoff

HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.CLAIM_SUPPORTED: Trace candidates with human validation; recall-weighted evaluation assumes review; cold-start, prompt, stochasticity and maintenance limits
HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.ROLE: DIRECT_PROMPT_RECOVERY_STUDY with human-validation assumptions; not full workflow replication
HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: Benchmark alignment is not current semantic truth; strongest few-shot needs labeled links; maintenance/industrial expansion remain future work

HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.CLAIM_SUPPORTED: 55 survey respondents and 14 interviewees with 8 overlap; perceived value, cost distribution, existing-tool reuse and human validation
HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.ROLE: ADJACENT_PRACTITIONER_CONTEXT for burden and validation needs; not causal algorithm benefit
HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: 61 distinct participants, mostly Europe, convenience/self-report and limited contextual resolution; no measured causal ROI

HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.CLAIM_SUPPORTED: Pre/post-specification tracing; provider/consumer costs; source participation and access; stale documentation and local cheap paths
HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.ROLE: CONCEPTUAL_AND_PRACTICE_ANTECEDENT for meaningful trace/source access; not current benchmark validation
HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.UNSUPPORTED_PROMOTION: Mixed practitioner/tool study, not causal treatment trial; historical practice not a census of current tools

GENEALOGY.DISPUTED_ATTRIBUTION_OR_ANACHRONISM_RISK: No claim of absolute first invention. Recovery metrics describe the evaluated label set; precision/recall costs vary by use; few-shot completion differs from cold-start generation.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: Use recovered links as candidates whose meaning, version/context and false-positive/false-negative consequences are checked against the consumer decision.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: A recovered source-target relation and its confidence/verification
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.FAILURE_MODE_OR_LIMIT_ADDRESSED: High recall/F-score on a benchmark is treated as a current, semantically valid trace set for another project.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MECHANISM: Choose relevant baselines and threshold/recall trade-offs, retain labeled-source provenance, then review candidate links semantically; measure missed-impact and review costs separately from benchmark scores.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Match metrics to decision costs and require semantic review; compare strong baselines and total workflow burden.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Reduced search space and discovery of links a human might miss.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE: 2024 comparison of six methods/13 Java datasets;2026 prompt study explicitly assumes human validation, with maintenance/industrial expansion future work. No universal automatic truth or lifecycle ROI.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Trace analyst or maintainer seeking an impact/rationale relation.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ALTERNATIVE_MECHANISMS: Lexical search, existing known links and direct source-person contact for small tasks.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Many plausible source-target pairs and a meaningful recovery/search cost.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A single obvious code/test change linked to one current requirement can be traced directly.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: Reference labels and candidate artifacts match the intended link semantics; reviewers can evaluate output and missing links.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ENVIRONMENT_AND_BOUNDARY: Recovery metrics describe the evaluated label set; precision/recall costs vary by use; few-shot completion differs from cold-start generation.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: Recovery metrics describe the evaluated label set; precision/recall costs vary by use; few-shot completion differs from cold-start generation. Excludes any target repository finding or inter-lineage ownership assignment.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: Automated relation similarity does not create a valid derivation, implementation or acceptance warrant.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.INPUT_AND_EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMEN: Artifact versions, relation definition, ground-truth process, split/prompt/model configuration, candidate score and human disposition.

DEPENDENCIES_AND_CONFLICTS.LIMIT: Relations are conditional; see internal_relations, not all listed items are mandatory prerequisites

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.FAILURE_OF_ASSUMPTIONS: A new requirement reuses old wording; the system recovers an obsolete test link and auto-certifies coverage without reviewing changed population.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Use recovered links as candidates whose meaning, version/context and false-positive/false-negative consequences are checked against the consumer decision.

EVALUATION_MODE.DEFINITION: Mode describes how evidence is assessed, separate from the commissioned predicate-role enum. A sufficiency challenge tests an asserted implication or universal process benefit; ordinary operational assessment evaluates the bounded source-informed rule. Mechanical record checks do not settle semantic, empirical or authority judgments.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: Assess(subject: A recovered source-target relation and its confidence/verification, context, consumerDecision, evidenceSnapshot, validTime) -> PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|INAPPLICABLE
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Universal only over explicitly enumerated material items needed for the declared decision and search scope. No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A recovered source-target relation and its confidence/verification
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Assessed at the named evidence/configuration snapshot. Hypothesized, desired, agreed and observed states remain distinct. Later changes require the stated invalidation procedure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Reference labels and candidate artifacts match the intended link semantics; reviewers can evaluate output and missing links.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: Many plausible source-target pairs and a meaningful recovery/search cost.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: For every recovered link relied upon, require a semantic witness at current versions/context; evaluate coverage gaps under the intended query. Benchmark F-score alone leaves semantic/currentness status UNKNOWN; a spurious or stale accepted link FAILS. Labeled search suggestions not yet relied on are INAPPLICABLE to final-link acceptance.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.LIMIT: Not a verbatim source theorem, source standard requirement or empirically validated universal acceptance algorithm

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Candidate list, labels and adjudication plus sampled missing-link investigation; evidence of actual consumer-query performance.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Artifact versions, relation definition, ground-truth process, split/prompt/model configuration, candidate score and human disposition.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: An informed evaluator checks applicability, identifies the exact claim and scope, reviews the named witnesses, tests the supplied counterexample class and records a reasoned four-valued outcome. Mechanical schema checks can establish presence/identity, not domain truth or authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite record checks are mechanically decidable. Semantic correspondence, legitimate representation, proxy validity and causal transfer generally require contextual judgment and may remain UNKNOWN. No claim of general decidability.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.TEXT: A high-recall system surfaces candidate test links; a reviewer rejects lexical matches that exercise a different account class and confirms the rest with test assertions.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.TEXT: A new requirement reuses old wording; the system recovers an obsolete test link and auto-certifies coverage without reviewing changed population.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: One local method is changed and its current requirement/test relation is directly inspectable.

FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_POSITIVE: A high F2 or a human-in-the-loop label is not assurance unless the review actually checks relation semantics.
FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_NEGATIVE: Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. A high F2 or a human-in-the-loop label is not assurance unless the review actually checks relation semantics.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Artifact/context/label meaning, prompt/model or operational error costs change; stale links need revalidation, not just reranking.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Inference/search cost plus false-positive review, missed-impact risk and maintenance; cheaper model is not automatically cheaper total workflow. Alternative: A single obvious code/test change linked to one current requirement can be traced directly.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: 2024 comparison of six methods/13 Java datasets;2026 prompt study explicitly assumes human validation, with maintenance/industrial expansion future work. No universal automatic truth or lifecycle ROI. The operational rule is a proposed audit discriminator, not a measured process-effect claim.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE: Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

Benchmark F-score alone leaves semantic/currentness status UNKNOWN; a spurious or stale accepted link FAILS. Labeled search suggestions not yet relied on are INAPPLICABLE to final-link acceptance.

OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: An explicit guard excludes the claim; cheap path must be justified

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.EMPTY_SCOPE_RULE: Empty obligation/source sets never establish completeness by vacuity; show scope adequacy or label inapplicable/unknown.

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.SUPPORT: Information-retrieval/machine-learning recovery;2024 benchmark comparison and2026 TraceLLM
HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.LIMITS: Origin means inspected antecedent, not an assertion of absolute first invention

FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.SUPPORT: Named language definitions and explicit counterexamples where applicable; no general effectiveness theorem
FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.LIMITS: The four-valued rule is an operational reconstruction; authority and world correspondence are not logically supplied by syntax

EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.SUPPORT: S024 compares six methods on 13 Java recovery datasets; S025 compares prompted trace-recovery variants and explicitly relies on human validation in its interpretation.
EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.LIMITS: These comparisons evaluate recovery against reference labels, not current semantic correctness after project changes or total human-review/maintenance return.

SOURCE_ROLES.ERE-S-S025: DIRECT_PROMPTED_RECOVERY_COMPARISON; different framework, not replication of the complete acceptance rule

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.SUPPORT: S024 reproduces and compares selected published recovery approaches on common benchmark datasets, directly informing the stronger-baseline and task-metric portion of this property. S025 supplies a separate prompted recovery study with explicit human-validation assumptions.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.LIMITS: These are narrower recovery evaluations, not replication of the full current semantic acceptance workflow. Repeated public datasets, reference labels and method implementations cannot be treated as independent industrial validation.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.ORIGINAL_OR_REPLICATED_CLAIM: Performance of published requirement-to-code recovery methods relative to relevant comparators; S024 assesses six selected methods rather than accepting each original comparison against weak baselines.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.POPULATION_TASK_AND_OUTCOME: 13 Java datasets; recovery against labeled links assessed with precision, recall and F1. S025 evaluates prompt/model strategies under its own benchmark and review assumptions.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.DEPENDENCE: S024 reuses public benchmark artifacts and reimplements/uses selected methods within one common evaluation. S025 is not a repeated execution of the synthesized currentness predicate; cross-paper dataset independence is not established here.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.TRANSFER_TO_RETAINED_PROPERTY: Supports comparing strong baselines and withholding semantic truth from benchmark scores. Human review, current versions and total workflow costs remain additional unvalidated parts of the synthesis.

INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.SUPPORT: Qualitative practitioner cases or source-document rewrite; distinctions in source records apply
INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.LIMITS: Reported practices and perceptions are not randomized process benefits or universal prevalence

NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.SUPPORT: Optimizing recall externalizes false-positive review cost; strong few-shot results rely on labels unavailable in cold-start tasks.
NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.LIMITS: A paper’s open problem is not an observed failure; the constructed cases are not incident reports

STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.SUPPORT: No external standard mandate asserted in this research sublane
STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.LIMITS: Language conventions and an author’s chosen criterion do not grant normative authority; cited ISO editions not independently adopted

PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Candidate list, labels and adjudication plus sampled missing-link investigation; evidence of actual consumer-query performance.
PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: A tool’s existence/performance on selected examples does not establish organizational success

TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.SUPPORT: A high-recall system surfaces candidate test links; a reviewer rejects lexical matches that exercise a different account class and confirms the rest with test assertions.
TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.LIMITS: Constructed examples expose distinctions; they are not evidence of implementation effectiveness in a target repository

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Unknown true links and benchmark-label incompleteness remain; proprietary model changes reduce repeatability.
CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: Contrary findings narrow claims; they do not justify symmetric overgeneralization

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.SUPPORT: Reference labels and candidate artifacts match the intended link semantics; reviewers can evaluate output and missing links.
ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.LIMITS: Artifact/context/label meaning, prompt/model or operational error costs change; stale links need revalidation, not just reranking.

DOMAIN_VALIDITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Recovering requirement-to-code or other source-target links under labeled benchmark tasks.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.SUPPORT: S024 compares six selected methods on 13 datasets, and S025 evaluates prompted trace candidates. These establish bounded alignment with the datasets and labels used.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.LIMITS: Java-only data in S024, task/preprocessing assumptions and model/prompt dependence limit transfer; agreement with benchmark labels is not current domain truth.

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: The analyst who must review candidates and the people bearing tracing costs.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.SUPPORT: S023 reports practitioner perspectives on tracing value and burdens; S025 explicitly assumes human validation when interpreting recall-oriented recovery.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.LIMITS: Benchmark participation and the practitioner sample do not show that every affected consumer or interpretation is represented in a recovered link set.

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Whether a recovered link creates an obligation or grants authority.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.SUPPORT: The mechanism offers decision support for retrieval and semantic checking; it is not a normative source.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.LIMITS: A correct source-target match cannot by itself establish an endpoint mandate, regulatory applicability or an authorized acceptance decision.

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Formal refinement validity inferred from recovery confidence.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.SUPPORT: The compared algorithms predict or rank trace relations; neither a high score nor a refines label is a formal preservation proof.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.LIMITS: Any relied-on refinement relationship requires its own semantic or formal argument outside this recovery assessment.

REALIZABILITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: System realizability inferred from requirement-to-code connectivity.
REALIZABILITY.SUPPORT: The studies address recovery of relations among given artifacts, not existence of an implementation satisfying the whole requirement set.
REALIZABILITY.LIMITS: Linked code, even correctly linked, does not prove behavioral satisfaction or feasibility of all requirements.

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Precision, recall and related recovery metrics against stated reference links.
TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.SUPPORT: S024 supplies comparative method evaluations and stronger-baseline challenges; S025 supplies prompt-based comparisons and a rationale for human validation.
TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.LIMITS: Missing or disputed gold labels, new versions and consumer-specific semantics are not repaired by F-score. The synthesized current semantic verification gate is not itself established by these scores.

ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Promotion of a recovered candidate into a link relied on by a decision.
ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.SUPPORT: S025 frames recovery as candidates needing human validation; S021/S023 explain source access and practical consumer needs. These support distinguishing search output from an accepted semantic relation.
ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: No trial validates the complete final-link acceptance rule, and a reviewer click alone is not evidence of semantic correspondence.

EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Algorithm/prompt comparisons versus total review and maintenance outcomes.
EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.SUPPORT: S024/S025 measure recovery performance and reveal baseline, prompt and cold-start sensitivity. S023 supplies descriptive adoption and cost context.
EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.LIMITS: The evidence does not establish total workflow return, missed-impact costs or lifecycle maintenance benefit; these must not be inferred from a benchmark improvement.

DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Matching thresholds and recall/precision trade-offs to the consuming query.
DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.SUPPORT: S024 shows why comparator choice matters; S025 uses recall-weighted evaluation under a human-review assumption. This supports explicitly naming review and missed-link consequences.
DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.LIMITS: No universal threshold or calibrated total-cost function is validated; a selected metric may be inappropriate for a different decision or reviewer budget.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.EVIDENCE_CEILING: 2024 comparison of six methods/13 Java datasets;2026 prompt study explicitly assumes human validation, with maintenance/industrial expansion future work. No universal automatic truth or lifecycle ROI. Source access levels bind every claim; schema completeness is not domain validation.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.TRANSFERABILITY_LIMITS: Recovery metrics describe the evaluated label set; precision/recall costs vary by use; few-shot completion differs from cold-start generation. Unknown true links and benchmark-label incompleteness remain; proprietary model changes reduce repeatability.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.UNVERIFIED_OR_OPEN_QUESTIONS: Evaluate real change-impact decisions and human review effort on current artifacts, including known-negative and missed-link controls.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: Evaluate real change-impact decisions and human review effort on current artifacts, including known-negative and missed-link controls.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: The reviewers inspected the complete claim/disposition population and selected detailed semantics/source bodies. Absence of an individual finding does not establish independent validation of every field, source or proposed predicate.

INTAKE.CROSSWALK_ELIGIBILITY_WITH_REASON: ELIGIBLE_WITH_CONTEXT: inspect equivalent existing mechanism, guard, cheap path and evidence before considering any adoption
TARGET_NEUTRAL_AUDIT_QUESTIONS: Who verified the recovered relation’s meaning, and how were missed links and review costs evaluated?
Does a simpler existing mechanism already answer the same consumer question?
Which assumption, scope or authority change would require re-entry?
PROHIBITED_OVERCLAIMS: State-of-the-art recovery scores certify semantic trace validity or reliable change-impact coverage.
No finding about any target repository or semantic owner is supplied.

EVALUATION_MODE.DEFINITION: Mode describes how evidence is assessed, separate from the commissioned predicate-role enum. A sufficiency challenge tests an asserted implication or universal process benefit; ordinary operational assessment evaluates the bounded source-informed rule. Mechanical record checks do not settle semantic, empirical or authority judgments.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: Assess(subject: A story and the human/tool context needed to implement, test or change it, context, consumerDecision, evidenceSnapshot, validTime) -> PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|INAPPLICABLE
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Universal only over explicitly enumerated material items needed for the declared decision and search scope. No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A story and the human/tool context needed to implement, test or change it
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Assessed at the named evidence/configuration snapshot. Hypothesized, desired, agreed and observed states remain distinct. Later changes require the stated invalidation procedure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: The right people are available when needed, or material context is externalized before it is lost.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: Story wording alone leaves material behavior or acceptance interpretation unresolved for a consumer.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: For each material consumer question, the story text, accessible discussion or retained criterion must provide a current answer or an explicit unresolved disposition. A syntactically complete card with lost essential context FAILS the claimed adequacy; missing assessment is UNKNOWN.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.LIMIT: Not a verbatim source theorem, source standard requirement or empirically validated universal acceptance algorithm

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Story package, consumer questions, discussion decisions and supersession records.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Source/role, discussion decisions, criterion, exceptions, version and supersession relation.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: An informed evaluator checks applicability, identifies the exact claim and scope, reviews the named witnesses, tests the supplied counterexample class and records a reasoned four-valued outcome. Mechanical schema checks can establish presence/identity, not domain truth or authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite record checks are mechanically decidable. Semantic correspondence, legitimate representation, proxy validity and causal transfer generally require contextual judgment and may remain UNKNOWN. No claim of general decidability.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.TEXT: A short story links an agreed cancellation example and exception decision; a later tester can resolve behavior without guessing the original conversation.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.TEXT: The card says “As an administrator I want notifications”; the conversation defined an exclusion but was lost, so developers implement the opposite scope.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: A single-user reversible text change is fully determined by one sentence and direct confirmation.

OUTCOMES.PASS: Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation

FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.SUPPORT: Named language definitions and explicit counterexamples where applicable; no general effectiveness theorem
FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.LIMITS: The four-valued rule is an operational reconstruction; authority and world correspondence are not logically supplied by syntax

EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.SUPPORT: S031 evaluates selected QUS/AQUSA text-defect detection on 1,023 stories from 18 organizations. The S030 interviews, S033 workshop and S034 survey provide distinct descriptive/use-context evidence elsewhere in this record.
EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.LIMITS: Tool detection metrics do not demonstrate downstream outcome improvement, a story-versus-document causal advantage, or the effect of retaining conversation and supersession context.

SOURCE_ROLES.ERE-S-S031: DIRECT_SELECTED_STORY_DEFECT_EVALUATION; not a trial of the complete context-retention mechanism

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.SUPPORT: S031 extends the authors’ 2015 QUS/AQUSA proposal with framework/tool and evaluation work; S030/S033/S034 provide distinct documentation, workshop and perceptions evidence. None is a replication of the complete story-context-retention/supersession rule.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.LIMITS: The 2015 precursor is described through S031 and is not independently evaluated here; exact dataset overlap across versions is not resolved. Distinct studies address different questions, so they are not interchangeable replications.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.ORIGINAL_OR_REPLICATED_CLAIM: S031 builds on a framework for story quality and the AQUSA tool concept, testing selected textual defects. The broader property concerns availability of conversation, criteria and current meaning to actual consumers.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.POPULATION_TASK_AND_OUTCOME: S031 evaluates 1,023 stories from 18 organizations, mostly Dutch ISVs. S030 interviews 20 practitioners; S033 is one domain workshop; S034 surveys 112 respondents about mapping/scenario knowledge and perceptions.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.DEPENDENCE: QUS conference/journal forms are one research program, not independent confirmation. The field studies are adjacent observations with different tasks, not replications of a shared causal intervention.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.TRANSFER_TO_RETAINED_PROPERTY: Supports bounded communication/context concerns. It does not establish causal gains from a specified retention policy, future-consumer completeness or operating efficiency.

INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.SUPPORT: Qualitative practitioner cases or source-document rewrite; distinctions in source records apply
INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.LIMITS: Reported practices and perceptions are not randomized process benefits or universal prevalence

NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.SUPPORT: Retaining everything destroys the economy of stories; relying on memory excludes later consumers.
NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.LIMITS: A paper’s open problem is not an observed failure; the constructed cases are not incident reports

STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.SUPPORT: No external standard mandate asserted in this research sublane
STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.LIMITS: Language conventions and an author’s chosen criterion do not grant normative authority; cited ISO editions not independently adopted

PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Story package, consumer questions, discussion decisions and supersession records.
PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: A tool’s existence/performance on selected examples does not establish organizational success

TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.SUPPORT: A short story links an agreed cancellation example and exception decision; a later tester can resolve behavior without guessing the original conversation.
TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.LIMITS: Constructed examples expose distinctions; they are not evidence of implementation effectiveness in a target repository

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Future questions may not be predictable and tacit domain knowledge can remain unavailable.
CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: Contrary findings narrow claims; they do not justify symmetric overgeneralization

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.SUPPORT: The right people are available when needed, or material context is externalized before it is lost.
ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.LIMITS: New consumer, delayed implementation, team turnover or changed criterion can invalidate adequacy without changing the card.

DOMAIN_VALIDITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Whether compact story text carries enough context for actual consumer tasks.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.SUPPORT: S031 distinguishes story text, conversation and acceptance criteria; S030 reports documentation/update problems. S033 supplies one mapping workshop and S034 supplies perceptions of mapping/scenario relations.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.LIMITS: These sources support contextual adequacy concerns, not universal story superiority or a validated optimum amount of retained discussion.

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Story roles, participants and perspectives in story use/mapping.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.SUPPORT: S030 reports role-involvement gaps; S033 highlights facilitation and additional perspectives; S034 surveys 112 respondents about mapping use and perceptions.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.LIMITS: A role field/persona does not prove representation. The samples and workshop do not establish comprehensive affected-party coverage or legitimate delegated authority.

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Whether a story author or product owner has remit for every represented need.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.SUPPORT: The inspected story-quality, documentation and mapping studies do not establish mandate validity. The property keeps source/role authority separate from syntax and conversational accessibility.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.LIMITS: Filling the role/goal/reason form or obtaining agreement from workshop attendees cannot by itself authorize a requirement.

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Formal preservation from story mapping or story decomposition.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.SUPPORT: Activity grouping, inquiry and story criteria organize understanding but are not a proof system for refinement. S033 provides an interpreted map, not formal entailment.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.LIMITS: A coherent map or split story can still change meaning; the retained-context criterion does not prove each decomposition correct.

REALIZABILITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Technical feasibility established by a usable story card or map.

REALIZABILITY.LIMITS: Usable wording, a mock-up or a testable criterion does not establish system-level feasibility.

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.SUPPORT: S030 identifies change and requirement/test documentation gaps; S017 supplies inquiry/rationale links. These motivate preserving consumer-relevant decisions as story meaning changes.
TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.LIMITS: No measured evaluation establishes accuracy or durability of the synthesized supersession/current-context scheme; future questions and tacit knowledge remain uncertain.

DECISION_MODEL_VALIDITY.LIMITS: No validated cost threshold determines the right retention depth or predicts every future consumer; the cheap-path and re-entry decisions remain contextual.

Does a simpler existing mechanism already answer the same consumer question?

SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.INPUT: Source/role, discussion decisions, criterion, exceptions, version and supersession relation.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.OUTPUT: Keep enough discussion, criterion and supersession context for the story’s actual consumers; text compactness is suitable only while those supports remain accessible and adequate.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.CONSUMER: Developer, tester or later maintainer whose question must be answered.
SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES.BOUNDARY: Story roles/personas are not automatically real stakeholder representation; card syntax and conversational adequacy are different.

SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.APPLICATION: Target-neutral schema applied to the property; worked cases are explicitly analytical
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.NARRATIVE_NOTATION: A story comprises brief text, conversation and acceptance criteria; textual role/means/end is only one component.
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.BEHAVIOURAL_SCOPE: Story roles/personas are not automatically real stakeholder representation; card syntax and conversational adequacy are different.
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.EXCEPTIONS: The card says “As an administrator I want notifications”; the conversation defined an exclusion but was lost, so developers implement the opposite scope.
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.ASSUMPTIONS: The right people are available when needed, or material context is externalized before it is lost.
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.FORMAL_LINKS: Any mapping to a state/temporal specification or executable oracle must be named and checked separately; no such map is presumed from prose form
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.TEST_DERIVATION: Use compact text to organize a conversation, record decisions and examples needed later, and preserve which revised story supersedes which meaning. An activity/story map may restore temporal and task context obscured by a flat backlog; its grouping remains an interpretation to review.
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.EVIDENCE_LIMITS: QUS tool study measures selected story defects;2016 interviews report incomplete documentation and update/link problems; no universal story-versus-document superiority. A domain workshop and a2024 survey support bounded mapping use/perceptions; neither establishes causal general improvements or actual-use efficiency.
SCENARIO_SPECIFICATION_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Co-located short-lived reversible work can use concise text and immediate discussion with a small recorded outcome.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Define a requirements-quality claim through its consumer activity, plausible causal mechanism and observed outcome, keeping context and uncertainty explicit.

EVALUATION_MODE.DEFINITION: Mode describes how evidence is assessed, separate from the commissioned predicate-role enum. A sufficiency challenge tests an asserted implication or universal process benefit; ordinary operational assessment evaluates the bounded source-informed rule. Mechanical record checks do not settle semantic, empirical or authority judgments.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: Assess(subject: A requirement expression used by a specified actor for a specified task, context, consumerDecision, evidenceSnapshot, validTime) -> PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN|INAPPLICABLE

VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS.CONSTRAINT: Outcome, unit, baseline and population explicit

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Universal only over explicitly enumerated material items needed for the declared decision and search scope. No quantification over all possible stakeholders, worlds or future changes. A universal sufficiency claim is refuted by a valid applicable counterexample; case PASS is not universal proof.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A requirement expression used by a specified actor for a specified task
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Assessed at the named evidence/configuration snapshot. Hypothesized, desired, agreed and observed states remain distinct. Later changes require the stated invalidation procedure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: The selected task/outcome represents the intended consumer and measurement is valid; causal assumptions are explicit.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: Quality rules are being prioritized or used to justify an intervention, tool or acceptance gate.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: A claimed quality benefit must name the affected activity and outcome, describe a causal/operational path and have evidence appropriate to that context. Direct contradictory task evidence FAILS the claimed benefit; mere conformity with no outcome warrant is UNKNOWN. Pure normative compliance is evaluated separately.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.LIMIT: Not a verbatim source theorem, source standard requirement or empirically validated universal acceptance algorithm

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Task outputs/errors, duration, participant/context descriptors and treatment comparison.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Feature definition, activity, participant/background, outcome measure, comparison, causal assumptions and uncertainty.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: An informed evaluator checks applicability, identifies the exact claim and scope, reviews the named witnesses, tests the supplied counterexample class and records a reasoned four-valued outcome. Mechanical schema checks can establish presence/identity, not domain truth or authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite record checks are mechanically decidable. Semantic correspondence, legitimate representation, proxy validity and causal transfer generally require contextual judgment and may remain UNKNOWN. No claim of general decidability.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.TEXT: Ambiguous pronoun removal changes readers’ domain-model associations under a declared task; evidence supports attention to that ambiguity in similar work.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.TEXT: A tool penalizes all passive voice equally and asserts equivalent downstream harm for each occurrence despite little relevant effect in the task evidence.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The guard plausibly applies but required source, semantic interpretation, authority, context or observation is missing/disputed; insufficient evidence is not silently coded FAIL or PASS.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: A requirement contains an explicit impossible numeric condition; direct domain reasoning resolves it without quality-score research.

FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_POSITIVE: A sophisticated statistical model cannot repair an invalid construct or irrelevant task.
FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_NEGATIVE: Rejecting a legitimate cheap path, demanding irrelevant evidence, or treating an unrecorded but unresolved dimension as known false.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An empty declared scope cannot pass merely because no obligations were listed: explain why the guard is inapplicable or why the scope is adequate. A sophisticated statistical model cannot repair an invalid construct or irrelevant task.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Changed task, reader competence, domain, wording feature or outcome definition invalidates broad transfer.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Studies and measurement can exceed local benefit; reuse relevant bounded evidence before collecting new data. Alternative: A clear direct contradiction can be corrected without an experimental quality model.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: 25-participant four-statement domain-modeling experiment finds different effects for passive voice and ambiguous pronouns, with important transfer and measurement limits. The operational rule is a proposed audit discriminator, not a measured process-effect claim.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE: Analytical operational reconstruction from inspected primary sources; no claim of a source-native theorem or universal algorithm.

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.RULE: A claimed quality benefit must name the affected activity and outcome, describe a causal/operational path and have evidence appropriate to that context. Direct contradictory task evidence FAILS the claimed benefit; mere conformity with no outcome warrant is UNKNOWN. Pure normative compliance is evaluated separately.

OUTCOMES.PASS: Required evidence supports the bounded claim within scope; no universal extrapolation
OUTCOMES.FAIL: An applicable observed contradiction, failed criterion or valid counterexample defeats the specified claim
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Relevant evidence/meaning/authority is missing, disputed or not discriminating
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: An explicit guard excludes the claim; cheap path must be justified

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.EMPTY_SCOPE_RULE: Empty obligation/source sets never establish completeness by vacuity; show scope adequacy or label inapplicable/unknown.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.POSITIVE_WITNESS_OR_WORKED_EXAMPLE: Ambiguous pronoun removal changes readers’ domain-model associations under a declared task; evidence supports attention to that ambiguity in similar work.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.NEGATIVE_WITNESS_OR_COUNTEREXAMPLE: A tool penalizes all passive voice equally and asserts equivalent downstream harm for each occurrence despite little relevant effect in the task evidence.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.NON_TRIGGER_EXAMPLE: A requirement contains an explicit impossible numeric condition; direct domain reasoning resolves it without quality-score research.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.OBSERVABILITY_AND_MISSINGNESS: Task outputs/errors, duration, participant/context descriptors and treatment comparison. Missing evidence remains UNKNOWN unless an explicit contradicted claim is being tested.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.CURRENTNESS_AND_INVALIDATION: Changed task, reader competence, domain, wording feature or outcome definition invalidates broad transfer.

CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Small experiments and weak experience proxies can create a false appearance of causal precision.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.KNOWN_FAILURES_AND_MISUSES: A tool penalizes all passive voice equally and asserts equivalent downstream harm for each occurrence despite little relevant effect in the task evidence.

CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESIDUAL_LIMITS: Sparse task-specific evidence, unmeasured interactions and imperfect context variables remain.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.CEREMONY_VERSUS_MECHANISM: A sophisticated statistical model cannot repair an invalid construct or irrelevant task.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RETENTION_RATIONALE: Retain the bounded mechanism with explicit guard, evidence and cheap path. State causal assumptions, effect uncertainty and context limits; seek discriminating replications rather than universal scores.

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.SUPPORT: Quality-in-use lineage; Frattini et al.2024/2025 controlled conceptual replication
HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.LIMITS: Origin means inspected antecedent, not an assertion of absolute first invention

FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.SUPPORT: Named language definitions and explicit counterexamples where applicable; no general effectiveness theorem
FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.LIMITS: The four-valued rule is an operational reconstruction; authority and world correspondence are not logically supplied by syntax

EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.SUPPORT: S027 directly studies passive voice and ambiguous pronouns through four domain-modeling tasks with 25 participants. S019 separately compares template/phrasing factors, S031 measures selected story defects, and S029 measures intrinsic quality of generated wording. These studies have different outcomes and are not pooled effect replications.
EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.LIMITS: Only S027 directly measures the cited linguistic-feature/domain-model effect. Template scores, defect-detection metrics and intrinsic ratings do not establish universal downstream harm, project benefit or transferable quality weights.

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.SUPPORT: S027 contributes a new conceptual replication of the passive-voice/domain-modeling hypothesis described from Femmer et al. (2014); its ambiguous-pronoun question extends the investigated features. S019 separately extends template comparisons using prior phrasing data.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.LIMITS: These studies support particular activity/feature claims and evaluation cautions. They do not replicate the synthesized activity-relative prioritization rule or establish universal quality weights; the original passive-voice study is accessed here through S027.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.ORIGINAL_OR_REPLICATED_CLAIM: Passive voice may affect downstream domain-model entities/associations; S027 replicates that subset and adds pronoun/context factors. S019 extends selected template-quality comparisons, not the same domain-modeling experiment.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.POPULATION_TASK_AND_OUTCOME: S027 describes an original 15-student/seven-requirement design and conducts a new 25-participant/four-sentence modeling study. S019 reuses 249 originals/1,764 phrasings and adds 43-subject usability work with explicit reliability limits.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.DEPENDENCE: S027 new experimental data are distinct from the original dataset; the earlier reanalysis is dependent on original data. S019 is explicitly a journal extension sharing data with its 2023 precursor. These are two different task families, not interchangeable replications.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.TRANSFER_TO_RETAINED_PROPERTY: Provides bounded evidence that feature effects and measurement meaning depend on the activity, while leaving broader causal transfer, normative applicability and the proposed decision rule unvalidated.

INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.SUPPORT: Qualitative practitioner cases or source-document rewrite; distinctions in source records apply
INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.LIMITS: Reported practices and perceptions are not randomized process benefits or universal prevalence

NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.SUPPORT: Small experiments and weak experience proxies can create a false appearance of causal precision.
NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.LIMITS: A paper’s open problem is not an observed failure; the constructed cases are not incident reports

STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.SUPPORT: No external standard mandate asserted in this research sublane
STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.LIMITS: Language conventions and an author’s chosen criterion do not grant normative authority; cited ISO editions not independently adopted

PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Task outputs/errors, duration, participant/context descriptors and treatment comparison.
PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: A tool’s existence/performance on selected examples does not establish organizational success

TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.SUPPORT: Ambiguous pronoun removal changes readers’ domain-model associations under a declared task; evidence supports attention to that ambiguity in similar work.
TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.LIMITS: Constructed examples expose distinctions; they are not evidence of implementation effectiveness in a target repository

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.SUPPORT: Sparse task-specific evidence, unmeasured interactions and imperfect context variables remain.
CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: Contrary findings narrow claims; they do not justify symmetric overgeneralization

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.SUPPORT: The selected task/outcome represents the intended consumer and measurement is valid; causal assumptions are explicit.
ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.LIMITS: Changed task, reader competence, domain, wording feature or outcome definition invalidates broad transfer.

DOMAIN_VALIDITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Effects of selected wording features on a downstream domain-modeling task.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.SUPPORT: S027 compares passive voice and ambiguous pronouns using 25 participants and four single-sentence requirements. Their different observed effects support specifying the consumer activity instead of assigning universal equal harm to wording deviations.
DOMAIN_VALIDITY.LIMITS: The task, sentence set and outcomes do not cover all requirements validity or all domains; conditional evidence for this activity cannot calibrate a universal quality score.

STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: The people and experience variables represented in quality evaluations.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.SUPPORT: S027 recruits from industry/university and records experience/context factors; S019 has a 43-subject mostly-student usability study; S031 uses organizational story samples.
STAKEHOLDER_COVERAGE.LIMITS: A study participant or tool evaluator is not a proxy for all stakeholders. S027 context self-reports and the acknowledged S019 usability problems limit interpretation.

NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Whether empirical quality-in-use evidence creates or removes an external convention.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.SUPPORT: This property evaluates task benefit. An applicable writing convention can be obligatory independently of its measured effect, but these experiments do not establish such applicability.
NORMATIVE_SOURCE_AUTHORITY.LIMITS: Observed task effects cannot themselves invalidate a legitimate normative requirement; no external standard adoption is inferred.

REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Whether better wording or model output proves refinement soundness.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.SUPPORT: S027 measures omissions/associations in derived domain models, not a formal theorem connecting refinement levels. The retained property concerns effect claims.
REFINEMENT_CORRECTNESS.LIMITS: A statistically supported task effect does not prove semantic preservation of arbitrary requirements transformations.

REALIZABILITY.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Implementation feasibility as a downstream quality outcome.
REALIZABILITY.SUPPORT: S027 measures domain-model properties; S019 measures template-related factors; S029 explicitly limits assessment to intrinsic wording and excludes feasibility.
REALIZABILITY.LIMITS: These observations do not establish realizability of the underlying requirements. Feasibility could be a relevant activity/outcome in another study but was not established here.

TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.SUPPORT: S027 defines manipulated features, domain-model outcomes and context variables, enabling a bounded empirical claim; S031 measures selected story defects.
TRACEABILITY_ACCURACY.LIMITS: This is a quality-evaluation chain, not evidence of accurate lifecycle traces. Measurement validity, gold judgments and omitted interactions remain limits.

ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Whether the chosen quality measure answers the consumer activity.
ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.SUPPORT: S027 links linguistic features to a declared domain-modeling outcome; S019/S029 show how wording criteria can be measured while contextual validity remains outside the evaluation.
ACCEPTANCE_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: This supports matching criterion to outcome, not a validated acceptance algorithm or a claim that intrinsic conformity alone establishes need fulfillment.

EMPIRICAL_PROCESS_EFFECTIVENESS.WHAT_WAS_EXAMINED: Task-specific wording effects, separated from tool/phrasing scores.
